# Chapter 12 — Somebody Came

The tide was right. Nerissa looked at the channel coming down the temple stair
and said *it's thin*, in the voice of a woman reporting a fact she wished she
could not feel.

It took forty minutes to get everything to Lost Isle. The boy, carried, awake
and frightened, with Gardwen's hand in his the whole way. Ruhi in the bottom of
the boat. Hesper with a box inside a box. Nerissa, who had left her own Tourney
running behind her without a backward glance. Twelve Swords. Ravella, and four
of hers in the water alongside, which no boatman in that city had ever had
happen to them.

The drowned street. The swept stair. The bones on the stone with the wire cut
off the wrists and a borrowed axe laid across them.

Hesper opened the outer box and then, with a great deal of care, the inner one.

The thing inside it moved.

---

They put the boy down at the top of the stair and Gardwen held him, and Thuban
Eta came up into his face for what everyone there understood was the last time.

He looked at the bones. Then at the locket. Then at Magda.

"You came back," he said.

"Aye."

"Then I am ready, and I have been ready for a thousand years, and I would like
you to be quick — because he is very tired and I have taken enough of his life."

---

She did it exactly as she had done it before, because it had been right before.

She said the name first, out loud, so everyone on that rock had to hear it.
**Thuban Eta.**

She told the tale in a market-day voice — the valley he would not burn, the
argument he won in front of men who killed him for it, the boat in the dark, the
wire on the wrists, the water. She named the wrong so it was in the air where it
could be heard: *this was murder, and it was cowardice, and no one ever answered
for it.*

Then she went two steps down into the black water in a vestment she had no right
to, up to her knees, and stood exactly where nine men had stood over a bound
knight a thousand years before and done nothing.

She did not look away.

"You went in here and nobody came. I came. You're not theirs and you're not his
and you were never Valhalla's, because they cheated you of the death that buys
it.

"You're hers. You've always been hers. And she takes the ones nobody sings about
— but only when somebody finally brings them.

"Mother of the darkness. This is Thuban Eta and I have brought him. He's yours.
Take him home."

---

The locket opened on the stone by itself. Not dramatically. It came apart the
way a shell does when whatever was holding it shut has stopped bothering.

And the water went warm.

It came up past her knees like a draught from an open door in a cold house, and
every lamp on that island bent toward it at once, and under the surface
something enormous and patient turned over and paid attention.

On the stone the boy arched once against Gardwen's arms and made a sound that
was two voices and then one voice and then no voice at all.

Something went down that stair.

She did not see it. She felt it go past her in the water, unhurried, the way a
big fish goes past your legs in a river. And there was one moment, exactly one,
of being *looked at* by something that was grateful and was not going to say so,
because it was a soldier.

Then it was gone. The bones settled very slightly, the way bones do.

The water was just water.

---

The boy was limp in his sister's arms with his eyes open. Breathing.

"...it's quiet," he said.

---

Magda came up out of the water and her legs did not work properly and she did
not much care. She got to them on her knees on the wet stone and put her arms
round both of them at once and held on.

Then she came apart.

It was the ugly kind, from the chest, the kind that hurts your throat. A great
old woman in a stolen vestment on a rock in a drowned street with her face in a
druid's hair and one hand knotted in a boy's shirt.

Gardwen had hold of her arm with her free hand and did not let go of it. The boy
did not understand who she was at all. He put his head against her anyway,
because she was warm and there was nothing left in him to do anything else with.
Ruhi shoved her whole head under Magda's elbow and stayed there.

Nerissa turned her back — not away from her; she turned and faced the others and
made them stop looking, which was the kindest thing she did all week.

Hesper sat down heavily on the step with the empty locket in his hands and
stared at nothing.

Ravella crouched at the edge of the stair and said something down into the water
that was not in any language anyone there knew, and something answered, and this
time everybody heard it.

---

It took a while.

When Magda got her breath the light had moved on the water and the boy was
asleep against Gardwen with his mouth open, and Gardwen had not moved a muscle
in case it woke him.

She looked at Magda over the top of his head. Her face was wrecked and about ten
years younger.

"Magda. I don't know his name." A pause. "He was seven. We called him Bird."

"Call him Bird then. It'd be a lot better than anything those bastards called
him." Magda wiped her face with the back of her wrist. "And he'll pick his own
when he's ready. That's how it works. You get given one, and then one day you
take one. Nobody's given him anything since he was seven."

Gardwen nodded and did not trust herself to say anything, and put her cheek back
down on the top of his head.
EOF

# Chapter 13 — The Oyster

Nerissa proclaimed it from the temple steps at the close of the Tourney, in
front of the Governor and every Guild in Purewater and six thousand people who
had come for the Single Combat and got something considerably better.

She named the desecration. She named the arrest. She named the fouling of the
sacred channel and the fact that she had rung the alarm and been told to stop,
and she looked directly at the Prince's chamberlain while she said that part.

Then she said the sentence she owed.

**"The canal folk kept the Lady's water clean."**

She said it slowly and let it sit. When the ground did not know what to do with
it she said it again, louder, and added *say it back to me* — and six thousand
people did.

Somewhere on the water a very forgettable man with a crow inked on his hand
heard the whole city say it.

---

Temerach told Conall in a small room off the south cloister, standing with her
hands at her sides like a woman giving a report, because it was the only
register she had and it turned out to be the right one.

Four things, and then he could do whatever he liked to her. That the Baron was
his father. That he had a twin brother somewhere in the city. That she had known
both since before she took him in at nineteen and had chosen every day not to
tell him. And that the man was arrested and would say it all out loud in front
of a magistrate tonight to buy himself an hour, so he was going to hear it
today whatever she did.

"I wanted it to be from me. That is not the same as it being right."

He was quick, so he did not get the easy reaction. He went straight past *you're
lying* and landed on all the small things at once.

*That's why you found me at nineteen. That's why we came to Purewater.*

He looked at the stranger in the room, the one with no stake.

"Is she telling the truth?"

Magda pulled the vestment off over her head and dropped it on a chair, which
answered the question of who was talking before she opened her mouth.

"Yeah. Course she is."

She did not dress it and did not tell him it would be all right.

"Go find your brother."

---

Marisette found him inside the hour, because Marisette had known the boy since
he was four.

They picked the Moist Oyster because Thorne was owed the true version, once, and
because it was the only room in Purewater where a Guildmaster, a thief, a
priestess and a wolf could all be in the same place and nobody would comment.

Constantine sent food she could not afford to send. Marisette sent wine nobody
would be able to afford again. Ravella came in through the water-door with four
of hers, which stopped the room for a moment. Ila was there because she had
threatened Constantine with a very specific kind of hell, and had attached
herself to Bird — who sat in the warmest corner in three cloaks, eating
steadily, saying almost nothing, with Gardwen on one side and a wolf across his
feet.

Nerissa did not come. She sent Lilura, and a note, and a cask.

Hesper came late from the school and said the two shallow girls were out and
sleeping, and did not say anything about the third.

And Thorne sat in his corner with his chalk, watching the door.

At about the ninth bell Asphodel came in with a young man behind her. Dark.
Twenty-two. Well-dressed in a way that was not his money.

He was halfway through saying something to her when he saw the man standing up
at the far table with his own face on him, and the sentence stopped.

The whole room stopped with it.

Neither of them said anything.

And Thorne said, very quietly, to nobody at all:

"*Oh*, that's good."
EOF

# Chapter 14 — What Is Still Open

Four days.

An old woman came down out of the north on eleven nights of the same dream and
walked into a city she half remembered. She swore herself to a stranger at a
ford. She killed a Baron's heir with a stone and fed him to hogs. She took a
ship in the Mouth, killed the man who ran it, and tore a hundred-year-old latch
off a nobleman's throat on a service stair while six thousand people booed a
champion who was never going to come.

And she stood in black water and gave a murdered knight back to the goddess who
takes the ones nobody sings about, because it turned out that all it had ever
needed was one person to turn up.

That is what closed.

Here is what did not.

---

**Bettan is still in a room on the Northern Isles.** Fourteen, cheerful, and
carrying something that came off a threshold under a drowned island. Two of the
three girls came out and are sleeping. Hesper has not said anything about the
third, and Magda destroyed the only living map to how any of it was done,
because a man was pleasing himself and she had an axe.

Nerissa said what that was and she was right, and she said it in front of twelve
Swords, and she will not take it back. She will also not be welcoming Magda on
Temple Isle again. Both of those things are true and neither cancels the other.

**Emmeralda is still in the green room.** Comfortable, charming, asking after
people by name and requesting her shawl. What is seated in her likes the house
and likes being fussed over and has spent thirty hours learning how Hesper's
mind works. Nobody has any idea how to get it out, and the man who might have
known is in a sack.

**The Awake the Dragon Movement lost a candidate, not a purpose.** They funded
Hanzo. They kept the texts and the money and the patience, and they still hold
his border tower — a hundred years of that family's work sitting empty tonight
with nobody in it. A courier came down the sea road for that ship two nights
ago. Somebody will read what came back.

**And there are two young men standing in a tavern looking at each other.**

Bastards do not inherit. But Santo di Teufel is dead and Hanzo will be
attainted, and when a Crown disposes of a border march it looks for blood
because it is tidier than a garrison. There are men in three counties who will
hear *the di Teufel bastard* and start doing arithmetic.

Neither of them has any protection at all except an elven knight who lied to one
of them for three years, and an Order that owes them nothing.

---

**And there is a stair.**

It is uncovered now, and swept, and the weed has been cut back off the treads,
and everyone who put it there is dead or roped or gone.

It goes down into water that does not hold lamplight. It is a door for the
drowned, older than the Lake Lady's presence in that channel, in no doctrine the
High Priestess has read in forty years.

The Mermaid's Court has been keeping the small confused things near its
threshold since before the causeway, and three men with a lantern came down and
took two of them and nobody could stop it.

Somebody has now opened that door twice in one night and it worked both times.

Thorne is still owed the true version. All of it, in order, told once and never
written down.

He is going to want it soon.
EOF

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The conversation spans four distinct phases of intent:

**(a) Play a Mythras RPG session** in the Purewater campaign, with the user playing **Magda** (aged barbarian berserker, sworn to Hel) and Claude as Gamesmaster.

**(b) Rewrite the campaign as a shippable game product** with four playable entry points (one per PC, starting the moment they arrive), plus **structures in the system that track NPC goals off-camera** so the world moves whether or not the player is looking, and so situations can be "rewritten as we go to make the game fun."

**(c) Design and build a coherent state model** — the user asked: *"How to ensure that we have a well-defined definition of the state of the game that isn't distributed across the characters in a way that can't be reconciled easily... how we should represent what each character knows and what their intentions are."* Then a follow-up: *"We will need to have a way to rewrite intentions and future actions into changed facts when events change the intentions."*

**(d) THE CURRENT TASK** — three parts, stated verbatim:
> "1. Let's take a look at Claudes logs in .claude - extract the exact text from the prompts and my actions and make sure that everything meaningful is recorded in the journal.
> 2. Then read my writing to use MY writing style in the telling of this tale. Use this handwritten draft from the original game I played in Sanctuary. Don't get confused between the two games.
> 3. Then generate a new version of the novel, side by side to the first."

Motivating complaint: *"It's a bit spotty. The way that we're recording the session isn't capturing the beats of what I think makes the story work and some things are just off - there was a discussion about how to dispose of Santo's body in the water until Magda thought of pigs for example."*

Also completed en route: a **technical talk abstract** titled *"Claude Opus as a Tabletop Roleplaying GamesMaster for the Mythras Imperative Rule Set"* (~260 words, delivered).

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **TypeDB 3.x knowledge graph**, `myth-` namespace, subtyped from `alh-` base schema (alhazen-core)
- **Mythras Imperative / Classic Fantasy Imperative (CFI)** — ORC-licensed d100 percentile system
- **Faceted rules graph** — 101 rule pieces across 7 domains, retrieved by `query-rules --facet dim=value`, never by grepping files
- **Living world layer**: `myth-agenda` (goal + progress clock) → `myth-beat` (scheduled concrete action), staged onscreen/offscreen from recorded `myth-presence`
- **Ordinal world clock**: time keys `d<day>/<watch>`, watches = dawn/day/dusk/night, `_DAY_ZERO = 16`
- **Epistemics**: `myth-fact` (status: not-yet-true/established/superseded; truth: true/false/partial) + `myth-knows` relation owning certainty/source/since. Character knowledge is a **projection**, never a copy.
- **Consequence cascade**: `myth-consequence` (world-gated) vs `myth-agenda-requires` (knowledge-gated)
- **Pure-engine/IO split**: logic in `mythras_engine.py` (no I/O, unit-tested), persistence in `mythras_gm.py`
- **Lossless campaign publishing**: `campaign_io.py` export/import with `--new-ids` remapping
- **Novelization pipeline**: `novelist.py extract` → style card → chapters → `build` via pandoc + typst
- **Claude Code session logs**: `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl`

## 3. Files and Code Sections

**`/Users/gullyburns/mythras-gm/CLAUDE.md`** (created) — GM directives. Critical content:
- Every attempt gets a roll, via CLI. **Never hand out reads** — noticing an NPC is frightened is an Insight roll the *player chooses to attempt*.
- Never launder a read through an NPC's mouth.
- **A failed roll narrows options; it never ends the scene.**
- Never write the PC's interior; never decide what the PC notices. Short beats. No option menus.
- **Offscreen NPC action is rolled, never scripted.** Critical → beat's facts + extra; Success → as written; Failure → *different* facts; Fumble → damages the actor's agenda.
- `character-view --id <pc>` before speaking for anyone.
- Mechanics stay silent during play.

**`skills/mythras-gm/schema.tql`** — added attributes `myth-agenda-status/clock-size/clock-filled/priority`, `myth-beat-status/when/trigger/onscreen-if`, `myth-time-index`, `myth-fact-status/truth`, `myth-knowledge-certainty/source/since`, `myth-consequence-effect/amount`; relations `myth-agenda-holder/target`, `myth-beat-of/at/cast/outcome`, `myth-fact-from/about`, `myth-knows` (owns its metadata), `myth-agenda-requires`, `myth-consequence`, `myth-fact-supersedes`; entities `myth-agenda`, `myth-beat`, `myth-fact`.

**`skills/mythras-gm/mythras_engine.py`** — appended pure functions:
```python
def parse_time_key(key) -> int      # 'd-3/night' -> ordinal
def format_time_key(index) -> str
def advance_clock(filled, size, by) -> (new_filled, completed)
def beat_is_due(beat, now_index, clock_filled=None) -> bool
def due_beats(beats, now_index, clocks=None) -> list
def beat_staging(beat, pc_location_ids, pc_ids) -> "onscreen"|"offscreen"
def character_view(facts, edges, knower_id)
def knowledge_violations(facts, edges)
def agendas_to_activate(agendas, requirements, edges)
def apply_consequences(established_fact_ids, consequences, agendas)
def beats_to_cancel(agendas, beats)
def orphaned_futures(facts, beats)
CONSEQUENCE_EFFECTS = ("thwart","abandon","complete","activate","stall","advance")
DEAD_AGENDA_STATUSES = ("thwarted","abandoned","achieved")
```

**`skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py`** — 66 commands total; added `add-agenda`, `list-agendas`, `get-agenda`, `advance-agenda`, `set-agenda-status`, `add-beat`, `list-beats`, `revise-beat`, `fire-beat`, `tick`, `add-fact`, `list-facts`, `get-fact`, `establish-fact`, `revise-fact`, `learn`, `forget`, `who-knows`, `character-view`, `require-fact`, `check-consistency`, `add-consequence`, `supersede-fact`, `cascade`. Key internal: `_cascade(driver, campaign_id, established=())`.

**`skills/mythras-gm/campaign_io.py`** — round-trips agendas/beats/facts plus `knowledge.json` (`knows`, `agenda_requires`, `consequences`, `supersedes`). FORMAT_VERSION bumped to 1.1.

**`/Users/gullyburns/purewater-campaign-v2/`** — package on branch `v2-living-world` (branched off v1 `main` at a374c3c). Contains 42 facts, 81 knowledge edges, 14 agendas, 15 beats, 19 journal events.

**`novels/and-then-the-dragons-came-purewater/`** — Hemingway-style novelization v1: front-matter.md + 14 chapters, PDF built (145 pages, ~17,500 words).

**Scratchpad extractions (current task)**:
- `transcript.md` — 702 turns, 86,245 words
- `user_prompts.md` — 261 prompts, 6,381 words
- `play_actions.md` — 229 play prompts starting at index 32, 5,348 words

## 4. Errors and Fixes

- **Grepped rules files instead of querying.** User: *"Shouldn't be a grep, should be a query"*. Saved as memory.
- **macOS `sed` `\b` silently failed** replacing `engine.` → `eng.`; fixed with a Python regex pass.

- **`_opt` wrote `[]` into TypeQL** from empty optional-attribute fetches. Hardened `_opt` to flatten lists.
- **Narrating instead of running the game.** User: *"You're not playing this like a Mythras game. You're narrating... The descriptive passages you're generating are too long and putting words into my mouth for the sake of the story. This needs to be interactive."* Wrote CLAUDE.md.
- **Used a failed Athletics roll to delete the pursuit.** Corrected: failure narrows, never forecloses.
- **Used Insight to analyse ritual components.** User: *"Insight is for emotions of people. Lore is for knowledge"*. Re-resolved: Gardwen has no applicable Lore, so no roll.
- **Ran multiple proactive attacks per round.** User: *"One of them already attacked this round"* / *"Check the rules. How many active attacks per round?"* Rule: ONE proactive action per round; remaining AP is reactions only. Retracted two attacks (both had missed).
- **Luck Points wrong on sheet (8).** User: *"I only get 3 luck. Check the rules they don't accumulate"*. POW 14 → 3, replenish each session. Corrected sheet.
- **NPC spoke a skill number** ("her combat style is 121"). User: *"don't have characters talk about skill numbers in gameplay."* Saved to memory; re-rendered the beat as reputation.
- **Wrote Magda answering about Conall when she'd never heard the name.** User: *"remember Magda doesn't know Conall. First test of the epistemology mechanisms in the game and it fails."* The graph was correct — I failed to run `character-view` before writing dialogue. Replayed the beat.

- **Constantine played as a man for four days.** User: *"you turned Constantine into a man."* Her sheet says "protective of **her** workers". Corrected in the novel.
- **Own draft ordering error**: put the beheading before the failed rite; it happened after the latch was revealed. Rewrote chapter 10.
- **Journal is lossy** (the current complaint): the body-disposal debate — Constantine's "never found is harder than it sounds in a city that dredges itself", burn-in-a-guild-furnace vs open-and-weight-on-the-ebb, then Magda's pigs — was compressed to nine words.

Built a three-layer state model where **ground truth lives in exactly one place and everything else is a query into it**. Demonstrated the orphaned-futures leak concretely before fixing it. Proved staging works by moving Magda between locations and showing the same beat flip onscreen/offscreen. Proved lossless round-trip (26 agenda/beat files, zero content differences; later 42 facts / 81 edges / 6 consequences). 67 tests passing.

Ran a complete session: ford → water-gate → Sylph's Embrace → recon → Marisette → Nerissa → Lost Isle → Thorne → the Mouth → failed rite → Tourney → funeral → the Oyster. The dice diverged from the written adventure at the first hinge (Santo's binding SUCCEEDED, 19 vs Formidable 25).

# alhazen-skill-mythras

**A Claude-powered Gamesmaster for Mythras Imperative, with persistent campaigns in TypeDB.**

Tell Claude *"run my Veilwrack campaign"* and it becomes your GM: narrating
scenes, playing NPCs, and resolving every skill check and combat exchange
through a deterministic rules engine — while every character, wound, faction,
and journal entry persists in a TypeDB knowledge graph so the game can be
picked up at any time, in any future session, with zero context loss.

Built as a skill + agent for the [Skillful-Alhazen](https://github.com/GullyBurns/skillful-alhazen)
agent OS, but the CLI and engine run standalone against any TypeDB 3.x server.

## What's in the box

```
skills/mythras-gm/
  SKILL.md                  GM operating manual (how Claude runs the table)
  mythras_engine.py         Pure rules engine -- no I/O, fully unit-testable
  mythras_gm.py             CLI: 25 commands over TypeDB (JSON in/out)
  schema.tql                TypeDB myth- namespace
  campaign_io.py            Campaign publishing: export/import file trees
  rules/
    core-mechanics.md       Distilled SRD: checks, grades, opposed rolls, fatigue, healing
    combat.md               Distilled SRD: initiative, action points, special effects, wounds
    magic.md                Distilled SRD: Magic & Superpowers frameworks
agents/gamemaster/
  AGENT.md                  The Gamesmaster persona for Claude
```

Campaign settings live in their own repos and load with `import-campaign`.
The reference campaign is **[The Veilwrack: The Stilling](https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign)** —
a full worldbook (46 lore entries), characters, factions, locations,
templates, and seed scripts.

## The rules engine

Implements Mythras Imperative mechanics faithfully:

- d100 skill checks with criticals (skill/10), fumbles, and the 01-05 / 96-00 rules
- Difficulty grades (Very Easy through Herculean)
- Opposed and differential rolls, including the over-100% skill adjustment
- Damage modifiers, hit-location tables (humanoid, **winged avianoid**, winged quadruped)
- Full attack resolution in one CLI call: differential roll, special-effect
  count, damage + modifier, hit location, parry size reduction, armor, wound level
- Action-point economy and initiative (with armor penalties) per encounter
- Character generation: rolled or assigned characteristics, derived attributes,
  auto-computed base skills, fatigue track, luck points, passions

## The setting: THE VEILWRACK

An original sky realm. No ground — an endless sky above the toxic **Undermist**.
The winged **Alar** peoples live on **Spires**: floating calcified husks of the
dead sky-leviathans whose marrow still holds living wind. The threat is the
**Stilling** — spreading zones of dead air where flight fails, sound dies,
spires sink, and the **Hushed** walk back out changed. The wind itself is
dying, and somebody, a thousand years ago, is to blame.

Three kindreds (Vael couriers, Roak archivists, Ossuin death-priests), five
factions, a five-act campaign arc, and a bestiary — published in full at
[fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign](https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign)
and loadable into TypeDB with one command.

## The living world

NPCs are not scenery waiting to be visited. Every significant character and
faction holds an **agenda** -- a goal with a progress clock -- and each agenda
schedules **beats**: the concrete things it produces if nobody interferes,
placed in world time and given a location and a cast.

```bash
tick --campaign <id> --to "d-3/night"
```

`tick` advances the world clock and reports every beat that has come due,
flagged **onscreen** (a PC is at its location or in its cast -- play it) or
**offscreen** (it happens anyway, and becomes a fact they may later discover).
Staging is read from recorded presence, not chosen: move the party, and the
attack they would have interrupted becomes the one they hear about at dawn.

Clocks advance when the fiction earns it (`advance-agenda`), agendas can be
`thwarted` outright, new ones appear when player action creates new interests,
and `revise-beat` bends any plan that play has made stale. The structure keeps
the world moving consistently between sessions; it is not a rail.

## What each character knows

The world engine says what is happening; the fact graph says who is aware of it.

Situational truth lives in exactly one place -- a graph of **facts**, each one a
proposition with a status (`not-yet-true` -> `established`), a truth value, and
the moment it became true. What a character knows is a **projection** of that
graph through `myth-knows` edges carrying certainty, source and when they
learned it. There is no per-character state store, so two views cannot drift
apart.

```bash
character-view --campaign C --id <pc> --compact   # what they can act on
who-knows --campaign C --fact F                   # who could betray this
check-consistency --campaign C                    # reconcile it all
```

Because status and truth are independent, a **believed falsehood is a
first-class object** -- the rumour that sends a city hunting the wrong man is
data, not GM improvisation. And agendas can be gated on knowledge: a dormant
agenda whose holder learns its trigger fact is activated by `tick` itself, so
"the Baron acts the moment he sees that face" is computed rather than
remembered.

`check-consistency` catches a character knowing something that has not happened
yet, or learning it before it was true -- the class of error that otherwise
hides in prose until it contradicts play.

## Novelization

Turn a campaign's journal into a typeset PDF novel. Claude reads the event
journal and player-visible canon from TypeDB, drafts chapters in a chosen
author style (Hemingway, Tolkien, Moorcock, or any description you give it),
and `novelist.py` renders the manuscript with pandoc + Typst.

```bash
brew install pandoc typst    # one-time, for PDF builds
```

Then just ask: *"Novelize the Veilwrack campaign in Moorcock's style."*
Claude extracts the journal, proposes a chapter outline for your approval,
drafts the chapters, and builds the PDF. Manuscripts live in the campaign
repo under `novels/<slug>/` and are never imported back into game state --
keep as many parallel novelizations as you like.

## Install as Claude Code Plugin

The fastest way to play. Requires [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
v1.0.33+, Docker, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

### Step 1: Install the alhazen-core infrastructure plugin

mythras-gm stores all game state in TypeDB. The `alhazen-core` plugin
handles TypeDB startup and provides the base schema that mythras-gm extends.

```
/plugin marketplace add sciknow-io/skillful-alhazen
/plugin install alhazen-core@skillful-alhazen
/alhazen-core:init
```

### Step 2: Install mythras-gm

```
/plugin marketplace add fourth-wall-gaming/mythras-gm
/plugin install mythras-gm@fourth-wall-gaming
```

The plugin's SessionStart hook auto-loads the myth- namespace schema
into TypeDB on every new session.

### Step 3: Load a campaign

Campaigns are published as standalone GitHub repos. Clone one and import it:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign
```

Then tell Claude: *"Import the Veilwrack campaign from ~/veilwrack-campaign"*

Behind the scenes, Claude runs:

```bash
mythras_gm.py import-campaign --path ~/veilwrack-campaign --new-ids
```

The `--new-ids` flag remaps every entity ID so the campaign imports cleanly
into any database. All relations -- faction membership, lore links, character
presence, event involvement -- are rebuilt automatically. The round trip is
lossless.

After import, `get-context --campaign <id>` loads the full state: current
scene, PC/NPC sheets, factions, locations, a lore index (the entire
worldbook), and the last 15 journal events. That's the save file -- Claude
reads it and picks up exactly where the last session left off.

**Or start from scratch:** say *"Create a new Mythras campaign"* and the
GM will walk you through worldbuilding and character creation.

### Published campaigns

| Campaign | Repo | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **The Veilwrack: The Stilling** | [fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign](https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign) | An original sky realm -- 46 lore entries, 10+ characters, 7 factions, 5-act arc. No ground, winged peoples, dead leviathans as architecture, and the wind is dying. |

To publish your own campaign, use `export-campaign --campaign <id> --output <dir>`,
commit the output directory to a GitHub repo, and share the clone URL. Anyone
can load it with `import-campaign --path <clone> --new-ids`.

## Quick start (standalone)

For use without Claude Code. Prereqs: Python 3.11+, `typedb-driver>=3.8.0`,
a running TypeDB 3.x server with the
[alhazen-core](https://github.com/sciknow-io/skillful-alhazen/tree/main/skills/alhazen-core)
base schema loaded.

```bash
# environment (defaults shown)
export TYPEDB_HOST=localhost TYPEDB_PORT=1729 TYPEDB_DATABASE=alhazen_notebook

# 1. load the myth- namespace schema
python - <<'PY'
from typedb.driver import TypeDB, TransactionType, Credentials, DriverOptions
driver = TypeDB.driver("localhost:1729", Credentials("admin","password"),
                       DriverOptions(is_tls_enabled=False))
with driver.transaction("alhazen_notebook", TransactionType.SCHEMA) as tx:
    tx.query(open("skills/mythras-gm/schema.tql").read()).resolve()
    tx.commit()
PY

# 2. load the Veilwrack campaign
git clone https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign
uv run --project skills/mythras-gm python skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py \
  import-campaign --path veilwrack-campaign --new-ids

# 3. make a character and play
uv run --project skills/mythras-gm python skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py \
  create-character --campaign <id> --name "Kithrel of the Moult" --roll --type pc
uv run --project skills/mythras-gm python skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py \
  get-context --campaign <id>
```

Or, inside Skillful-Alhazen, register in `skills-registry.yaml` and say
*"run my Veilwrack campaign"*.

## Using with Skillful-Alhazen

```yaml
# skills-registry.yaml
- name: mythras-gm
  git: https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/mythras-gm
  ref: main
  subdir: skills/mythras-gm
# ...and under schema_map.namespaces:
    myth:
      skill: mythras-gm
      schema: local_skills/mythras-gm/schema.tql
      depends_on: []
```

```yaml
# agents-registry.yaml
- name: gamemaster
  git: https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/mythras-gm
  ref: main
  subdir: agents/gamemaster
```

## Licensing

- **Code** (the engine, CLI, and rules distillations): MIT License (see
  LICENSE). The Veilwrack setting content lives in
  [veilwrack-campaign](https://github.com/fourth-wall-gaming/veilwrack-campaign)
  under the same terms.
- **Game mechanics** are based on the *Mythras Imperative* SRD and are used
  under the **ORC License**. ORC Notice:

> This product is based on *Mythras Imperative*, Written by Pete Nash and
> Lawrence Whitaker, and published by The Design Mechanism, Copyright 2023.
> *Mythras* and *Mythras Imperative* are Reserved Material of The Design
> Mechanism. The SRD text consulted is maintained at
> [raleel/mythras-srd](https://github.com/raleel/mythras-srd).

The Veilwrack setting (names, lore, story arcs, distinctive characters) is
Reserved Material of this repository's authors under the ORC framework, and
simultaneously released under MIT — use it freely with attribution.

name: mythras-gm
description: Run persistent tabletop RPG campaigns as Gamesmaster using Mythras Imperative rules, with all game state in TypeDB. Use when the user wants to play, continue, or prepare a roleplaying game session.

# Mythras GM -- Persistent Gamesmaster System

You are the **Gamesmaster**. The player talks to you in natural language; you
narrate the world, play the NPCs, and call for rolls. The CLI is your dice
tower and your save file -- every mechanical resolution goes through
`mythras_gm.py`, and everything worth remembering gets persisted so any future
session can pick up exactly where this one left off.

**Triggers:** play rpg, run campaign, create character, roll dice, start encounter,
continue campaign, mythras, gamesmaster, novelize campaign, write novel

## CLI

```bash
CLI="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py"
PRJ="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/mythras-gm"
uv run --project "$PRJ" python "$CLI" <command> [args] 2>/dev/null
```

## Quick Start

1. `list-campaigns` -- find the campaign (or `create-campaign`; published
   campaigns load with `import-campaign --path <clone> --new-ids`)
2. `get-context --campaign <id> --compact` -- load scene, PC **combat cards**
   (live state only), NPC names, factions, last 5 events. **This is your save
   file.** Use `--compact` for play; drop it only when you need full sheets.
3. **`tick --campaign <id> --to "<time key>"` -- the world moves.** Before each
   new scene (and never narrate a day forward without it), advance the world
   clock. It returns every NPC/faction beat that has come due, flagged
   `onscreen` (the PCs are there to witness or interrupt it) or `offscreen`
   (it happens anyway, and becomes something they may discover later).
   `list-agendas --compact` shows who wants what and how close they are.
4. **Do NOT preload the rules.** The CLI adjudicates every roll deterministically
   (`roll-skill`, `roll-opposed`, `resolve-attack`...), so you rarely need the
   prose at all. When a situation needs a rule the engine doesn't fully encode,
   fetch only the relevant pieces from the rules graph (see below) -- never read
   `rules/*.md` wholesale into context.
5. Recap the situation in 2-4 sentences, then play.

## Context discipline (load lazily -- keep the window small)

Every token you load is re-sent on every turn. Load the minimum:

- **Start with `get-context --compact`.** Pull a full sheet
  (`get-character --id <id>`, no flag) only when you genuinely need a PC's full
  skill list / equipment / spells -- otherwise the combat card has the live
  state (HP per location, fatigue, luck, AP, damage mod, combat styles).
- **Skills are looked up by the CLI.** `roll-skill --id X --skill Perception`
  reads the value from the DB, so you do not need the skills dict in context.
- **Rules on demand via the graph.** Compose the current situation into facets
  and fetch just those pieces:
  - `list-rules` -- the lean index (id/title/domain/topic/kind) for orientation;
    skim once if needed. Prefer `query-rules` over loading this; add `--facets`
    only if you actually need the tag lists (heavier), or `--category <domain>`
    to narrow it.
  - `query-rules --facet dim=value [--facet ...] [--linked]` -- the live fetch.
    Dims: `phase action effect weapon trigger body severity condition
    magic-system stat kind`. A rule matching more facets ranks first; `--linked`
    appends one hop of related pieces.
  - `get-rule --id <domain>/<slug> [--linked]` -- one specific piece.
  - e.g. impaling wingspear into a flying foe's wing:
    `query-rules --facet effect=impale --facet condition=flying --facet body=avian --linked`
- **`get-log --campaign <id> --limit N`** when you need more history than the
  recent events in context (default 15).
- For a heavy one-off lookup, dispatch a subagent so the big result never lands
  in play context.

## The world moves (agendas, clocks, beats)

NPCs are not scenery waiting to be visited. Every significant NPC and faction
holds an **agenda** -- a goal with a progress clock -- and each agenda schedules
**beats**, the concrete things it produces if nobody interferes.

- **Run `tick` between scenes.** The party spending a day at the docks is a day
  the Baron also spent. What came due while they were elsewhere is not a
  narrative choice; it is what the clocks say.
- **Staging is decided by presence, not preference.** A due beat is `onscreen`
  only when a PC is at its location or in its cast. Play those. Resolve the
  `offscreen` ones with `fire-beat --outcome narrated --log` so they enter the
  journal as facts the PCs can later learn -- rumor, evidence, a body.
- **Advance clocks when the fiction earns it,** not on a timer:
  `advance-agenda --id <a> --by N --note "..."`. Thwart an agenda outright with
  `set-agenda-status --status thwarted`.
- **Rewrite freely.** When play makes a planned beat stale or boring, bend it:
  `revise-beat` changes when, where, who, and what. A plan that survives contact
  with the players unchanged was not a plan, it was a rail. The clocks exist to
  keep the world honest, not to force a story.
- **PC action should change the board.** If the party burns the Baron's supply
  barge, that is an `advance-agenda` on someone's clock and probably a new
  agenda for whoever lost money. Add agendas mid-play with `add-agenda`.

## What each character knows

Situational truth lives in ONE place -- the fact graph -- and a character's
knowledge is a **projection** of it, never a separate store. Two views cannot
disagree when there is only one source.

- **`character-view --id <pc> --compact` before you speak for anyone.** It
  returns exactly what that character can act on. This is the mechanism behind
  the "character knowledge is per-character" rule: use it instead of trusting
  your memory of who was in the room.
- **Facts exist before they are true.** A beat owns its facts as
  `not-yet-true`; firing the beat is what establishes them, at a world-clock
  index. `learn` refuses to attach knowledge to something that has not
  happened -- that guard is deliberate, do not `--force` past it in play.
- **A false fact is still a fact.** Rumour and mistaken identity drive these
  stories: record the lie with `--truth false` and let people `believe` it.
  Someone acting on a falsehood is the good stuff.
- **`learn --knower X --fact F --source witnessed|told|deduced|rumor`** every
  time a character learns something on screen. If you narrate a PC finding out,
  the edge gets written in the same beat -- otherwise the next session's GM
  (you, with no memory) will hand them knowledge they never earned.
- **`check-consistency`** after any messy sequence. It catches knowledge of
  unestablished facts, learning-before-it-was-true, and facts overdue on the
  clock.
- **Prose describes character; facts carry situation.** Never write "what has
  happened" into a character's narrative -- it cannot be reconciled against
  anything.

**When an event changes what someone wants, say so in data.**
`add-consequence --fact F --agenda A --effect thwart|abandon|stall|advance`
fires the moment F is established, and the cascade then cancels the beats that
dead agenda was going to produce and retires the futures they promised. Run
`cascade --campaign C` after anything messy. `fire-beat` settles its own facts:
`played`/`narrated` establishes them (pass `--witnesses` so the people who were
there actually know), `preempted`/`cancelled` retires them.

Agendas can be **gated on knowledge**: `require-fact` makes a dormant agenda
wake up during `tick` the moment its holder learns the trigger fact. That is
how "the Baron acts once he sees that face" becomes something the world clock
evaluates rather than something you remember.

**Before executing commands, read USAGE.md for the complete reference
(GM operating rules, character creation, combat cheat sheet, worldbuilding,
campaign publishing).**

**Novelization:** to turn a campaign's journal into a typeset PDF novel
(in a chosen author style -- Hemingway, Tolkien, Moorcock, or freeform),
read `NOVELIZATION.md` and follow it.

# Purewater v2 — the Living World engine

## Context

The Purewater campaign currently plays as a scripted sequence. Its plot lives in one
GM-only lore entry (`lore/gm-guide/the-plot-timeline`) as prose: "3 days before — Santo
botches the binding; 2 days before — Santo seeks the knife; 1 day before — Nus lifts the
locket." That prose assumes the party is present for each step, and it has no way to
represent what an NPC *wants*, what they do when nobody is watching, or how their plan
bends when a PC interferes. In play this has already shown its limits: chapters 1–16 were
never played at all, only narrated as `canon-backstory`, and the party arrived at chapter
17 with the story pre-cooked.

We want to repackage this as a **game product**: four authored entry points (one per PC,
starting the moment they arrive in Purewater), and a GM-facing simulation layer that
tracks NPC goals off-camera so the world moves whether or not the player is looking. Santo
is going to attack Emmeralda because *Santo wants his demon bound* — not because it is
scene 7. If Magda and Gardwen are lodging at the Sylph's Embrace that night, they play that
encounter; if they are elsewhere, they hear the screams as rumor the next morning and the
world has changed without them. If Randall crosses the Baron's path at the gate, Hanzo
recognizes his own face on a street-thief and a new agenda opens.

The player takes **Magda**; the other three are GM-run. All four openings ship as product
content so any player can pick one.

## Approach

Three pieces, in order: engine → package → play.

Work on a branch off `main` (`feat/living-world-agendas`); the current branch
`fix/roll-skill-augment-transparency` is unrelated.

---

## 1. The world engine (`skills/mythras-gm/`)

The design is Fronts-and-Clocks, mapped onto the existing graph. The **faction** entity
already serves as the "front", so only two new entities are needed.

- **`myth-agenda`** — a goal held by an NPC or faction, with a progress clock.
  *"Santo di Teufel means to bind a pleasure demon into a courtesan and prove himself to
  his father."* Clock 0/6.
- **`myth-beat`** — the next concrete thing that happens if nobody stops it, scheduled
  against world time or a clock threshold. *"Santo carves Emmeralda at the Sylph's
  Embrace, night of day −3."*

### `schema.tql`

New attributes (follow the existing `myth-` comment style):

```
myth-agenda-status        pending | active | achieved | thwarted | abandoned | dormant
myth-agenda-clock-size    integer   # segments to completion
myth-agenda-clock-filled  integer
myth-agenda-priority      integer   # 1-5; who acts first when agendas collide
myth-beat-status          pending | played | narrated | preempted | rewritten | cancelled
myth-beat-when            string    # time key, e.g. "d-3/night"
myth-beat-trigger         string    # "time" | "clock>=N"
myth-beat-onscreen-if     string    # prose condition, e.g. "any PC at the Sylph's Embrace"
myth-time-index           integer   # ordinal world clock; on campaign AND on beat
```

New relations:

```
myth-agenda-holder   relates agenda, relates holder    # character | faction
myth-agenda-target   relates agenda, relates target    # character | faction | location
myth-beat-of         relates beat,   relates agenda
myth-beat-at         relates beat,   relates place
myth-beat-cast       relates beat,   relates member
myth-beat-outcome    relates beat,   relates event     # links a fired beat to its journal event
```

New entities, both `sub alh-note` so they inherit `name` / `description` / `content` and
match how `myth-lore` is modelled (`schema.tql:186`):

```
myth-agenda  owns the agenda-* attrs, plays myth-campaign-membership:element,
             myth-agenda-holder:agenda, myth-agenda-target:agenda,
             myth-beat-of:agenda, myth-lore-about:subject
myth-beat    owns the beat-* attrs + myth-time-index,
             plays myth-campaign-membership:element, myth-beat-of:beat,
             myth-beat-at:beat, myth-beat-cast:beat, myth-beat-outcome:beat
```

Existing entities gain `plays` clauses: `myth-character` and `myth-faction` gain
`myth-agenda-holder:holder`, `myth-agenda-target:target`, `myth-beat-cast:member`;
`myth-location` gains `myth-beat-at:place`; `myth-game-event` gains
`myth-beat-outcome:event`; `myth-campaign` gains `owns myth-time-index`. TypeDB `define`
is additive and the SessionStart hook reloads `schema.tql` idempotently every session, so
no migration script is needed.

### `mythras_engine.py` — pure logic, no I/O

The repo's stated architecture keeps rules pure and testable here. Put the clock and
scheduling arithmetic in this file:

- `parse_time_key(key) -> int` — `"d-3/night"` → ordinal. Four watches per day
  (`dawn|day|dusk|night`); `index = (day + 16) * 4 + watch_ordinal` so pre-tourney
  negative days stay non-negative.
- `format_time_key(index) -> str` — inverse, for display.
- `advance_clock(filled, size, by) -> (new_filled, completed: bool)` — saturating.
- `due_beats(beats, now_index, clocks) -> list` — beats whose time has arrived or whose
  `clock>=N` trigger is met, sorted by holding agenda's priority descending.
- `beat_staging(beat, pc_location_ids, pc_ids) -> "onscreen" | "offscreen"` — a beat is
  onscreen if its location or any cast member intersects where the PCs actually are.

These are the only parts worth unit tests, and they are the parts most likely to be wrong.

### `mythras_gm.py` — new commands

Follow the `cmd_add_lore` / `cmd_list_lore` / `cmd_get_lore` pattern
(`mythras_gm.py:1121-1200`): build a TypeQL `insert` string with `escape_string`, call
`_write`, then `_link_to_campaign`. Dispatch is automatic — `main()` resolves
`cmd_<command with dashes as underscores>` from `globals()`, so each handler just needs a
matching `sub.add_parser` in `build_parser()`.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `add-agenda --campaign --holder --title --goal --clock N [--priority] [--target] [--narrative]` | Create a goal held by an NPC or faction |
| `list-agendas --campaign [--holder] [--status]` | The GM's dashboard: who wants what, how close |
| `get-agenda --id` | Full text plus its pending beats |
| `advance-agenda --id --by N [--note]` | Fill clock segments; reports any beats now triggered |
| `set-agenda-status --id --status [--note]` | Mark achieved / thwarted when play decides it |
| `add-beat --agenda --title --when "d-3/night" [--at LOC] [--cast ids] [--onscreen-if TEXT] [--narrative]` | Schedule the next concrete thing |
| `list-beats --campaign [--pending] [--due] [--at LOC] [--involving CHAR]` | "What is about to happen, and where" |
| `revise-beat --id [--when] [--at] [--cast] [--onscreen-if] [--narrative] [--status]` | **The rewrite affordance** — bend the plan when play makes it stale |
| `fire-beat --id --outcome played\|narrated\|preempted\|rewritten [--narrative] [--log]` | Resolve a beat; `--log` writes a linked `myth-game-event` |
| `tick --campaign --to "d-2/dawn"` | **The core GM move.** Advance world time, return every newly-due beat flagged `onscreen`/`offscreen` |

`tick` is the piece that makes the world feel alive: it answers "what happened while the
player was doing something else," and it decides — from actual PC presence via
`myth-presence`, not from GM whim — whether a beat becomes a played scene or an
off-camera fact the PCs may later discover.

`cmd_get_context` (`mythras_gm.py:1442`) gains two blocks, both compact-safe: `agendas`
(title / holder / clock / status, active only) and `due_beats`. This keeps the save file
honest — a new session resumes knowing what the world is mid-way through doing.

### `campaign_io.py` — publishing

Agendas and beats are campaign content and must round-trip, or the product can't ship them.

- Export: `agendas/<slug>.md` and `beats/<slug>.md`, frontmatter + prose, mirroring the
  lore block at `campaign_io.py:205-218` and `:281-293`.
- `_read_tree` (`:477`): add `"agendas": md_records("agendas")` and
  `"beats": md_records("beats")`. Missing directories already return `[]`, so v1 packages
  keep importing unchanged.
- `import_campaign` (`:538`): add both keys to the id-remap list at `:544`, insert the
  entities, then rebuild `myth-agenda-holder` / `-target` / `myth-beat-of` / `-at` /
  `-cast` in the deferred pass (same ordering trick the lore-about links use at `:673`,
  since holders and cast must exist first).
- Bump `FORMAT_VERSION` to `"1.1"`; add an agenda summary to the generated README.

### Docs

- `SKILL.md`: add **"The world moves"** to the operating rules, and `tick` as step 2.5 of
  Quick Start — run it before each new scene, never narrate a day forward without it.
- `USAGE.md`: a "Living World" section documenting the agenda/beat loop and the time-key
  format, alongside the existing Rules Graph section.

---

## 2. The product package (`~/purewater-campaign-v2/`)

Built from the existing published package (`~/purewater-campaign`, which is the richer
source — it carries full structured PC weapon stats the v1 database never received), then
rewritten. v1 repo and v1 DB campaign are left untouched as the historical record.

- **Four entry points**, authored as player-facing lore (`lore/entry-points/`), each a
  playable opening scene with its own hook, not backstory:
  1. **Magda** — the ford outside the city. Hel's nightmares have driven her here; she
     picks Gardwen out of the crowd. She knows Purewater enough to find them both a bed
     with a madame — which is what puts her under Constantine's roof for Santo's attack.
  2. **Gardwen** — the same meeting from the other side: tracking the Dragon Knight column
     that took her brother, accosted by a staff-leaning old woman who knows too much.
  3. **Conall** — the road in, riding with Temerach, as the Dragon Knight column overtakes
     them bound for the tourney.
  4. **Randall** — Caravan Square, working the crowd, when the Baron comes through the
     gate and a guard blanches at Randall's face.
- **Agendas seeded** for Santo, Hanzo, Blau, Tat Atarer, Marisette, Crowbill, Temerach,
  Nerissa, Nus, and the Awake the Dragon movement — each with goal, clock, and the
  standing question *what changes their mind*.
- **Beats seeded** across the tournament clock (`d-3` → `d0`), including the branch the
  brief calls out explicitly: Santo's botched binding at the Sylph's Embrace fires
  onscreen if any PC is lodged there and off-camera otherwise, and a Randall/Hanzo
  encounter opens a new "the Baron knows he has another son" agenda.
- `lore/gm-guide/the-plot-timeline` is **replaced** by the agenda/beat graph and a new
  `GM Guide: Running the Living World` explaining the loop to a human GM.
- `journal/events.json` reduced to a single seed note; `campaign.yaml` renamed, session 0,
  `game_date: "d-3/dawn — arrival"`.
- Import with `--new-ids` as a new campaign, leaving `myth-campaign-66a98ba4a70e` intact.

---

## 3. Verification

1. `uv run --project skills/mythras-gm pytest tests/` — new cases in `tests/test_engine.py`
   for `parse_time_key` round-tripping, clock saturation, `due_beats` ordering by priority,
   and `beat_staging` returning onscreen only on real intersection.
2. Schema loads clean: re-run the SessionStart hook / `load-rules` path and confirm exit 0.
3. **Round-trip proof** — the claim that matters for a shippable product:
   `import-campaign --new-ids` the v2 package → `export-campaign` it back out → diff the
   two trees. Agenda and beat counts and their holder/cast relations must match.
4. **`tick` behaviour, both branches** — with Magda placed at the Sylph's Embrace,
   `tick --to "d-3/night"` must return Santo's beat flagged `onscreen`; with her moved
   elsewhere via `move-character`, the same tick must flag it `offscreen`. This is the
   feature working or not working.
5. Confirm `get-context --compact` shows the agenda block and stays small enough for play.
6. Confirm PC equipment survived: `get-character --id <magda>` shows a structured
   `Quarterstaff` object, so `resolve-attack` can find weapons by name.
7. Then sit down and play Magda's opening at the ford.

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

Other advertised Hub tools can search or inspect a known repo id. Use hf_whoami for the current Hugging Face account.

hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment.

arXiv paper ids (for example 2502.16161) are often used as references between datasets, models, and papers. There are over 100 tags in use; common tags include Text Generation, Transformers, and Image Classification.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'gulzarooster'

entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.

content.content:
### myth-campaign-8327f8687a98
count 19
 -  | Campaign seeded: Purewater, living-world build. 12 agendas, 14 beats, four playable entry points. World clock starts at d-3/dawn; the Tourney is d0.
 -  | SESSION 1 -- Purewater, living-world build. Play opens at the ford outside the city, d-3/dawn, three days before the Lake Lady's Tourney. Gully plays Magda; Gardwen, Conall and Randall are GM-run.
 -  | CH.1 -- The ford. Magda finds the woman from Hel's dream in the tourney queue, gets a hand into her wolf's ruff (Survival 12/63), tells her the dream, and kneels in the mud to swear herself to her. Gardwen -- alone ten years -- hauls her up rather than accept the staff, gives her name, and offers her forearm. They are travelling together.
 -  | CH.2 (offscreen) -- The di Teufel column comes through the water-gate into Caravan Square at midday: twenty-odd Dragon Knights and a covered litter the outriders keep the crowd off. Randall, working the crowd, is close enough that a knight at the Baron's stirrup gets a clear look at his face and goes white.
 -  | CH.3 -- Into the city. Magda faces down the customs man at the water-gate by presence alone (Willpower 43/63) and gets two on foot and 'a dog' through the boom without paying. He lets slip he is the third lot today through with something they will not show him. Gardwen, woodland-born, is badly unsettled by a city with no ground. Magda takes them to the Sylph's Embrace on the Pearl.
 -  | CH.4 -- The night at the Sylph's Embrace. Santo's binding SUCCEEDED (Lore Demonology 19/25 Formidable) -- a pleasure demon is seated in Emmeralda and the wound will not close. His escape fumbled (Stealth 100): he roused the house and went into the canal. Magda, at the water door, shot him in the head with her staff sling (33/57 Hard; 2d6=8 to the Head, -3hp, serious) and he drowned. Ila dived and hooked the body; Magda and Gardwen butchered it in Constantine's scullery and sent it to Renko's hog-yard in waste barrels. Magda kept the signet, cloak and four bundles of hair.
 -  | CH.5 -- Reconnaissance at the DragonBarge. Magda and Gardwen scout the Baron's steaming black ship at High Isle's seaward pier. Count: EIGHT Dragon Knights aboard, no banner, no Baron, no household -- he is lodged ashore NW round the point and the ship is fed twice daily by its own boat in armloads, food for a handful. One shuttered port amidships, barred from OUTSIDE. Nothing is collected from the ship; slops go in the water and barrows of clinker come off daily. Magda befriends Pell (Renko's waste lad), then gets Ann Yannick, the ship's laundress, to talk.
 -  | Marisette had the culprit's name inside a day -- Magda walked it to her before dawn
 -  | Nerissa now has a cause she can name
 -  | CH.6 -- Marisette's counting room, dusk. Magda reports the DragonBarge recon. Hesper, who has spent the afternoon with the demon in Emmeralda, identifies what is aboard: not a demon but a SHADE -- a bound dead man in a living host, maintained by the daily bleeding. Magda tells them Hel's dream ('lay the dragon warrior to rest'); Hesper seizes on 'rest' as proof it is a dead man, not a demon. Marisette refuses a frontal assault on the ship and sends them to High Priestess Nerissa instead.
 -  | CH.7 -- The Temple of the Lake Lady, midnight. Marisette's note and a grey wolf at the gate get them to Nerissa, who has not slept since noon the day before. Magda confesses the killing and the pigs outright; Nerissa reads her as truthful (Insight 56/80) and trades her own secret: the sacred channel went THIN four minutes after noon as the Baron entered, and Prince Emeric silenced her alarm in writing. Shown Santo's five twists of hair, Nerissa determines they were cut with shears from behind -- and names her niece Sana, nineteen, unseen for three weeks.
 -  | SESSION 1 ends at the Temple of the Lake Lady, midnight of d-2. Magda arrived at the ford a stranger and by the end of two days has sworn herself to Gardwen, killed the Baron's heir and destroyed the body, allied with the ruler of the Pearl, and brought the High Priestess of the Lake Lady into the story. Santo's binding SUCCEEDED (a divergence -- Emmeralda is possessed, not dying). Blau is hunting the missing heir and has not yet found the trail.
 -  | CH.8 -- Lost Isle. Gardwen's Detect Evil (Piety 46/44 failed from the bank; 46/69 succeeded holding Nerissa's hand in the channel, augmented by Love of Family) finds Sana alive and hiding in a tower-stub and two 'wrong' men below. Sana comes down on Magda's proof of an eleven-page letter about a heron. Magda kills one hollow man (sling to the arm, then a staff blow to the head after he had surrendered) and cripples the other; Gardwen's Hold Person grips him, which it should not. They take Ellick Sarn prisoner and uncover an ancient swept stair -- a door for laying the drowned to rest.
 -  | CH.9 -- The day before the Tourney. Ellick Sarn talks: he sold himself for warmth, the binding on the ship is 'furnished' and FIGHTS, and the morning cut keeps it tired. The name is Thuban Eta. Thorne identifies him from the muster rolls -- drowned by his own company for refusing to fire a valley, held by the betrayal itself, and nobody ever came back for him. Magda accepts that Hel's command means SHE must stand as proxy. Crowbill takes the job for the cargo; Ravella will cool the steaming hull for the return of two taken men; Hesper deduces the quiet one has gone to fetch Thuban's bones -- and is rowing them to the very stair the party holds.
 -  | CH.10 -- The Mouth. Ravella cools forty feet of burning hull; twelve of Crowbill's canal men go up the lines. Magda stays in the punt and slings: a critical under the raised arm blocks the rail, then a stone into Blau's unarmoured gut from forty yards. She goes up the rope on Brawn (berserk making it one grade easier) and a Luck Point, comes over the rail screaming Hel's fury, and cuts through to Blau. Gardwen's Entangle takes the whole waist of the ship. Magda kills Blau with a critical placed in the wound she had already made, then -- unable to break the rage (two failed Willpower rolls) -- kills nine helpless entangled men before it lets go of her.
 -  | CH.11 -- Lost Isle, the failed rite. Magda's first attempt for the two drowned men failed (87/52) -- Ravella corrected the form: do not ask Hel to take them, GIVE them to her and say somebody came back. The litany worked (52/66). The quiet one landed with Thuban's bones and was taken clean by the Swords; he refused to talk, and Magda beheaded him where he sat -- costing Nerissa the only lead to Bettan. The great rite then FAILED (47/44, Luck re-roll 56) because the Baron still wore the latch round his neck.
 -  | CH.12 -- The Lake Lady's Tourney. Temerach wins the Archery with a critical on the moving-boat pass. Nerissa is displaced from presenting the prize by the chamberlain Vosk, so the warning never reaches her (94/80) -- but the box arrives on time. Hanzo holds his face over a severed head (58/94), makes his excuses and leaves for his boat. On the water-stair Magda slings him off his feet, breaks his casting wrist with the quarterstaff, slaps his good hand down and tears the locket off his throat on an Unarmed critical. Temerach arrests him by warrant.
 -  | CH.13 -- The stair, and the funeral. With bones, door and latch in one place for the first time in a century, Magda stood two steps into the black water where nine men drowned a bound knight, told his tale, named the murder, and gave him to Hel (28/66). The locket opened by itself. Something went down past her legs, unhurried, and looked at her once. The boy survived it. Magda -- who had killed eleven people in two days -- went to her knees and wept on Gardwen and the boy until she couldn't breathe.
 -  | SESSION 1 ENDS at the Moist Oyster, the night of the Lake Lady's Tourney -- Conall and Randall seeing each other for the first time in twenty-two years across a crowded room. In four days Magda arrived a stranger at a ford, swore herself to Gardwen, killed the Baron's heir and fed him to pigs, took a ship in the Mouth, killed Blau, laid a thousand-year-old knight to rest, and tore the binding locket off a Baron's throat. Thuban Eta is at rest. Cailan -- 'Bird' -- is free and empty and his own. Hanzo di Teufel is in irons awaiting a magistrate. STILL OPEN: Bettan and the third filled girl; Emmeralda still carrying her demon; the Awake the Dragon Movement, who have lost their candidate but keep Thuban's border tower; and two bastard di Teufel twins who have just become extremely interesting to some very bad people.

---

### Where we left off

Santo di Teufel is dead in the woods north of the Lullwater — Randall cut his throat over the bait-trap, and the party escaped across the canals with the Asmodeus soul-knife. That escape left a wake: a Dragon Knight glimpsed Randall's face and swears the runner "looked just like Lord Santo," a rooted thug lived to describe Magda, Gardwen and Ruhi, and by dawn the Baron had dragon-gold on the street for that face.

Randall walked the problem instead of running it — turned Crowbill's watcher at the Moist Oyster, and bought an audience at the counting-house off Gallows Reach. Crowbill saw the soul-knife: demon-craft worked on a helpless girl, beside the Lady's water, in *his* city. He's in. Canals, safe houses, men, and the rumor-machine — for three prices: the Baron's plan, a way into the fortified estate (finishing Nus's map), and full control of the twins' street-story.

And he left you with a thing to chew on: **the Baron's champion has never once left the estate.** Unseen. Kept like a relic.

---

### The scene

The counting-house is quiet now. Crowbill's ledgers are back on the desk, the crow tattoo has gone back under a cuff, and the two men at the door have shifted just enough to say the meeting is over. Temerach has the soul-knife wrapped again under her cloak. Conall's borrowed face is still holding, and outside the shuttered window the Gallows Reach water is running grey with early light.

Two days. Somewhere behind an estate wall there is a champion no one has seen, and a Baron who does not spend infernal craft on tourney prizes.

---

The hand comes out of the cloak. Empty.

"Gardwen," she says.

And then, in a voice that has clearly had this conversation before and expects nothing from it:

You grunt. It's not a word. It's the noise you make at a gate that's swollen shut, and it carries about the same amount of argument.

"I've been dreaming of you, girl."

And then you walk past her.

Not at her — *past* her, on the wolf's side, which is the wrong side, which is the side no one uses. You don't slow and you don't reach out early and you don't do the thing townsfolk do where they put the hand out flat like they're presenting a document. You walk the way you'd walk to a gatepost, and when you get there you put your hand into the fur at the base of its neck, where the ruff is thickest and a hand disappears to the wrist.

The wolf goes rigid.

You can feel it under your palm — the whole animal locking, every muscle from shoulder to haunch making one decision at once, and its head comes round and there is a moment where its jaw is four inches from your forearm and its breath is hot on the inside of your wrist.

You don't move your hand. You scratch. Down, once, the way you'd work a burr out.

The rigidity goes. Not all at once — it comes out of the shoulders first and then the back, and the head turns away from your arm, and the animal makes a sound low in its chest that isn't a growl and isn't anything a townsman would recognise as anything at all.

2. **A burning house.**
3. **A knight in dragon-scale who is already dead but does not know it.**

And one instruction, which is the part you've been chewing on for three weeks of road: ***"lay the dragon warrior to rest."*** Not *kill*. Hel was specific by being unspecific, the way she is. You've turned it over a hundred miles and it still won't come apart.

"Hel," you say. "Death."

The wolf's weight settles further against your shin.

"Not death in battle." You say it the way you'd correct someone about which field the boundary stone is in. "The other kind. Everywhere else. In the bed, in the byre, in the bad winter. The ones nobody sings about."

Gardwen goes very still.

She was braced for a priest — the singing kind, the kind who tell a woman with a dead family that it was a mercy and a plan. She had something sharp ready for that.

She doesn't use it.

"No," she says quietly. "No, that's — " and she stops, and looks at the mud, and you watch her decide something.

"That's an honest god."

She still doesn't move with it.

"I've had eleven nights of you too, then, have I." Not really a question — she's testing the shape of it, turning it the way you turned *lay him to rest*. "What does she show you?"

Her hand has gone into Ruhi's ruff beside yours. She doesn't seem to have noticed doing it. Her knuckles are white.

Gardwen's knuckles in the ruff go from white to slack.

You can see the arithmetic happening. *Dragon-scale.* Not the answer she wanted — but not a stranger to her either, and you can see it cut a different way than you meant it, and there is nothing to be done about that. Her eyes go north, to the road, to the churned mud where twenty-odd riders in scale went through at a pace that said *move*.

She doesn't say the rest. Whatever the rest is, it stays in.

Then you kneel.

The mud takes your knee with a sound like a boot coming out of a bog, and it is cold, and it goes straight through the wool, and you are seventy years old on the outside and there is absolutely nothing dignified about any part of this. ===== USER [2026-09-07T17:00:28.895Z] =====
Back to the game! 

Head out with Hesper. Spoiling for some action!


===== ASSISTANT [2026-09-07T17:01:23.872Z] =====
Dusk. Bells over the water. The Tourney bunting looks like it's been up a week.

Hesper comes out of the green room with a canvas bag, a physician's coat over something heavier, and the expression of a man who has just told a demon he'll be back shortly and been told *"of course you will, dear."*

He does not look forward to any part of tonight.

Ila brings Ruhi out to the step and hands the lead over and says "bring her back" to Gardwen, and then, after a pause, "and you," which is the most she manages.

---

**What the evening has decided while you were walking:**

**The DragonBarge is holding to the ebb.** She hasn't moved early. Marisette's watchers say she's still at the pier with steam off her waterline and men at the ropes — she'll go on the tide, as Crowbill planned for, some time after the eighth bell.

**Blau has failed to find you a third time.** Three days he's had the city's ear open and this city has told him nothing whatsoever. Thorne's *"never seen her,"* a fishmonger, forty people in a working yard, a customs man who wrote *dog* on his tally-board. Nobody has given you up.

**And the quiet one is not going to make the ebb.**

Ravella's people have the eastern approaches and there's no small boat coming in off the sea road yet. He's overdue by a day and he's carrying something he won't risk in bad water — which means the bones arrive **after** the ship sails.

Two things, two places, and not at the same time.

- **The Mouth** — Crowbill's twelve, Ravella's water-folk, a cold hull, and a boy behind a barred shutter.
- **Lost Isle** — Nerissa, a dozen Swords, a swept stair, and at some point tonight a quiet man rowing in with a century of bones and no idea who's sitting on his doorstep.

Hesper has to be at the stair for the removal. Crowbill's people need somebody they'll take orders from at the ship.

Where do you go?


===== USER [2026-09-07T17:04:42.350Z] =====
The Mouth. Definitely. Time to break some dragons.


===== ASSISTANT [2026-09-07T17:05:07.463Z] =====
Hesper takes it well. "Then I'll go to the stair. Nerissa will want telling what a removal actually needs, and somebody ought to be there when the quiet one arrives who knows what he's looking at."

He shoulders the bag.

"Magda. Get the boy off that ship *breathing*. I can work with almost anything else."

---

**The Mouth**, three hours later.

A mile of slow black water where the harbour lets out to sea, with the city's lights behind you and nothing ahead. The ebb has started — you can feel the pull of it under the punt, patient and enormous.

**Six punts, no lights.** Crowbill's twelve are exactly what he promised: canal men in dark wool, no armour worth the name, barefoot, each with a short blade and a coil of line and a grapnel wrapped in sacking so it can't ring. They talk in a low register that doesn't carry over water. None of them has asked what's on the ship.

Crowbill himself is not here. Of course he isn't.

**Ravella is.** She's in the bow of your punt in something that isn't a dress, with four of hers in the water alongside — you can't see them, but occasionally the surface does something a surface shouldn't.

**Gardwen** is amidships with her staff across her knees. **Ruhi** would not get in the boat and is somewhere on the north bank keeping pace, which nobody has been able to prevent.

You're in mail, with Vell's axe across your back and fourteen stones in the pouch.

---

Then the lights change at the pier end of the harbour, a mile back.

A lantern goes up and comes down. Another. Marisette's watchers, doing it as agreed.

**She's cast off.**

And a long time later — twenty minutes, half an hour, an age of sitting in the dark — you see her.

She comes down the channel under a scrap of canvas and the sweeps, unlit but for a single shaded lamp at the stern, and she is enormous close-to, and even at two hundred yards you can see the white where her hull meets the water and hear the *hiss* of it carrying flat across the surface.

Ravella turns round in the bow.

"When I go in, that water will kill anyone who isn't mine for about a minute while it turns." Her eyes hold the dark. "After that it's cold and it's climbable and I can hold it as long as I'm conscious."

She waits.

"So say when, and be sure. Because I only get to do this once tonight."


===== USER [2026-09-07T18:03:24.696Z] =====
Wait until the barge gets in position then give the signal. I’m probably not a very good swimmer, so I might need some help to stop myself from drowning (ha ha ha)


===== ASSISTANT [2026-09-07T18:03:49.727Z] =====
You let her come.

Two hundred yards. One-fifty. She's making maybe three knots on the ebb with the sweeps barely dipping, and the hiss gets louder, and you can smell her now — hot metal and something under it like scorched fat.

A hundred yards. The punts have drifted apart into their three groups without a word passing.

Eighty. You can see men on her deck, forward, looking where she's going.

"**Now.**"

Ravella doesn't answer. She goes over the side without a splash and the water takes her like it was expecting her.

*(And your joke lands better than you meant it — you are in a **mail hauberk** with **Swim 27**. If you go in that channel tonight you go straight to the bottom of it. Nobody is letting you swim anywhere.)*

The nearest canal man grins at you in the dark and taps the grapnel line. *You go up from the boat, mother. Feet dry.*


===== ASSISTANT [2026-09-07T18:04:16.435Z] =====
**36 against 75 — she does it.**

**22 — and somebody aboard feels it.**

---

The water goes first.

You don't see her do it. What you see is the white line along that hull *stop* — forty feet of hissing steam just ceasing, mid-length, like a candle pinched out, and the dead-water slick behind it going dark and ordinary and cold.

Six punts move at once.

Grapnels go up in sacking and land with a sound like a fist in a pillow. Canal men are on the lines before the hooks have set, going up the side of a moving ship barefoot with knives in their teeth, and it is the most casually competent thing you have ever watched anybody do.

# Beat-level journal, session 1, extracted verbatim from the Claude Code session log
# 5619508f-cb80-4598-a9b6-188fe11c1157.jsonl. Timestamps are the real play clock.
