BEATS = [

("2026-09-06T06:53:40", "scene", M+","+G+","+FORD,
 "The ford: Magda walks out of the queue to the woman nobody will stand near, and asks her name.",
 """Thirty feet of churned mud, and the whole queue has already decided the space around that woman belongs to somebody else's problem. At twelve feet the wolf stands up -- no growl, no teeth, just rising off its haunches to face her square, and every conversation within thirty feet stops.

Gardwen's hand goes inside her cloak. Not fast. The way you put a hand on a door latch in a house you don't trust.

Magda stops an arm's length outside what the wolf considers hers, nods once -- the nod you'd give a neighbour over a fence -- and asks: "Who are you?"

It lands wrong. She was braced for *what do you want* or *get that animal away from me*, and had answers ready for both. The hand comes out of the cloak. Empty.

"Gardwen," she says. And then, in a voice that has had this conversation before and expects nothing from it: "You'll want to be somewhere else, mother. People who stand near me have a poor time of it."
"""),

("2026-09-06T06:58:29", "skill-roll", M+","+G+","+RU+","+FORD,
 "Magda walks past Gardwen on the wolf's side and puts her hand in Ruhi's ruff. Survival 12/63.",
 """"I've been dreaming of you, girl."

She doesn't reach out early and she doesn't put a flat hand out the way townsfolk do. She walks the way you'd walk to a gatepost, on the wolf's side, which is the wrong side, which is the side nobody uses -- and puts her hand into the fur at the base of the neck where a hand disappears to the wrist.

The wolf locks. Its jaw comes round four inches from her forearm. She doesn't move her hand. She scratches, down, once, the way you'd work out a burr.

Up north they'd say the dog had decided you were furniture, and furniture is the highest rank a stranger gets.

"--*don't*," Gardwen says. Too late by three seconds. "Ruhi doesn't let people do that."

"My goddess tells me you're someone I need to help. Don't know why. That's what she told me."

"Your goddess," she says slowly. "Which one." -- and Magda can hear what the question actually is. She's asking whether this is one of the singing ones. Ruhi sits back down. Against Magda's leg, now, not hers. Gardwen notices that too.
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:02:28", "decision", M+","+G+","+FORD,
 "\"Hel. Death. Not death in battle -- the other kind. Everywhere else.\" Gardwen: \"That's an honest god.\"",
 """"Not death in battle." Said the way you'd correct someone about which field the boundary stone is in. "The other kind. Everywhere else. In the bed, in the byre, in the bad winter. The ones nobody sings about."

Gardwen goes very still. It's the look of a bucket that's had the bottom go out of it -- she was braced for a priest, the singing kind, the kind who tell a woman with a dead family that it was a mercy and a plan. She had something sharp ready for that. She doesn't use it.

"No," she says quietly. "No, that's -- that's an honest god."

Then, before Magda can answer, she asks the real one instead, fast, like a woman pulling a splinter:

"Does she show you a boy?"

Her hand has gone into Ruhi's ruff beside Magda's. She doesn't seem to have noticed doing it. Her knuckles are white.
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:06:56", "decision", M+","+G+","+FORD,
 "\"No. Not a boy. A knight in dragon-scale.\" Then Magda kneels in the mud and offers her staff. Gardwen refuses it and hauls her up instead.",
 """"A knight. Dragon-scale. Never seen anyone look that way before, and I've seen a great many people look a great many ways. He's dead, girl. Standing up and walking and dead, and nobody's told him."

Gardwen's knuckles in the ruff go from white to slack. Her eyes go north, to the churned mud where twenty-odd riders in scale went through at a pace that said *move*.

"Dragon Knights," she says. Flat. "It's Dragon Knights you dream of."

Then Magda kneels. The mud takes her knee with a sound like a boot coming out of a bog, and it is cold, and it goes straight through the wool, and she is seventy years old on the outside and there is nothing dignified about any part of it. Somewhere behind her one of the tumblers says something and another one laughs and is hit.

She holds out the staff crosswise, both hands, the way her grandmother did it to a man who died the following spring. "I'm to fight for you, girl. Protect you and yours, however you'd ask it. Die for you, if it comes to that."

Gardwen doesn't take the staff.

"Get up," she says. It comes out wrong. She tries again. "Get *up*. You'll -- the ground's freezing, you'll ruin your knees, get up--" And she's reaching down to haul her, one hand under her arm, and her grip is stronger than it looks and it is not steady at all.

"Ten years," she says, very low, only for Magda. "Ten years and not one person. Not one. And a pig-farmer kneels in the *mud* at a *ford*--" She stops. Swallows it. Puts the flat watchfulness back on like a hat, and it doesn't sit right any more, and she knows it doesn't.

"I don't know what to do with you," she says. Then, properly, offering her forearm the way soldiers do, the woodland version, wrist to wrist: "Gardwen. My brother was taken by men in that armour. Ten years ago. He's the only thing I have left to look for, and if your god has business with a dead man in dragon-scale then Hel and I want the same road for a while."

RECORDED: Magda gains the Passion **Sworn to Gardwen (by Hel) 70**.

AND THE THING NEITHER OF THEM CAN SEE: Gardwen has just heard *a knight in dragon-scale who is already dead* and filed it under the enemy who took her brother. She cannot connect it to *him*. Magda's dream is pointing straight at the thing she has walked ten years to find, and the graph will not let either of them know it.
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:11:47", "scene", M+","+G+","+PW,
 "The causeway. Gardwen asks about the dream twice more, from different sides. She never asks about the burning house.",
 """Two miles of raised stone across a flat of reed and standing water, at the pace of the slowest cart. Gulls. The smell getting stronger and less like salt.

"Three days I've been eating their dust," Gardwen says. "Then they have to queue like everyone else, and I'm suddenly close enough to smell the horses. I don't know whether that's luck."

She talks a little, the way people do when they haven't in a while -- mostly about the road, nothing about the ten years. She asks twice more about the dream, in different words, hunting the same answer from different sides. She gets the same three things each time. A woman with a wolf. A burning house. A dead man in dragon-scale.

She doesn't ask about the burning house. Magda notices that she doesn't.
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:17:44", "skill-roll", M+","+G+","+PW,
 "\"No bollocks from these fuckers.\" Magda walks up the line to the customs man and intimidates two women and a wolf into Purewater. Willpower 43/63.",
 """She doesn't wait to be got to. She goes to him -- straight up the line past the fishmonger, past a family with a goat, until she's standing at his elbow with the wolf at her knee. Which is wrong, and everyone in the queue knows it's wrong.

He turns with his mouth already open. Something practised. *Back in line, mother.*

She looks at him. She has put her hand over the eyes of men who were shouting an hour before, and gone out afterwards and fed the pigs, because the pigs don't care. Whatever that does to a face, it has had fifty years to do it to hers, and she lets him have all of it.

"We're going in."

The mouth closes. He looks at the staff, which is not a walking stick and has never once pretended to be. He looks at the wet grey animal watching him with the total patient attention of something that has never in its life been told it's a good girl.

"There's a fee," he says. It comes out with no starch in it at all.

"There is." A pause long enough for him to understand she is not going to fill it.

"Two on foot," he says to his tally-board. "And a *dog*." He writes *dog*. He underlines *dog*, as though the underlining is a form of protest that history will one day recognise. "--and I never saw it."

"You never did."

And as she passes under the chain-boom, because he can't help it, because the thing has been sitting in the top of his head all morning: "Third lot today gone through with something they won't show me."
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:21:36", "scene", M+","+G+","+RU+","+PW,
 "Gardwen learns the ledges. A ferryman charges for the wolf and not for her, and won't say why.",
 """There is no ground. That's the thing nobody tells you and Magda had forgotten. Buildings, and water, and between them ledges a yard wide, no rail, slick as an eel -- and the traffic that matters is underneath you, poled and rowed, shouting.

Gardwen stops dead six feet inside the gate with her hand knotted in Ruhi's ruff and her back to a wall, breathing like someone who has just been put somewhere with no trees. "There's no *ground*," she says.

She learns it the way woodland people learn things: badly for ten minutes, then all at once. Magda keeps her on the inside, hand flat on the wall, and after the third bridge she stops looking at her feet and starts looking at the water. After the fifth she's reading it -- which boat has right of way, which shout means *move*, which of the poled barges will take a passenger and which is somebody's home.

Ruhi hates all of it and does it anyway, low and close, ears flat, a wet grey misery at heel.

The ferryman across the Lullwater charges for the wolf and doesn't charge for Gardwen, and won't explain why.

Everywhere, bunting. Somebody's cousin selling favours in di Teufel colours off a tray -- dragon-scale green, three for a copper -- and doing well at it. Away over the roofs a bell starts up, and then another one, ragged, out of time with the first. The bells stop. Nobody they pass seems to know what they were for.
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:27:27", "scene", M+","+G+","+CO+","+EM+","+IL+","+SYLPH,
 "The Sylph's Embrace. Constantine opens the door twenty years older than the knock remembers. Ila drops an armful of linen at the sight of a wolf.",
 """A green door under a carved lintel -- a sylph, wings folded, worn nearly smooth by two hundred years of hands. Magda knocks the way she knocked twenty years ago.

"*Magda.*" -- "Constantine." -- "You're not dead." He says it with genuine delight, as one professional to another. "Not yet. It keeps being suggested."

He takes in the rest of it in one pass -- the young woman standing too straight, the staff, the wolf -- and to his enormous credit the only thing that moves is one eyebrow, and only slightly. "Beds. It's Tourney week, I've got the city and half the border in my lap and every room's spoken for -- so you'll have the top back room over the water, and it's cold, and the shutter sticks, and I'll bring a brazier up. Bring the dog. If it eats a client I'll take it out of your purse."

A girl of about thirteen goes past the foot of the stairs with an armful of linen twice her size, sees the wolf, stops dead, and drops the entire load. "*Ila*," Constantine says, without heat. She isn't listening.

And on the landing above, leaning on the rail with her hair down: "Constantine, you've brought home a *wolf*." -- "I've brought home a *friend*, Emmeralda. The wolf is incidental."

Emmeralda takes Magda's chin in two fingers, unhurried, professional, examining. "Not one day. Not *one*. You were a hard old woman when I was a young one and you're the same hard old woman now, and I've had two decades of people telling me *my* face is unnatural." -- "Mine's a curse." -- "Mine's an *asset*."

Then, later, quietly, reading her the way Magda read the customs man: "You didn't come for the Tourney." -- "No." -- "No." She accepts that, and files it, and doesn't push.
"""),

("2026-09-06T07:56:00", "scene", G+","+EM+","+SYLPH,
 "Upstairs, over bread and cold fowl, Gardwen says the elf was afraid of something. \"It's not a thing you can point at. The field's wrong.\"",
 """Constantine brings it up himself: bread, a hard yellow cheese, half a cold fowl, a jug of the brown beer they make out on the Shoals, and a brazier he sets going with a professional's economy of movement. The shutter does stick, and when it opens the canal is directly below -- close enough to hear the water working at the stone, and a barge going through in the dark with a lantern on its bow.

Gardwen eats like someone who has been rationing without admitting it.

"That woman," she says eventually, with her mouth full. "The elf. She was afraid of something. Not of us. Underneath. The way a doe is when there's nothing in the field. It's not a thing you can point at, it's just -- the field's wrong."

Then she puts her cup on the sill and looks out at the dark water. "Magda. I've got no plan. That's the truth of it. I've followed that column for three days on nothing but *keep them in sight*, and now they're behind a wall somewhere in this city and I don't know one street from another and I've a wolf that can't be seen and no coin left worth the name. You said we'd plan. So plan at me, because I've nothing."

Down in the house someone starts up on a stringed instrument, badly, and is shouted at, and gets better.

And three floors below there's a knock -- the sort a young man gives a door when he's certain of his welcome -- and a young man's voice, well-bred, border vowels, asking by name for Emmeralda.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:39:59", "skill-roll", M+","+SA+","+SYLPH,
 "Magda creeps to the turn of the stair and watches Santo di Teufel come into the house. Stealth 39/68.",
 """She gets the door shut without the latch speaking and goes down as far as the turn above the second landing, where the overhang puts her in shadow and the hall lamp doesn't reach.

Constantine has his back to her. The young man is facing him -- hood back, dark clothes, road-dust still on the hem. Nothing in his hands. He's talking, quickly, and Constantine is nodding in the way he nods.

Then Emmeralda comes into view from the parlour door. She's changed since the afternoon: hair up, something green. She says something. The young man laughs.

Then she goes up the near stair -- the one that comes past the second landing, twelve feet from where Magda is standing -- and the young man follows her. They'll pass below her in a few seconds.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:42:35", "decision", M+","+SA+","+EM+","+SYLPH,
 "THE CHOICE NOT TAKEN: \"Withdraw -- not my business.\" Magda watches Santo go up the stairs with Emmeralda and goes back to bed.",
 """The shadow is good. It is not a wall. They are about to come up the near stair and pass within twelve feet of her, and staying put becomes a contested thing.

She has about three seconds to hold or withdraw.

"Withdraw. Not my business."

She goes back up. Gardwen doesn't ask. Ruhi resettles across the door and the house carries on being a house.

It is not her house and it is not her business and Hel did not walk her three hundred miles to mind a brothel door. Constantine has run this place for thirty years. Emmeralda is not a girl.

Some while later -- an hour, maybe more -- it goes wrong downstairs.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:43:03", "gm-note", SA+","+EM+","+SYLPH,
 "OFFSCREEN, ROLLED NOT SCRIPTED: Santo's binding SUCCEEDS (Lore Demonology 19 vs Formidable 25). His escape FUMBLES (Stealth 100).",
 """The written adventure has Santo botch the binding and leave Emmeralda dying. The dice said otherwise at the very first hinge, and the whole back half of the campaign came out of it.

**Santo -- Lore (Demonology), Formidable (50 -> 25). Rolled 19. Success.** His father does this work. He has watched. Whatever he came to that house to do, he did it.

**Then Stealth 50. Rolled 100. Fumble.**

There is no scream. There is a crash -- something big going over, a table or a chest, and glass after it -- and then a man's voice, high and completely undone, saying *no no no no* very fast, and a door hitting a wall hard enough to shake the frame two floors up. Running feet on the canal-side stair. A slip. A worse noise: a body hitting a landing full length and something metal skittering away across boards. A shutter thrown. And a splash in the canal below far too big to be a man getting neatly into a boat.

Then voices all over the house. Constantine bellowing. Someone hammering on a door. And under it all, from the room they went into: nothing at all.

CONSEQUENCE: because the binding took, Emmeralda lives -- comfortable, chatty, house-proud, and possessed. That is the only reason anyone in Purewater ever learns what a shade is.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:46:47", "skill-roll", M+","+IL+","+SYLPH,
 "Down three flights in the dark at seventy. Athletics 69/50 -- failure. Ila hits her on the second landing, white to the lips.",
 """A failure here costs time and wind, not the trail. She arrives breathing hard.

It's **Ila**, barefoot in a shift, going flat out -- she hits Magda rather than stops, grabs two fistfuls of her skirt, and her face is white all the way to the lips.

"She won't *open* it--" She's hauling, trying to turn her round, back up. "The door's shut and she won't open it and Constantine's got the bar out and Emmeralda *won't answer*--"

Gardwen goes past both of them toward that door without breaking stride.

Ila's hands are still in her skirt. Below, the canal-side stair keeps going down -- past the boot room, to the water door and the slipway. Nobody has gone that way. Everyone in this house is going *up*. Down there in the dark it's quiet, and the water is still moving from whatever went into it.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:49:00", "decision", M+","+SYLPH,
 "Magda goes DOWN instead of up. Boot room, water door, slipway -- loading the sling as she goes.",
 """Ila's hands come off her skirt.

Boot room, then the water door -- unbarred, standing half open, swinging. Whoever came through here left it that way. She loads as she goes: stone in the pouch, cord round the knuckles, staff cocked back along the forearm.

Four stone steps going down into black water, green and slick below the third. A skiff moored to the ring at the bottom, riding oddly -- the painter's still tied but the boat's been shoved out and drifted back, and it's rocking hard, more than the canal's doing.

The water directly off the slipway is still working. Not ripples -- the deep slow turnover of something that went in heavy and recently.

One lamp on the far bank forty feet off. Under the surface, nothing at all.

Something is on the second step down, right at the waterline -- a shape that isn't stone.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:50:25", "skill-roll", M+","+SYLPH,
 "She hauls a soaked cloak off the mooring ring and scans forty feet of black water. Perception 51/70 -- the swimmer.",
 """Heavy with canal, dark, good cloth, expensive, the hem still carrying road-dust under the wet. It was caught on the mooring ring. It did not come off a man who was being careful.

Thirty feet out and moving left, upstream: the fast ugly chop of somebody swimming badly and in a hurry. A head, the pale smear of a face turning back toward the house, and then just the shoulders working.

He's making for the far ledge where the lamp is. There's a set of iron rungs up the wall under it. Forty feet of open water between him and them, and he's covered maybe a third.

He hasn't seen her. She's a shape in a dark doorway and he's looking at the upper windows, where all the noise is.

The sling is loaded and the range is nothing.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:51:20", "combat", M+","+SA+","+SYLPH,
 "\"Kill whatever that is.\" Berserker style, Hard 33/57. 2d6=8 to the Head, no helmet. Santo di Teufel drowns thirty feet off Constantine's slipway.",
 """Backlit against the far lamp, thirty feet, swimming hard. Dark water and a moving target. **Berserker combat style, Hard (85 -> 57). 33 -- a hit. 8 damage. Head. No helmet -- he's swimming. 5 hit points there; he's at -3. Serious wound.**

The staff comes over and the stone goes out flat across the water with that low buzzing note they make.

She doesn't hear it hit. She *sees* it -- the head snaps sideways, hard, wrong, the way a head does when it has stopped being steered from inside. The working shoulders stop working.

He goes under without a sound. No thrashing. No cry. The chop where he was smooths out into ordinary canal, and the wake he'd been dragging catches up with the place he isn't any more, and there is one hand above the surface for a moment, open, not grasping at anything -- and then that's gone too.

Forty feet away the lamp on the far bank goes on being a lamp. The iron rungs he was making for go on being empty. The water closes and keeps moving.

Behind her, up in the house, a woman starts screaming, and this one doesn't stop.
"""),

("2026-09-06T12:53:11", "skill-roll", M+","+SYLPH,
 "Searching a wet cloak in the dark with feet on the stairs above. Perception 62/47 -- she doesn't finish.",
 """Outer pockets first, because that's where a hurrying man puts things: a few coins, a folded scrap gone to pulp in the canal, a lump of resin or wax.

("2026-09-06T12:59:38", "skill-roll", M+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:03:45", "scene", M+","+G+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:06:14", "skill-roll", M+","+EM+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:08:33", "scene", M+","+EM+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:10:56", "decision", M+","+EM+","+CO+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:19:00", "decision", M+","+G+","+CO+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:22:38", "skill-roll", G+","+M+","+CO+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:27:20", "decision", M+","+IL+","+CO+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:32:17", "scene", M+","+G+","+IL+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:32:32", "skill-roll", IL+","+M+","+SYLPH,
 "Ila goes over the side. Willpower 44/72, Swim 8/40 -- barely off a critical. She surfaces saying the right thing first: \"His face is up.\"",

("2026-09-06T13:36:00", "decision", M+","+CO+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:38:59", "decision", M+","+CO+","+SYLPH,
 "THE DEBATE THE JOURNAL LOST: \"How about we do this -- he's never found?\" Constantine: \"Never found is harder than it sounds in a city that dredges itself.\"",
 """Magda shrugs. Keep the ring, keep the clothes, keep the cloak. He's never found.

Constantine looks at the sack for a while.

("2026-09-06T13:39:20", "scene", M+","+IL+","+SYLPH,

("2026-09-06T13:44:05", "decision", M+","+G+","+CO+","+SYLPH,

Constantine laughs -- one, no humour in it at all. "Of course you will." He puts the pole in and starts bringing the skiff back round. "There's a saw and a cleaver in the scullery. And a bone-tub. Don't ask me why I know where they are."

("2026-09-06T13:47:46", "scene", M+","+G+","+SYLPH,

She takes a clean sheet off the folded stack and shakes it out flat across the bench and puts her hand down on it. "Sheet goes on the bed this way -- hem to the head, you can tell from the wear where a man's heels go. So." She lays her palm high on it, a little left of the middle. "It's *here*. Every morning, four days. About the size of my two hands together."

She spreads her fingers. "Upper body. Left side. Chest, or just under the arm -- high enough that if he was on his back it ran sideways, because the edge of it's always feathered toward the outside. Same spot, same size, and it's *sharp*-edged, not spread. That's not a wound that's healing and breaking open. A healing wound weeps different every day, wider then narrower, and the shape wanders. This doesn't wander.

"Somebody opens the same place, the same way, every morning. And then somebody else changes the bed.

"And the grey. That's not in the blood. It's *round* it -- you get the red out and the grey stays behind in a ring, like a scorch. That's what numbs your hands."

Then she squares the sheet off on the stack and stands there with both hands on it. "You said choose sides."

She goes to the end copper and lifts the lid and starts fishing the load out. "They're due at the sixth bell for that. They'll get it. I'll smile at the white-haired bastard and take his coin.

"But you tell Marisette that Ann Yannick washes for that ship every morning, and she'll go on doing it, and she'll go on *looking*. And if that boy's still bleeding on the day of the Tourney, I want somebody to have done something about it."
"""),

("2026-09-06T15:53:20", "decision", M+","+HE+","+MA+","+PEARL,
 "THE TIMELINE. The ship came five days ago; the laundry started four days ago; the Baron was still three days up the road. \"Nobody started anything here. That is a *routine*.\"",
 """"No," Marisette says. "The Baron rode in through Caravan Square yesterday at midday. I had it from three people within the hour. But the *ship* came before him. ("2026-09-06T15:56:13", "decision", M+","+HE+","+G+","+PEARL,
 "Magda tells them Hel's dream, and Hesper seizes on one word. \"You don't lay a demon to rest. You lay a *dead man* to rest.\"",
 """She tells them. The eleven nights, the woman with the wolf, the burning house, and the knight in dragon-scale who is dead and hasn't been told. And what Hel asked: *lay the dragon warrior to rest.*

Hesper does not say anything for a long time. When he does, his voice has changed -- the unremarkableness has gone out of it.

"Say the last part again." -- "Lay the dragon warrior to rest."

"*Rest*," he repeats. "Not destroy. Not banish. **Rest.**" He puts both hands flat on his knees. "Madam, you don't lay a demon to rest. There's nothing in a demon to rest. You bind it or you break it and either way you may as well be arguing with a fire.

"You lay a *dead man* to rest."

He stands and takes two steps and stops, because it's a small room. "'The old kind. The kind that remembers being a person.' That is a **shade**. A person who died and did not go where the dead go -- kept, and bound, and put somewhere. And you cannot keep a shade in a jar or a stone for long, it wears through. You keep it in a *living body*, because a living body renews itself, and the wearing-through goes into the flesh instead of the vessel.

"Which is why somebody opens the same place on that boy's chest every single morning. It's not torture and it's not a ritual scar. It's *maintenance*. You bleed the host to keep the seat clean. The grey your laundress can't boil out is what comes off the seam -- that's the shade's wear coming out of him with the blood, and it's numbing her hands through a copper of lye."

Gardwen has not moved at all. "How long," she says, "can they keep a person like that?"

"Years," says Hesper. "If they start young enough that the body grows around it."

"""),

("2026-09-06T16:01:42", "scene", M+","+G+","+PEARL,

("2026-09-06T16:01:43", "decision", M+","+NE+","+MA+","+PEARL,

("2026-09-06T16:06:59", "decision", M+","+MA+","+HE+","+PEARL,
 "\"There's only 8 of them on that boat. With enough men we could just go and get him.\" Marisette: \"It's not that it's stupid. It's that it's *last*.\" Hesper: \"You'd be stealing a lit lamp.\"",
 """Marisette doesn't flinch and she doesn't laugh.

"Eight is eight. I can put twenty men at that pier before the sixth bell tomorrow. Crowbill can put forty, and he'd do it for what's in your purse, because he'd rather do it than be asked twice."

She lets that sit.

"And then I have twenty men against eight Dragon Knights in scale, on a deck, at night, and I lose eleven of them and it's still even money. And by dawn every one of them has a name and a mother on this island, and Hanzo di Teufel -- who is at this moment eating supper with the Governor's brother -- knows to the hour who came for his ship."

("2026-09-06T16:10:21", "scene", M+","+G+","+RU+","+TEMPLE,

("2026-09-06T16:22:30", "scene", NE+","+TEMPLE,
 "NERISSA'S HALF: the channel went THIN four minutes after noon, and Prince Emeric silenced her alarm in writing before the third peal.",
 """"Now I'll tell you mine, and then we'll be even.

"Yesterday, four minutes after noon, this channel went **wrong**. Not fouled -- I've had fouled, fouled is a dead ox and a week of prayers. This went *thin*. The Lady's presence in her own water went thin, the way a voice goes thin at a distance, in the space of about ten heartbeats." Her hands have closed. "I have served here since I was nineteen and it has never once done that.

"So I rang the tower. And by the third peal there was a boy from the Governor's household at my gate with a written instruction to *cease*, on the grounds that the city was welcoming a distinguished guest and the bells were causing alarm during a formal entry."

She turns round. "Written and sealed by **Prince Emeric**. Who is twenty-four years old, and well-meaning, and who has been told by three separate men on his council this fortnight that his uncle would like the Tourney to go smoothly."

"And you stopped."

"I stopped." Something flat and furious goes across her face. "Because I am the High Priestess of a temple that is paid for by this city's Guilds, and because I had *nothing*. A thin feeling in the water and no cause I could name in front of a magistrate. If I had rung on I would have been removed by Thursday and replaced by somebody who wouldn't ring at all."

She comes back and sits down on the step again, closer. "And now an old woman walks in at midnight and tells me there is a ship at the Forge Quarter pier that steams where it sits, that arrived five days ago, and that has a dead man bound into a living boy aboard it.

("2026-09-06T16:24:16", "decision", M+","+NE+","+TEMPLE,
 "Nerissa asks one question about the hair that nobody else thought to ask: is there a knot in it, or is it cut clean at both ends?",
 """Magda lays it all out on the low table by the lamp and takes it apart for her the way you'd show someone a bad joint of meat. The cloak, the tailor's tower, the ring, the letter, the eleven coins. And then the oiled silk.

"Five of these. Four still full. Hair, bound at one end with copper wire. And a bit of something brown that isn't wax. That one's empty. He used it." -- "On the courtesan." -- "Aye." -- "Whose hair is black." -- "Aye."

Nerissa picks up the first twist. She doesn't open it. She holds it, and her thumb moves once across the silk.

"So he came into this city carrying five women in his coat," she says. "And he spent one of them on a girl at Constantine's, and he had four left."

She opens it then, and lets the hair out into the lamplight, and looks at it a long moment. Then, in a voice that has gone completely level:

"Beneath the wire. Is there a knot in it, or is it cut clean at both ends?"

Magda turns it. The wire's at one end. The other end of the hank is blunt, square, all the strands the same length. "Cut clean."

"Then it was taken with shears, off a head, by somebody standing behind her." Nerissa lays it down very carefully. "It was not gathered off a comb or a pillow. **Somebody got close enough to my sister's daughter to put shears in her hair, and she did not scream, and she has not told me.**

"Her name is **Sana**. She's nineteen. And she has been at the temple school on Lost Isle for six weeks and I have not seen her in three."
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:06:49", "decision", G+","+M+","+TEMPLE,
 "\"What does Gardwen want to do?\" -- \"I want to go to that pier tonight. So I'm not to be trusted about this. I know that about myself.\"",

("2026-09-06T17:15:13", "scene", M+","+G+","+TEMPLE,
 "\"I'm pledged to you girl. Where you go, I go.\" Gardwen doesn't say anything. She takes Magda's wrist and holds it for three seconds and then goes and checks her knife.",
 """That's the whole of it. It's enough.

("2026-09-06T17:19:05", "scene", M+","+G+","+"myth-loc-ec677c07203d",
 "Corbie's at one in the morning, with a light burning over the door. \"We sent a boat at dusk, Mother -- didn't it come?\" Nothing came. And there is a light moving on Lost Isle.",
 """Magda limbers as she walks. Neck first -- it goes with a crack that makes one of the Swords glance round. Then the shoulders, then two slow swings of the staff at half-length in the colonnade, feeling where the joints are tonight, which is: not good, but adequate. She counts the sling bullets by touch in the pouch. **Eleven.** She'd have liked twenty.

Gardwen watches her do it and doesn't say anything, and then starts checking her own kit, which is thinner than hers.

Twenty minutes on black water with two Swords rowing. Nobody talks. Nerissa sits in the bow with the lamp shuttered and her hand trailing over the side in the water the whole way, which is not idleness -- you can see her listening to it.

The woman who opens the door is the mistress of the school and she has been crying. She sees Nerissa and her face does something terrible.

"We sent to you at *dusk*," she says. "We sent a boat at dusk, Mother -- didn't it come?"

Nerissa has gone very still on the step. "No," she says. "Nothing came."

"Sana's gone. Since yesterday morning. We've had every girl out looking and we've dragged the channel and I sent Bettan to the temple *myself*--"

And across the water, four hundred yards off, Lost Isle sits low and black and weed-choked with nothing on it at all. Except that there's a light moving on it. Not a lamp -- too low, and the colour's wrong. A dull red, close to the waterline, that doesn't swing the way a carried light swings.

("2026-09-06T17:21:55", "skill-roll", G+","+NE+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "Detect Evil across four hundred yards of open channel. Piety 46 against 44 -- she misses by two. \"I got about halfway across and it went out like a candle in a draught.\"",
 """She goes down on one knee at the water's edge and puts both hands flat in the channel, and says something under her breath that has the shape of a name in it. And you *feel* the room she makes -- the way the air goes when a door opens somewhere else in a house. Then it closes. Nothing comes.

She sits back on her heels, breathing like she ran here. "Too far. It's not the distance, it's -- the water's all *hers* here, and I'm not hers, and I was asking a favour in someone else's house."

Nerissa has been watching her the whole time with an expression Magda can't read at all.

"You reached," she says. It isn't a question. "From the bank. Across running water that isn't yours, at a rank you shouldn't manage."

"No." Nerissa is already unpinning her other sleeve. "You reached *at all*. Girl -- **you were asking a favour in someone else's house because you were standing on the doorstep shouting.**"

She steps down into the channel until she's shin-deep, and holds out her hand. "So come inside and ask properly. Take my hand and do it again, and this time the Lady will hear where it came from."

("2026-09-06T17:24:29", "skill-roll", G+","+NE+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "PLAYER FINDS THE MECHANIC: \"Could she use a passion to augment it?\" Love (Brother + Family) 80 -> +16. 87+16 = 103, Hard -> 69. Rolled 46. She's through.",
 """A woman who has spent ten years looking for a taken child, being asked to find a taken girl. That is squarely inside the passion, and Nerissa channelling it removes the problem that beat her the first time.

She takes Nerissa's hand and goes into the channel up to her knees, and the second time is not like the first. Her fingers lock on Nerissa's hard enough to hurt and her breath goes out of her all at once, and Nerissa stands there in the water and takes it without moving, the way you'd hold a rope.

Then Gardwen starts talking, fast, flat, describing as she goes:

"There's -- the whole island's *humming*. Underneath. Not evil, just old, there's a great deal of something old down under the weed and it doesn't care about us at all. Above that. On the stone. There's a *working*."

"""),

("2026-09-06T17:34:25", "skill-roll", M+","+G+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",

("2026-09-06T17:38:06", "skill-roll", M+","+G+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "\"Say what she calls my mother.\" Magda can't -- so she uses the eleven-page letter about a heron instead. Sana 54/60. She believes it.",
 """Gardwen calls up the stairwell, pitched to carry that far and no further: "**Sana.** Your aunt sent me. Nerissa sent me. She's stood in the water at the corner and she's got her mace and she is *extremely* angry."

"Aye. Stood in the channel at the corner with a mace in her belt and no robe on."

A sound that might be a laugh and is mostly not.
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:39:00", "scene", G+","+M+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "Sana comes down -- nineteen, barefoot, hair chopped ragged on the left side, looking about twelve. \"They didn't come for me. They came for the *place*.\"",
 """It takes a long time, because she has been folded into a gap between two floor-joists for a day and a half and her legs have stopped being reliable. Twice she stops and just breathes.

Gardwen goes up the half-stair to meet her and brings her the last of it, and she comes out into the weed-light barefoot in a school shift. Dark red hair. What's left of it.

She grips Gardwen's forearm and won't let go and talks in a rush, hoarse, too fast:

"There were three of them yesterday. Three. There's only been two since this morning -- the other one went off in the boat before dawn and hasn't come back--"

"Slow down, lass."

"You don't understand." She's shaking. "**They didn't come for me. They came for the *place*.** I only ran because I *saw* -- I came out to look at the ruin like everyone does and they were *already here*, and they had a girl from the school with them, and she was walking with them like she knew them."

She looks between them.

"Bettan. Her name's Bettan. She's fourteen. She's the one they sent to the temple last night with the message."
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:42:06", "decision", M+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "MAGDA'S QUESTION: \"How well do you know this girl? Did she change recently?\" And Sana, clever, makes herself stop shaking to answer it properly.",
 """"About a month ago.

"She was -- Bettan's a *baby*. Fourteen and homesick and cries at everything, and she'd got herself half-drowned in the misery of it, and none of us were kind enough about it. Then she went quiet for about a week. Properly quiet, wouldn't come down to meals, and Mistress Corliss had her in and we all thought she'd be sent home.

"And then she came back *cheerful*."

She looks up. "That's the bit. Not better -- *cheerful*. And she started being lovely to everyone. Girls she'd never spoken to. She sat with Ana Vell for a whole week and Ana Vell is *horrible*. We all said it was nice. Mistress Corliss said it was nice. Everyone was so pleased."

Then, and her voice drops: "**She stopped wearing her shawl. In *February*.** She'd sit in the window bay with the shutter open at night doing her letters and the rest of us are three to a bed with chilblains, and she'd say she was warm.

"And she started asking about people's families. All the time. Who's your mother, where's your house, have you got sisters. And we all told her, because she was being *nice*."

She looks at the ragged side of her own head.

"She did my hair. Three weeks ago. She said she could do the plait my aunt does and she stood behind me with the scissors and she did it *beautifully*, and I said thank you."
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:44:18", "scene", M+","+NE+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "Corvin and Ash find the punt fast (14/60). Two men sitting side by side in the dark, not talking, for twenty minutes. Nerissa: \"are waiting for something.\"",
 """"Found it, Mother. Not a boat -- a **punt**, flat, no keel, tied off in a doorway about sixty yards up. Corvin's sat on it. It's poled, not rowed. And it's the *only* one -- we went the length of the north side."

Which means the third man took the other boat before dawn and hasn't brought it back, and these two have been on this rock all day with one flat punt between them.

"And them?"

"Forty yards past it, in what's left of a big room -- half a roof on, no wall on the water side. There's a fire *in* there, laid on a slab, but it's not lit now. They've a lantern with a red slide. And Mother -- they've been *digging*. There's a heap of weed and muck pulled up out of the floor and stacked, and something under it they've uncovered. Stone. Cut stone with work on it.

"They're just sitting. Both of them, on the edge of the slab, side by side, not talking. Been like that since the light went out."

Gardwen has gone very still at *not talking*. "How long is that now?" -- "Near on twenty minutes."

Nerissa lifts the mace slightly. "Two men who have sat in the dark without speaking for twenty minutes are waiting for something."
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:46:03", "scene", M+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "Magda goes up the drowned street alone. Both men turn their heads at once -- \"not together like men who heard the same thing. *At once*, like two doors on one hinge.\"",
 """Sixty yards. The punt in its doorway with Corvin folded down beside it, who doesn't look up as she passes.

Half a roof, no wall on the water side, so you can see straight in from thirty feet: a stone floor above the waterline, a raised slab, and the heap of dragged-up weed and muck stacked against the standing wall. Where they've cleared it there's cut stone showing -- deep-carved, and the carving goes on down under the water at the edge, and it is a great deal older than anything else on this island.

The red-slide lantern sits on the slab, shut. And the two of them are sitting side by side on the edge of it, facing the water, facing *her*, in the dark.

She is twenty feet away before either moves.

Then both of them turn their heads at once. Not together like men who heard the same thing -- *at once*, the same speed, the same distance, like two doors on one hinge.

Neither stands.

One of them -- sandy, thirties, a boatman's forearms -- says in an entirely ordinary voice: "You're not her."

And the other one, without any pause at all, in the same voice, finishes it: "--she was meant to bring the girl."
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:49:07", "combat", M+","+"myth-char-f1333241e707",
 "\"No girl, just little old me. All alone surrounded by big scary warriors\" -- and the stone goes out on the last word. 56/128, right arm, serious. He doesn't look at it.",
 """It takes the sandy one high on the right arm, on the outside, and you *hear* the bone go from twenty feet.

The arm drops. It doesn't swing -- it just stops being part of him and hangs.

He doesn't make a sound. He doesn't look at it. He doesn't even look at *her*.

Both of them stand up at the same moment, the same speed, like the slab tipped them.

And the sandy one says, conversationally, with his arm hanging off him: "That's going to make the poling difficult."

And the other one finishes: "--we'll manage."

They come off the slab into the water together. The billhook comes up off the wall into the second one's hands.
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:51:39", "combat", M+","+"myth-char-f1333241e707"+","+"myth-char-d33fde43d59d",
 "Parry and disarm on the differential, then everything into the sandy one's already-broken arm. Bone through the sleeve. Neither of them has bled a drop.",
 """The billhook comes in at her shins and she doesn't step back -- she drops the staff-end into its path and rolls her wrists, and the hooked head skids off the shaft and goes *past*, and while his weight is still following it she carries the same motion up and round and takes the haft out of his hands with the top third of the staff. It goes into the black water. He watches it go.

Then she pivots off the back foot and puts everything into the sandy one. Aiming for the same arm. She gets it.

It's already broken high up and this takes it below the elbow, and there is a wet crack and the whole limb comes apart at two places at once, and what's hanging off his shoulder now is not a limb. Bone through the sleeve. Six inches of it.

He goes back a step from the force of it. Only one. Then he straightens up.

He looks at the ruin of his own arm -- and this time he *does* look at it, curiously, turning slightly to see it better, the way you'd inspect a torn coat.

And the other one, standing empty-handed in the water beside him, says in that same flat conversational voice: "That's the arm gone, then."

"Mm," says the sandy one.

**Neither of them has bled a drop.**
"""),

("2026-09-06T17:59:41", "combat", G+","+"myth-char-f1333241e707",
 "Gardwen's Hold Person takes -- and it should not. \"There shouldn't be enough person in him to grip.\"",
 """She doesn't shout it. She puts one hand out flat toward him and says three words in the old tongue, and the water between them goes still in a ring.

("2026-09-06T18:03:08", "combat", M+","+"myth-char-d33fde43d59d"+","+RU,
 "The billhook-man takes hold of Magda's forearm and will not let go. Ruhi trips him and both of them go under. He isn't struggling. He doesn't need to breathe and he has all night.",
 """He goes *through* the parry and takes hold. One hand closes on the staff. The other closes on her left forearm above the wrist, and it is like being gripped by a piece of machinery -- no squeeze, no threat, just a closing to a fixed position and then no further movement at all.

She has felt a great many hands in seventy years and none of them were this cold through wet wool.

He doesn't pull. He doesn't twist. He turns his head and calls, conversationally, to nobody in particular: "I've got this one." And behind her, frozen mid-step with his arm hanging in two pieces, Sandy says quite clearly: "--good."

Ruhi goes low, takes the leg at the back of the knee, and *pulls* -- forty stone of wolf against a man standing in three feet of water with both hands committed to holding an old woman.

He goes. And because he will not let go, she goes with him.

Under there it's silent, and cold, and absolutely black. He is not struggling. He is not trying to hold her down. He is simply lying on the bottom of a drowned street holding on, waiting, because he does not need to breathe and he has all night.

Her face is about eight inches under.

Gardwen's **Command** opens the hand -- all four fingers at once, like a catch releasing -- and Magda comes up off the bottom into air and lamplight coughing canal.

He sits up in the water beside her with his hands open in his lap, palms turned upward, and looks at them. "That wasn't me," he says, with what might almost be interest.
"""),

("2026-09-06T18:10:18", "combat", M+","+"myth-char-d33fde43d59d"+","+NE,
 "THE KILLING THAT SHOULD NOT HAVE HAPPENED. He had stopped, put his hands down and stepped aside to show Nerissa the stone. Magda takes his head off anyway.",
 """He gets up, doesn't come at her, and wades unhurried toward the slab with his hands still open at his sides. Nerissa is between him and it, and she doesn't move, and neither does he.

They look at each other across four feet of black water.

Then he says: "You're the Lady's, aren't you." -- "I am." -- "Good," he says. "She'll want to see this."

And he steps sideways, out of her path, and gestures with an open hand at the cut stone they've spent a day digging out of the weed.

**Berserker, Easy (85 -> 128), no defence. 75. Eight damage. Head: -4 of 5. Serious.**

She comes out of the water and doesn't say anything, and plants her back foot in the mud and swings the way you'd swing at a fence post that had offended you. Six feet of ash across the temple. Nothing between it and the bone.

His head goes sideways past where a head goes. He drops where he stands, straight down, no stagger. The body doesn't float.

Nerissa doesn't move. She's still standing exactly where she was, mace up, four feet away, with her mouth slightly open. She lowers the mace slowly.

"He had stopped," she says. Not accusing. Just stating it, like a woman reading a figure back to check she has it right. "**He had stopped, and he was showing me the stone.**"
"""),

("2026-09-06T18:15:02", "skill-roll", M+","+NE+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "\"I'm a berserker. That means I fight until someone convinces me to stop.\" Nerissa's Insight: 4 against 80. CRITICAL. She reads Magda completely -- and gives her a reason instead of an order.",
 """Whatever she was going to say next, she doesn't say. She changes her footing -- stops standing like a woman about to remonstrate and starts standing like a woman at the side of a horse that's still running.

"Ah," she says. Very quietly. "*Ah.* You're not deciding anything, are you."

She lowers the mace all the way and lets it hang.

"I've seen this twice. Once in a man at the Shoals after a fire, and once in my own father." She keeps her voice completely even -- not soothing, not raised, the pace of someone reading a list. "**You're not cruel. You've simply not been given a reason to stop yet, and nobody in this water has thought to give you one, they've only told you to.**"

She moves round until she's in front of her rather than beside her, slowly, so she can see her do it.

"So. Here's the reason.

"**Sana is in a boat forty yards behind us**, nineteen years old, with her hair cut off, watching. That girl has spent a day and a half in a hole in the dark being brave, and what she can see from there is an old woman breaking a man who can't move.

"That's it. That's the whole reason. Not the man -- he's nothing to me and I'd hang him tomorrow. **Her.**"

She holds out one open hand. Not to take the staff. Just open.

Magda doesn't answer and doesn't lower the staff. She just stops. Water running off her. Breathing like a bellows. Everything in her face still exactly where it was -- and standing entirely still in the middle of it, which is not the same as being calm, and everyone there knows the difference.
"""),

("2026-09-06T18:22:30", "scene", M+","+"myth-char-f1333241e707",
 "Sandy comes back to life mid-step, trussed, and smiles for the first time all night: \"You're the one who did the boy in the canal. The face like a spade. He described you before he went.\"",
 """Corvin and Ash work fast and say nothing. Elbows first, then the wrists behind, then a running loop from the wrists to the ankles so he can shuffle and not stride. They do it around the ruined arm rather than through it, which is more care than Magda would have taken.

Gardwen counts down under her breath -- "*--four, three--*" -- and on two the ring of stillness lets go and Sandy comes back to life mid-step and finds himself trussed and sitting. He doesn't fight it. He looks down at the rope with mild interest and settles.

Then he looks up, finds Magda, and smiles.

"You're the one who did the boy in the canal," he says. "The face like a spade. He described you before he went."

*He described you.* The one who left before dawn in the other boat. The one who hasn't come back.
"""),

("2026-09-06T18:35:53", "skill-roll", NE+","+"myth-loc-69e2657b23c6",
 "THE STAIR. Nerissa's Lore (Water spirits) 59/80 -- she has it. Lore (Theology) 96/88 -- she doesn't. \"It's a door. Not for people. For the drowned.\"",
 """She can tell you exactly what it *does*. She cannot tell you what it *means*, and you watch that bother her more than the corpse in the water.

"It's a door." She traces the carving with two fingers, following it down, and her hand goes under the surface and keeps going.

"Not for people. For the drowned. There are -- there are old stories about the Northern Isles going under. Not one flood, a slow one, over generations, and everything in them that died went down with the streets. And whoever cut this cut it so that what stayed in the water had somewhere to *go*. A way out. **You lay them to rest through a thing like this.**"

She looks up, and there's something urgent in it. "It isn't a Lady-stone. It's older than her presence in this channel and it isn't in any doctrine I've read in forty years, and I could not tell you who cut it or to what."

Then she stands, and holds the lamp out over the cleared patch. And you see that it isn't a slab at all.

It's the top of a **stair**. Four steps showing, cut into the same worked stone, going down at an angle and disappearing into black water that does not reflect the lamp the way the rest of the channel does. Weed hangs off the edges where they've hacked it away. The steps are *swept* -- there's no silt on them, and there should be a foot of it.

Something has been using them.

Behind them, roped and sitting in the shallows, Sandy says pleasantly: "That's what he went to fetch the boat for. You'd best hurry -- he's been gone since before dawn, and he'll not be coming back alone."
"""),

("2026-09-06T19:00:59", "decision", M+","+NE,
 "\"They're raising the drowned, just like our two chatty friends here.\" Nerissa: \"They're not raising them, Magda. They're *shopping*.\"",
 """"They don't bleed. They don't breathe. Ruhi had that one under for a good half-minute and it did nothing to him. They talk like one man with two mouths. And her *Hold Person* took. Gardwen said it shouldn't. There's enough person left in him to grip and not enough to bleed."

"And there is a door for the drowned dead under this island," Nerissa says slowly, "which they have been digging out for a day."

She looks back at the swept stair going down into water that doesn't hold the lamplight.

"They're not raising them, Magda. **They're *shopping*.**"
"""),

("2026-09-06T19:04:32", "scene", M+","+"myth-char-f1333241e707",
 "ELLICK SARN. \"They came to me in the winter... And then on the fourth time he said, would I like to not be cold any more.\"",
 """He has to think about his own name. That's the unsettling part.

"Ellick," he says at last. "Ellick Sarn. That's -- yes. That's right, I'm fairly sure. I poled the Forge Quarter run. Timber mostly, sometimes charcoal, and a woman called Tam who I think was--" He stops. Frowns very slightly at the sky. "There was something about Tam. It's gone."

"They came to me in the winter. Not the young lord -- the *quiet* one, him that's gone for the boat. He asked did I know the Northern Isles and I said better than any man breathing, which was true, and he paid me eleven marks to take him out to the drowned streets four times and say nothing. I did say nothing. I want that noted. I kept my end.

"And then on the fourth time he said, would I like to not be cold any more."

He says it perfectly evenly.

"I've been cold on that water for thirty-one years, missus. Every winter. Hands gone the colour of the sky. And he said it like he was offering me a coat." His head tips a little. "And I said yes. **That's the part everyone wants to skip past. Nobody did anything to me that I didn't stand still for.**"

Sana has both hands over her mouth. "What went in you?"

"Something out of the stairs. It's not unkind. It doesn't want anything much. It likes the digging. It's got a lot more of me than it had at Candlemas. That's the trade -- it warms you and it *wears* you, and you don't notice the wearing because the part that would notice is the part it's wearing."

Then, conversationally: "You'll be wanting to know about the one on the ship. That's a different thing entirely. That one's *furnished*."
"""),

("2026-09-06T19:04:59", "decision", M+","+"myth-char-f1333241e707",
 "\"What are you fuckers up to?\" -- the door is for taking something OUT. \"You can't keep a thing in a boy for ever.\" And Sana: \"The girls with the red hair aren't for the demon. They're spares.\"",
 """"The quiet one wants the door open. That's the whole of the digging. Four days, and it wants to be open before the Tourney and not after -- he was very hard about that. There's a tide thing in it. He said something about the water being *thin* on the day and it having to be while it's thin."

Nerissa's head comes round. "He said *thin*?" -- "His word."

"And the door's for taking something *out*. That's the bit I did understand, because I asked him -- I said is this for putting things in, like you did with me, and he laughed. Only time I saw him laugh. He said no, Ellick, that's the easy way and any fool with a knife can do that. He said the hard thing is getting one *out* whole and putting it somewhere better.

"Because you can't keep a thing in a boy for ever. He said that too. They wear through. He said the one they've got has nearly used up what it was put in."

He turns his head and looks straight at Gardwen for the first time.

"**That's why they came here. It's not a rescue they're worried about, love. It's a *removal*. He's outgrown the boy and they've somewhere better to put him.**"

And Sana, very quietly, from the far thwart:

"...The girls with the red hair aren't for the demon. **They're spares.**"
"""),

("2026-09-06T19:07:36", "decision", M+","+G+","+"myth-char-a46cf24af084",
 "THE NAME. \"That one *fights*.\" Two voices out of one throat, arguing for hours. \"You bleed a man to keep him from arguing.\" Thuban. Thuban Eta.",
 """"Mine's *content*, see. It got a boatman who was cold and it's warm now and it likes lifting stone. There's no fight in it. That's why I'm still able to sit here and talk to you about Tam and nearly remember her."

He nods north-west, toward where the black hull sits steaming at its pier.

"That one *fights*."

Ash has stopped rowing. Nobody tells him to start.

"I was aboard twice, carrying. You can hear it through the deck. Not screaming -- worse than that, it's *arguing*. Goes on for hours. Two voices out of one throat having a row, and one of them's a boy and one of them isn't, and the one that isn't sounds like a man who's been told to do something he thinks is dishonourable." He shakes his head slowly. "That's what the morning cut's for. It's not just the wear. It's to keep it *tired*. **You bleed a man to keep him from arguing.**

"They've a name for it. Old-sounding. The quiet one says it like a title, not a name." He works his jaw. "Thoo-- *Thuban*. Thuban something. Eta, maybe. He's a knight out of the dragon wars and he's been in one thing or another for a very long while, and he doesn't want to be, and he never has."

He looks around the boat at all of them.

"You keep saying *rescue the boy*. I'd think about that. **There's two in there, and only one of them's been asking to get out.**"
"""),

("2026-09-06T19:11:16", "decision", M+","+NE+","+G,
 "\"That's the dead knight. That's Hel's command.\" Nerissa: \"She showed you the *passenger*. It is not a rescue. It's a *funeral*.\"",
 """Nobody rows. The boat drifts.

Nerissa says it first, slowly, the way you'd read something off a wall. "Eleven nights. A knight in dragon-scale who is already dead and does not know it." She turns to look at her. "And *lay the dragon warrior to rest*. Not the boy. She never once showed you the boy."

"No."

"She showed you the **passenger**." Nerissa's hand has gone to her breast. "Magda -- your goddess has been telling you the answer since before you left home and none of us could hear it because we were all looking at the child."

Gardwen has gone absolutely still in the bow. "Say the rest of it," she says. "Say it out loud so I've heard it."

Nerissa does.

"If Thuban Eta is laid to rest, he leaves. And whatever is left in that body is your brother, and only your brother." A pause. "**It is not a rescue. It's a *funeral*. And the boy walks out of it because the funeral wasn't for him.**"

Ellick, helpfully, into the silence: "That's what the door's for, mind. Same door. Only the quiet one wants him lifted *out and moved*, and you want him lifted out and let *go*. You'll be wanting the same night and the same stair as him, then. And the same thin water."
"""),

("2026-09-06T19:23:25", "scene", M+","+NE+","+G,
 "\"What are you talking about? Makes no sense to me.\" Nerissa stops using her temple voice and explains it on three fingers.",
 """"Right. Plainly.

"There is a dead man stuffed inside Gardwen's brother. Has been for years. He's the thing that makes the boy a champion -- he's the swordsman, not the child.

"He's worn the boy out. You can't keep meat in the same barrel for ever, it goes. So the Baron needs him **out** and into something fresher before he ruins the one he's got.

"There's exactly one way to get a dead man out of a living body whole. That stair on Lost Isle. It's a door. That's what those two have been digging for four days."

She drops her hand.

"So the Baron's man opens the door, takes the knight *out* of your girl's brother, and shifts him into a new body he's picked out. Probably one of the four girls whose hair was in that boy's coat. That's a **removal**, and it's the day after tomorrow because that's when the water goes thin enough to do it.

"Now. Your goddess wants the same door, the same night, the same knight -- and she wants him taken out and *put in the ground* instead of moved house.

"**It's the same job, Magda. Right up until the last moment, it's the *identical* job.** Get the dead man out. The only difference is what happens to him in the second after that, and whether there's a new girl standing there waiting to be filled."

Gardwen, from the bow, without turning round: "And either way my brother comes out of it empty. Alive, and empty, and his own."

Ellick nods along, agreeable as anything. "Told you it was a funeral."
"""),

("2026-09-06T20:24:19", "skill-roll", NE,
 "\"Do we hold the door, or break it?\" Nerissa consults the Lady. Lore (Theology) 38/88 -- she gets an answer, and it isn't the one she wanted. \"She says the door isn't hers.\"",
 """She puts both hands over the side into the channel and stops moving for a long moment, and the water round the boat goes glassy in a way that has nothing to do with the wind.

Then she takes her hands out and looks at them.

"She says the door isn't hers."

"Meaning?"

"Meaning she won't tell me to break it, and she won't tell me to hold it." Nerissa's voice is tight. "It was cut before her. It's not in her gift. What she *will* say -- is that the water goes thin tomorrow whether we like it or not, and that a thing left in the wrong place too long spoils what's around it. Which is not an instruction. **That is a woman telling me the milk's turning and leaving me to deal with it.**"

She snorts, and it's very like Magda's snort.

"Fine. Then we do it your way, and I'll answer for it later."
"""),

("2026-09-06T20:24:41", "decision", M+","+NE+","+"myth-char-eb79260a2a9b",
 "MAGDA'S BEST IDEA OF THE NIGHT: \"Maybe you can ask the prince if he wouldn't mind.\" Nerissa: \"I have been so angry with that boy for a day and a half that it did not once occur to me to *use* him.\"",
 """She stops with one foot on the water-stair.

"...Say that again."

"Ask the prince. He's the one signed the paper. Ask him to unsign it."

She comes back down the step.

"Magda, I have been so angry with that boy for a day and a half that it did not once occur to me to *use* him." She says it like a woman finding a tool she'd thrown across the room. "And he's the only person in Purewater who can make any of this **lawful**.

"With a Governor's warrant, holding Lost Isle isn't twenty armed men on a rock -- it's the *Watch* posting a cordon, and nobody has to explain themselves. And going aboard that ship isn't a raid, it's a **search**, and eight Dragon Knights at a pier cannot lawfully refuse it in a treaty port without their master forfeiting the Tourney entry on the spot."

Gardwen: "And if he says no?"

"Then he's told the Baron by noon and we've lost surprise and the day. That's the wager. He's twenty-four, he's frightened of his council, and he signed that instruction because three grown men told him it was the polite thing to do. He is not wicked. "So you're not asking me to rob a lord. You're asking me to *humiliate* one, and put my name on it, in exchange for goods I'd have to fence quietly for a year."

Then he tells her which version of her two days is running fastest, and it ends: "And the Baron's entered a champion that not one soul in Purewater has been allowed to look at. That last part's new. That went out this morning and it's *everywhere*, and it's the bit the Guildmasters are chewing on."

His eyes come up. "So here's my question, and I want the true answer, because I'm not putting forty men on a pier for a story. **What's wrong with him?** Nobody hides a swordsman. You hide a thing that would *lose you everything* if it were seen."
"""),

("2026-09-07T01:17:34", "decision", M+","+CB+","+G,
 "\"It's not a humiliation. It's a rescue.\" And Crowbill goes to the window and tells her the one rule of his that isn't about money.",
 """"The champion's the ghost of a fallen general from a thousand years ago contained in the body of this woman's nineteen year old brother. I serve Hel and she wants the ledger set right and the ghost released. That clear enough of a read for you?"

"Seventeen," Gardwen says quietly.

Crowbill looks at her, and then back at Magda, and doesn't say anything for a while. Then: "A boy with a dead general in him." -- "Aye." -- "Being kept on a ship for it." -- "Bled every morning to keep him quiet. There's a laundress on that pier who's been boiling the sheets for five days and can tell you the shape of the cut."

He stands. He goes to the window, which looks at a wall, and stands there with his hands behind his back.

"I've a rule," he says to the wall. "I've a few. Most of them are about money and one of them isn't, and the one that isn't is why I've still got a city to work in.

"**Children aren't stock. You don't sell them, you don't use them, and you don't let anyone do it on my water and call it business.**" He turns round. "Your Marisette knows that rule. It's why we get on."

"So. I'd have done it for the cargo anyway. Now I'll do it *properly*, which is different, and here are my terms -- and they're not money.

"**One.** Everything on that ship that isn't the boy is mine, and nobody counts it but me.
"**Two.** My name is nowhere. Tonight was *thieves*, and this city has plenty.
"**Three** -- and this is the one I care about." He puts one finger on the desk. "When it's done, the **High Priestess of the Lake Lady** stands up and says publicly that the canal folk kept her water clean. Not me. Not names. *The canal folk.* Because I have four hundred people who get moved on and blamed and dredged out of the channel, and one sentence from that woman is worth more to them than a Baron's whole hold.

"Can you get me that?"
"""),

("2026-09-07T01:21:08", "decision", M+","+CB+","+MOUTH,
 "\"You're the river men, I'm just a pig farmer.\" TAKE HER OFF THE PIER. Crowbill's face becomes interested for the first time: \"Nobody watches a wake.\"",
 """"She has to leave to sail. Once she's off that pier she's not got four men at the bollards and four at a ramp -- she's just a hull in the dark with a channel round her, and the channel's yours."

"It is." He's already pulling a scrap of paper over. "And she cannot get out to sea without going through the **Mouth**, and the Mouth on the ebb is a mile of slow water with the harbour lights behind it, and I have men who have been going up the sides of anchored hulls in that stretch since they were nine years old." He's drawing. "You don't need forty. You need *twelve*, in six punts with no lights, and you take her from three sides at once while she's making way and everyone aboard is looking forward.

Then he stops drawing. "One problem, and it's yours to solve, not mine."

I've had a man put his hand in that water off the stern two days ago on a dare and he's still got no feeling in three fingers.

"My people go up the outside of hulls. They cannot climb *that* one -- not at the waterline, and that's where you have to start.

"""),

("2026-09-07T01:24:00", "decision", G+","+M+","+CB+","+RV,

("2026-09-07T01:57:01", "scene", M+","+RV+","+SIREN,

 """"There are people living in the deep channels of this city who were here before the causeway. Not many. They keep out of the way and they mind their own business and their whole lives are *water that behaves*. And for five days there has been a hot wound in the eastern channel that pushes ahead of the tide, and every one of them has had to move -- old, young, sick -- and two haven't managed it."

She says the last part very flatly. The canal outside the window has gone glassy in a strip about four feet wide.

("2026-09-07T01:58:40", "decision", M+","+RV+","+SIREN,
 "THE ARRANGEMENT: two dead men laid down properly, for one cold ship. \"There isn't a version of this where a boatman walks home to his supper.\"",
 """"Two." Ravella doesn't move. "Where." -- "One's dead. I put an axe through his head on Lost Isle last night. The other's roped in a cellar under the Lake Lady's temple with two Swords on the door, and he talks. Boatman. Ellick Sarn."

Something passes over her face at the name and she doesn't explain it. "Ellick. He poled the Forge Quarter run. He carried for us twice."

She's quiet a moment. "Then you already have both of them and you didn't know what you had. Here is the arrangement, and I'll speak for the Court because they'll agree and because there isn't time to go down and ask.

"That's the whole price. Not the ship, not the Baron, not your boy -- those are your business and the Court doesn't care about a dead general or a barony. The two you've got are *ours*, and they need to go back through that threshold and be let go properly, and until they are they're neither ours nor dead nor alive, and that is an obscenity."

She looks at her very directly. "You should understand what you're agreeing to. The thing in Ellick Sarn came off our threshold and it goes back to it. What's left of Ellick is -- *thin*. **There isn't a version of this where a boatman walks home to his supper.** He said yes to a warm coat in a cold winter and he has been paying for it ever since, and the kindest end available to him is the right one.

"You'd be taking him to that stair and standing there while it's done." She turns her cup again. "And I understand that's your trade."

Then, briskly: "Do that, and I will come out to the Mouth myself tonight and put my hands on that hull and make it cold enough to climb. For as long as you need, not four minutes. And I will bring people who can be in the water beside it while it happens, which your Crowbill's boys cannot.

"Two dead men, laid down properly, for one cold ship. Do we have an arrangement?"

"Don't know where the second one is. But sure. I'll do what I can."

She takes her hand anyway. "You don't need to know where he is. He went into a drowned street off Lost Isle with an axe wound in his head and did not float. He's in our water. We'll have him on that threshold by dark and you won't have to look for him -- **you'll have to *stand* there, which is the part that matters.**

"And Magda -- when you're standing over those two tonight, say it out loud. Whatever your goddess's words are. The Court will be listening from underneath and they will want to hear that somebody up here said it."
"""),

("2026-09-07T02:09:10", "decision", M+","+HE+","+G,

("2026-09-07T02:18:28", "decision", M+","+HE+","+G,

("2026-09-07T17:05:08", "decision", M+","+HE+","+MOUTH+","+LOST,
 "THE SPLIT: two things, two places, not at the same time. Magda picks the Mouth. \"Get the boy off that ship *breathing*. I can work with almost anything else.\"",
 """The DragonBarge is holding to the ebb. Blau has failed to find her a third time -- three days he's had the city's ear open and this city has told him nothing whatsoever. Thorne's *"never seen her,"* a fishmonger, forty people in a working yard, a customs man who wrote *dog* on his tally-board.

("2026-09-07T18:04:20", "combat", M+","+RV+","+MOUTH,
 "Ravella goes over the side and forty feet of hissing hull just STOPS, like a candle pinched out. 36/75. And 22 on the second roll -- somebody aboard feels it done.",
 """"When I go in, that water will kill anyone who isn't mine for about a minute while it turns. After that it's cold and it's climbable and I can hold it as long as I'm conscious. So say when, and be sure. Because I only get to do this once tonight."

The water goes first. You don't see her do it. What you see is the white line along that hull *stop* -- forty feet of hissing steam just ceasing, mid-length, like a candle pinched out, and the dead-water slick behind it going dark and ordinary and cold.

Six punts move at once. Grapnels go up in sacking and land with a sound like a fist in a pillow. Canal men are on the lines before the hooks have set, going up the side of a moving ship barefoot with knives in their teeth, and it is the most casually competent thing Magda has ever watched anybody do.

But a ship that has hissed for five days and suddenly *doesn't* is a ship that has changed its noise -- and there's a man aft who has lived beside that sound long enough to notice its absence.

A voice on the quarterdeck. Not a shout. A question. Then a shout. Then a bell.
"""),

("2026-09-07T18:05:45", "combat", M+","+MOUTH,
 "\"Shoot anyone I see on deck with my sling.\" She's not going up that hull and she knows it. First stone misses (69/57). Second is a 1 -- CRITICAL, under the raised arm, and the body blocks the rail.",
 """The first one leans out over the side with a knife, going for the grapnel lines -- which will drop three men into cold water and the ebb. The stone goes past his head close enough that he flinches back, which buys the line about three seconds and no more.

("2026-09-07T18:08:15", "combat", M+","+BL+","+MOUTH,

("2026-09-07T18:31:35", "combat", M+","+BL+","+MOUTH,

("2026-09-07T18:34:53", "combat", M+","+BL+","+MOUTH,

("2026-09-07T18:40:10", "scene", M+","+CA+","+TB+","+MOUTH,
 "THE CABIN. Chalk that is kept and redrawn every day. A cot bolted down, stripped to the canvas. And a wound that has been made and remade in the same place four hundred times.",
 """Small. Low. Lamp-lit, and hot -- hotter than the deck, hot the way a byre is hot, and the air in it is *wrong*: scorched hair and something sweetish, the exact smell that came out of Emmeralda's room on the Pearl.

("2026-09-07T18:42:27", "skill-roll", M+","+TB+","+MOUTH,

("2026-09-07T18:46:00", "combat", M+","+MOUTH,

("2026-09-07T19:11:00", "decision", M+","+HE+","+NE+","+LOST,

("2026-09-07T19:18:15", "skill-roll", M+","+LOST,
 "\"How would we honour a mighty warrior, murdered by cowards?\" Customs 26/48. It comes back not as instructions but as smells -- and then she hits the thing at the bottom of it.",
 """Woodsmoke and wet wool and somebody's aunt weeping professionally.

**You put his weapons back in his hands.** A man goes out armed. Whatever was taken off him when he died is given back, and if you haven't got it you give him yours, and that's better anyway.

**You say the name.** Out loud, first, before anything, so everyone standing there has to hear it.

**Then you tell the tale.** Not a prayer -- a *telling*. Who he was, what he did, and how he died, said in front of witnesses, in the open, at full volume.

**You settle the debt.** If a man was murdered, somebody stands up and says so, and names it, and the wrong is spoken into the air where everyone can hear it. Nobody goes into the ground with an unpaid killing on him.

**Then fire.** Or water, for a drowned man. You give him back to whatever took him, on purpose this time, with people watching.

**And you feast, and you brawl, and you get disgracefully drunk**, because a death that nobody celebrates is a death that didn't count.

**Valhalla isn't his.** That's for the battle-dead. Thuban Eta went over a gunwale in the dark with his hands tied by his own people. He was *cheated* of the death that buys that hall, and he has been paying for their crime with his afterlife for a thousand years.

Task 1 is done and committed. Task 2 is blocked, and it's a real block rather than something I can work around.

**The journal.** I read the whole play spine out of the session log — lines 960–9880 of the transcript, all 229 of your prompts and every GM response — and pulled 184 beat-level events back out of it. They're logged at their real play timestamps, so they interleave with the 13 chapter summaries in true order instead of piling up at the end. I added `--at` to [log-event](skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py) to make that possible.

Journal narrative went from ~4,000 words to ~40,000. 203 events. Consistency clean, 67 tests pass, package re-exported.

The disposal argument is now three separate events rather than nine words: Constantine's two ways with the ring; then *"never found is harder than it sounds in a city that dredges itself… in six or seven days the gas brings him up with the weights still on him, and then it isn't a drowning any more — it's a murder, and the Watch works murders"*, the guild-furnace-and-blackmail-for-life option against the deep channel on a ninety-minute ebb; and then the pigs, and Constantine admitting *"it's better,"* and hating it.

Other things the summaries had lost entirely:

- You watched Santo go up the stairs and chose to withdraw — *"not my business"*
- Asking your own Swim skill (27), ruling yourself out, and then asking about Ila's
- The joke about blood that dies in the wash-house steam — Influence 54 against 27
- Nerissa's Insight critical, a 4 against 80: *"You're not deciding anything, are you"*
- Thorne on why he sells stories and not lies, and the craft of letting the stone come out of nowhere
- Crowbill going to the window: children aren't stock
- Ravella correcting the litany — *you said take them; she never comes and fetches*
- Thuban refusing to be beaten out of a child
- The beheading, and Nerissa: *"That isn't purity, Magda. That's arithmetic"*
- You asking Ravella what **she** wanted done with the ship, and *"Nobody's asked me that"*
- Taking the vestment off before you answered Conall

The log is copied to [session-logs/](../purewater-campaign-v2/session-logs/) with the extraction scripts and a README explaining what was rebuilt and why.

**The blocker.** Your Sanctuary/Zorastor draft is gone. It was a PDF attachment in the message before the context compaction, and Claude Code doesn't persist attachment text to the session log — I checked the `attachment` records, and only file *reads* survive, not pastes. The compaction summary kept the character names (Myrtis, Lythande, Hakiem, the Vulgar Unicorn, Jubal, Moriata) and nothing of the prose. It isn't in Downloads, Documents, Desktop, or either repo.

I can't derive a style card from a document I can't see, and guessing would waste the whole novel. Re-attach it, or give me a path and I'll read it off disk — then I'll write the style card and build v2 side-by-side with the Hemingway version.
