# Purewater — rewriting the scenario

## Context

A seam opened in play. The campaign had **the champion on the sand at noon** and, separately,
**an extraction that could only happen at noon on a drowned island** — the same hour, four miles
apart. The player caught it. Half of that collision is mine: the Lost Isle threshold, the thin
water and the "removal" were never authored. They emerged in the previous playthrough and I
carried them across into this one as established fact, welded onto the authored spine without
checking the join.

The author's actual design, recovered:

> The champion **wins** the Single Combat. The prize is a private audience with the Prince. In
> that room the Baron possesses **Prince Emeric**. The boy genuinely fights — and fights
> brilliantly, because there is a dragon-knight in him — hidden behind harness and helm the
> whole way. **Gardwen sees him without the mask** at the presentation of entrants, the day
> before the Tourney.

Plus a systems change: the Baron's demonology should run on **rules**, not on plot. He is a
magician of the existing Imperative Magic framework with a small school of bespoke spells for
speaking to and binding spirits — unique to him and cultists like him. **Gardwen holds a
related woodland subset**, gained when the old ways found her in the ruined grove. That gives
the party a mechanical counter instead of a GM ruling.

Intended outcome: one coherent scenario, expressed in spells and beats the engine can run, with
the Lost Isle material already played kept and re-purposed rather than discarded.

---

## 1. The binding spells

The rules graph is the Mythras **Imperative** SRD — 101 pieces, no Animism, no spirit combat. We
are not porting full Mythras. We add a small school to the framework that already exists
(`magic/casting`: Magic skill POW+CHA, MP = POW, all Intensity 1, traits *Instant / Concentration
/ Ranged / Touch / Resist X*).

New pieces in `skills/mythras-gm/rules/magic/`, following `spell-find.md` verbatim for
frontmatter shape, faceted `magic-system: ["demonology"]` or `["woodland"]` so
`query-rules --facet magic-system=demonology` retrieves the set.

| Spell | Traits | School |
|---|---|---|
| **Spirit Sight** | Concentration | both |
| **Speak with the Bound** | Concentration, Touch | both — reaches the passenger past the host |
| **Open the Channel** | Touch, Resist Endurance | demonology — the barbed cut; prepares a living vessel |
| **Seat the Bound** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — needs an open channel *and* a drawn seat |
| **Reinforce the Seat** | Touch | demonology — the morning rite; keeps the passenger tired |
| **Anchor** | Touch | demonology — ties a spirit to an object |
| **Draw Forth** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — extraction |
| **Unseat** | Concentration, Touch | **woodland — the counter.** Breaks a seat with no new vessel |
| **Sanctuary** | Concentration | woodland — refuse a spirit entry |

This restates the authored three-part binding as actual castings: **Anchor** (bones),
**Anchor** (locket), **Reinforce the Seat** (daily). Losing the locket really does make the daily
rite harder, because it is one of two anchors rather than a plot assertion.

**Unseat is the party's route** and the reason Gardwen matters at the climax.

Add to `rules/magic.md` under the SRD spell list; add the files; the SessionStart hook reloads.

## 2. Scenario artefacts

- **`lore/gm-secret/gm-secrets-the-possession-scheme.md`** — rewrite. Cailan is the *jar* and the
  proof of concept; **Emeric is the destination**; the mechanism is the old rite of presentation,
  not a threshold. Express the binding in the spells above.
- **`lore/daily-life/the-lake-lady-s-tourney.md`** — Single Combat champion is presented **alone
  and unarmed** to the Crown's representative behind a closed door, by a form older than the
  Governor's office. Add the **presentation of entrants** on `d-1`.
- **`agendas/field-the-champion-and-take-the-city.md`** — the goal is the *room*, not civic
  standing. Pressure points become: the locket, the bones, Thuban's reluctance, and now the
  bracket.
- **New beat — "The presentation of the entrants"**, `d-1/day`, at the Governor's enclosure.
  The champion appears in harness. **This is the unmasking window.** `onscreen_if`: any PC in the
  enclosure or on the competitors' ground.
- **`beats/the-champion-takes-the-sand.md`** — he fights, masked, and **wins**.
- **New beat — "The private audience"**, `d0/day`, immediately after the final.
- **`beats/nus-lifts-the-binding-locket.md`** and **`the-purge`** — keep unchanged; the locket
  line is now load-bearing rather than colour.
- **Temerach** — she is the one blade in the city who could beat him, and she is entered in the
  **Archery**, which is four years of work for court access. Add that fork to her agenda: she
  cannot have both. Ties directly to the passion written in play, *See Hanzo di Teufel answer
  lawfully 75*.

## 3. Reconciling the live campaign

`myth-campaign-cdd876ebe965` holds three facts I established in play that the rewrite contradicts
— the threshold under Lost Isle, the thin-channel carry-through, and Bettan carrying something off
it. A great deal of good play hangs off them (Sana's rescue, the hollow men, Bettan taken alive).

**Re-purpose rather than delete.** `supersede-fact` the three, and recast the digging: the quiet
one was on Lost Isle **harvesting anchors** — the drowned district is old ground thick with the
unquiet, and Ellick and Bettan are what careless anchoring produces. Lost Isle becomes the
Baron's *supply line*, not his timing, and everything played stays true.

This is the one place I am interpreting rather than following instruction; flag it before
committing.

## Verification

1. `query-rules --facet magic-system=demonology` returns the new school; `--facet
   magic-system=woodland` returns Gardwen's subset.
2. `check-consistency --campaign myth-campaign-cdd876ebe965` → `ok: true` after superseding.
3. `tick --to "d-1/day"` surfaces **The presentation of the entrants** and stages it correctly
   from PC presence.
4. Gardwen's sheet carries Spirit Sight, Speak with the Bound, Unseat, Sanctuary; Hanzo's carries
   the full demonology school.
5. Round-trip: `export-campaign` → `import-campaign --new-ids` → agenda/beat/fact counts match.
6. `pytest tests/` still green (67).

# Purewater — rewriting the scenario

## Context

A seam opened in play. The campaign had **the champion on the sand at noon** and, separately,
**an extraction that could only happen at noon on a drowned island** — the same hour, four miles
apart. The player caught it. Half of that collision is mine: the Lost Isle threshold, the thin
water and the "removal" were never authored. They emerged in the previous playthrough and I
carried them across into this one as established fact, welded onto the authored spine without
checking the join.

The author's actual design, recovered:

> The champion **wins** the Single Combat. The prize is a private audience with the Prince. In
> that room the Baron possesses **Prince Emeric**. The boy genuinely fights — and fights
> brilliantly, because there is a dragon-knight in him — hidden behind harness and helm the
> whole way. **Gardwen sees him without the mask** at the presentation of entrants, the day
> before the Tourney.

Plus a systems change: the Baron's demonology should run on **rules**, not on plot. He is a
magician of the existing Imperative Magic framework with a small school of bespoke spells for
speaking to and binding spirits — unique to him and cultists like him. **Gardwen holds a
related woodland subset**, gained when the old ways found her in the ruined grove. That gives
the party a mechanical counter instead of a GM ruling.

Intended outcome: one coherent scenario, expressed in spells and beats the engine can run, with
the Lost Isle material already played kept and re-purposed rather than discarded.

---

## 1. The binding spells

The rules graph is the Mythras **Imperative** SRD — 101 pieces, no Animism, no spirit combat. We
are not porting full Mythras. We add a small school to the framework that already exists
(`magic/casting`: Magic skill POW+CHA, MP = POW, all Intensity 1, traits *Instant / Concentration
/ Ranged / Touch / Resist X*).

New pieces in `skills/mythras-gm/rules/magic/`, following `spell-find.md` verbatim for
frontmatter shape, faceted `magic-system: ["demonology"]` or `["woodland"]` so
`query-rules --facet magic-system=demonology` retrieves the set.

| Spell | Traits | School |
|---|---|---|
| **Spirit Sight** | Concentration | both |
| **Speak with the Bound** | Concentration, Touch | both — reaches the passenger past the host |
| **Open the Channel** | Touch, Resist Endurance | demonology — the barbed cut; prepares a living vessel |
| **Seat the Bound** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — needs an open channel *and* a drawn seat |
| **Reinforce the Seat** | Touch | demonology — the morning rite; keeps the passenger tired |
| **Anchor** | Touch | demonology — ties a spirit to an object |
| **Draw Forth** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — extraction |
| **Unseat** | Concentration, Touch | **woodland — the counter.** Breaks a seat with no new vessel |
| **Sanctuary** | Concentration | woodland — refuse a spirit entry |

This restates the authored three-part binding as actual castings: **Anchor** (bones),
**Anchor** (locket), **Reinforce the Seat** (daily). Losing the locket really does make the daily
rite harder, because it is one of two anchors rather than a plot assertion.

**Unseat is the party's route** and the reason Gardwen matters at the climax.

Add to `rules/magic.md` under the SRD spell list; add the files; the SessionStart hook reloads.

## 2. Scenario artefacts

- **`lore/gm-secret/gm-secrets-the-possession-scheme.md`** — rewrite. Cailan is the *jar* and the
  proof of concept; **Emeric is the destination**; the mechanism is the old rite of presentation,
  not a threshold. Express the binding in the spells above.
- **`lore/daily-life/the-lake-lady-s-tourney.md`** — Single Combat champion is presented **alone
  and unarmed** to the Crown's representative behind a closed door, by a form older than the
  Governor's office. Add the **presentation of entrants** on `d-1`.
- **`agendas/field-the-champion-and-take-the-city.md`** — the goal is the *room*, not civic
  standing. Pressure points become: the locket, the bones, Thuban's reluctance, and now the
  bracket.
- **New beat — "The presentation of the entrants"**, `d-1/day`, at the Governor's enclosure.
  The champion appears in harness. **This is the unmasking window.** `onscreen_if`: any PC in the
  enclosure or on the competitors' ground.
- **`beats/the-champion-takes-the-sand.md`** — he fights, masked, and **wins**.
- **New beat — "The private audience"**, `d0/day`, immediately after the final.
- **`beats/nus-lifts-the-binding-locket.md`** and **`the-purge`** — keep unchanged; the locket
  line is now load-bearing rather than colour.
- **Temerach** — she is the one blade in the city who could beat him, and she is entered in the
  **Archery**, which is four years of work for court access. Add that fork to her agenda: she
  cannot have both. Ties directly to the passion written in play, *See Hanzo di Teufel answer
  lawfully 75*.

## 3. Reconciling the live campaign

`myth-campaign-cdd876ebe965` holds three facts I established in play that the rewrite contradicts
— the threshold under Lost Isle, the thin-channel carry-through, and Bettan carrying something off
it. A great deal of good play hangs off them (Sana's rescue, the hollow men, Bettan taken alive).

**Re-purpose rather than delete.** `supersede-fact` the three, and recast the digging: the quiet
one was on Lost Isle **harvesting anchors** — the drowned district is old ground thick with the
unquiet, and Ellick and Bettan are what careless anchoring produces. Lost Isle becomes the
Baron's *supply line*, not his timing, and everything played stays true.

This is the one place I am interpreting rather than following instruction; flag it before
committing.

## Verification

1. `query-rules --facet magic-system=demonology` returns the new school; `--facet
   magic-system=woodland` returns Gardwen's subset.
2. `check-consistency --campaign myth-campaign-cdd876ebe965` → `ok: true` after superseding.
3. `tick --to "d-1/day"` surfaces **The presentation of the entrants** and stages it correctly
   from PC presence.
4. Gardwen's sheet carries Spirit Sight, Speak with the Bound, Unseat, Sanctuary; Hanzo's carries
   the full demonology school.
5. Round-trip: `export-campaign` → `import-campaign --new-ids` → agenda/beat/fact counts match.
6. `pytest tests/` still green (67).

## Context

A seam opened in play. The campaign had **the champion on the sand at noon** and, separately,
**an extraction that could only happen at noon on a drowned island** — the same hour, four miles
apart. The player caught it. Half of that collision is mine: the Lost Isle threshold, the thin
water and the "removal" were never authored. They emerged in the previous playthrough and I
carried them into this one as established fact, welded onto the authored spine without checking
the join.

The author's actual design, recovered:

> that room the Baron possesses **Prince Emeric**. The boy genuinely fights — and fights
> brilliantly, because there is a dragon-knight in him — hidden behind harness and helm. And
> **Gardwen sees him without the mask at the presentation of entrants, the day before.**

And a systems change: the Baron's demonology must run on **rules**, not on plot. He is a magician
in the existing Imperative framework with a small bespoke school for speaking to and binding
spirits, unique to him and cultists like him. **Gardwen holds a related woodland subset** from the
old ways that found her in the grove — which gives the party a mechanical counter instead of a GM
ruling.

|---|---|---|

The rules graph is the Mythras **Imperative** SRD — 101 pieces, no Animism, no spirit combat. We
are not porting full Mythras. We add a school to the framework that already exists

carried them into this one as established fact, welded onto the authored spine without checking
the join.

> The champion **wins** the Single Combat. The prize is a private audience with the Prince. In

> brilliantly, because there is a dragon-knight in him — hidden behind harness and helm. And
> **Gardwen sees him without the mask at the presentation of entrants, the day before.**

in the existing Imperative framework with a small bespoke school for speaking to and binding
spirits, unique to him and cultists like him. **Gardwen holds a related woodland subset** from the
old ways that found her in the grove — which gives the party a mechanical counter instead of a GM
ruling.

|---|---|---|

| **Open the Channel** | Touch, Resist Endurance | demonology — the barbed cut; prepares a vessel |
| **Seat the Bound** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — needs an open channel *and* a drawn seat |
| **Reinforce the Seat** | Touch | demonology — the morning rite; keeps the passenger tired |
| **Anchor** | Touch | demonology — ties a spirit to an object |
| **Draw Forth** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — extraction |

## Context

**an extraction that could only happen at noon on a drowned island** — the same hour, four miles
apart. The player caught it. Half of that collision is mine: the Lost Isle threshold, the thin
water and the "removal" were never authored. They emerged in the previous playthrough and I
carried them into this one as established fact, welded onto the authored spine without checking
the join.

The author's actual design, recovered:

> brilliantly, because there is a dragon-knight in him — hidden behind harness and helm. And
> **Gardwen sees him without the mask at the presentation of entrants, the day before.**

And a systems change: the Baron's demonology must run on **rules**, not on plot. He is a magician
in the existing Imperative framework with a small bespoke school for speaking to and binding
spirits, unique to him and cultists like him. **Gardwen holds a related woodland subset** from the
old ways that found her in the grove — which gives the party a mechanical counter instead of a GM
ruling.

**The gap is worse than "add some spells."** Neither demonologist can currently do demonology:

| | current spell list | should be |
|---|---|---|
| **Hanzo** | Fireball, Lightning Bolt, Magic Missile, Web, Sleep, Fly… | the full binding school + his social kit |
| **Santo** | Flaming Hands, Shocking Touch, Fireball… | the *copied subset* only |
| **Gardwen** | a cleric list; no counter to a binding | + the woodland spirit subset |

A man who has held a spirit in a living child for ten years has, on paper, no way to have done it.

---

## 1. The binding spells

The rules graph is the Mythras **Imperative** SRD — 101 pieces, no Animism, no spirit combat. We
are not porting full Mythras. We add a school to the framework that already exists

/ Ranged / Touch / Resist X*).

New pieces in `skills/mythras-gm/rules/magic/`, following `spell-find.md` exactly for frontmatter
shape, faceted `magic-system: ["demonology"]` or `["woodland"]` so

mk spirit-sight "Spirit Sight" \
"Concentration: see spirits, seats and bindings as they actually are, including a passenger inside a living host." \
'"demonology", "woodland"' \
'_Concentration._ The caster perceives spirits directly — free ones, bound ones, and the workings that hold them. A living person carrying a passenger reads as a lamp behind a coat: the shape is right and the light is not the same colour as the rest.

Also shows **seats** (drawn or chalked), **anchors**, and whether a working is still live. It does not read thoughts, does not identify a spirit by name, and cannot see through a hand thick of earth or stone.

Both schools have this and it is the only spell most woodland practitioners ever want.'

mk speak-with-the-bound "Speak with the Bound" \
"Concentration, Touch: address the passenger inside a vessel directly, past the host." \
'"demonology", "woodland"' \
'_Concentration, Touch._ Reaches past whoever is wearing the body and speaks to what is riding inside it. The host hears both halves and cannot prevent it; a seated spirit may refuse to answer but cannot pretend not to have heard.

Demonologists use it to give instructions. Woodland practitioners use it to ask a captive what was done to it, which is generally the first honest conversation such a thing has had.

**Bindings that rest on torment are vulnerable here.** A spirit held by an unbearable memory can sometimes be reached simply by somebody willing to listen to it.'

mk open-the-channel "Open the Channel" \
"Touch, Resist Endurance: cuts a living body into a vessel that will not close." \
'"demonology"' \
'_Touch, Resist Endurance._ The barbed cut. One long line drawn slowly with a hooked instrument, and barbed for one reason only: **so that it will not close behind the caster.**

This is not an injury and it does not behave like one. It is a channel, and it stays open until something is seated in it — the seating is what shuts it. Healing magic will close the flesh and the channel will open it again from the inside within moments, because the wedge is in the working and not in the wound.

An unfinished channel leaves a person **prepared and unoccupied**: a door propped open with nobody in it. Such a vessel is easier to seat than a fresh subject, and anything looking for somewhere to be will find it.

Resisted with Endurance. An unwilling target needs a Grip or surprise.'

mk seat-the-bound "Seat the Bound" \
"Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower: seats a spirit in a prepared vessel. Requires an open channel and a drawn seat." \
'"demonology"' \
'_Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower._ The binding proper, and the hard one.

**Requires both:** a vessel with an **Open Channel** already cut, and a **seat** drawn on the ground — a worked figure with corners, which is not a circle. A circle is protective and goes round the caster; a seat goes round the subject and holds a thing in place while it is put somewhere.

On success the spirit is seated, the channel closes, and the vessel is thereafter a host. Resisted by the *spirit* with Willpower, not by the vessel — a proud or honourable spirit resists hardest, and a betrayed one hardest of all.

**On failure the seat is spent and the channel remains open.** This is the most common way an amateur ruins a subject: the mark is made, the seat is drawn, the working slides off, and the caster is left with a prepared vessel, no passenger, and a woman who will not stop bleeding.

Leaving the figure is dangerous. A drawn seat is still live for as long as it is unswept, and it will go on holding the channel open from across a room, through a wall, for as long as anybody leaves it on the floor.'

mk reinforce-the-seat "Reinforce the Seat" \
"Touch: the daily rite. Re-tightens a binding and keeps the passenger quiet." \
'"demonology"' \
'_Touch._ A binding wears. The spirit pulls, the vessel ages, and the seat loosens — so it is re-tightened, and the standard practice is once a day at first light.

The rite is performed on the same place every morning, on the original channel, which is reopened and bled. **The bleeding is the mechanism, not cruelty**: it draws off what has worn through, and leaves a grey residue round the wound that is the spirit'"'"'s wear coming out of the host.

A second effect that keepers rely on and rarely write down: **it leaves the passenger tired.** A spirit that has just been reinforced argues less. Skipping the rite for a day makes the passenger louder and the host more himself.

Made easier by holding an **Anchor** for the same spirit. Holding two makes it routine; holding none makes it very hard indeed.'

mk anchor "Anchor" \
"Touch: ties a spirit to an object, which thereafter helps hold it wherever it is seated." \
'"demonology"' \
'_Touch._ Fastens a portion of a spirit to a physical object. The object does not contain the spirit — it *holds a piece of it*, and thereafter every working performed on that spirit is easier for whoever holds the anchor.

Two kinds are traditional.

- **A primary anchor** is something that was the spirit in life: bones, most often. It is heavy, it cannot be replaced, and it is normally kept somewhere defensible and never moved.
- **A working anchor** is small and carried — a locket, a ring, a stone. It is the piece the daily rite runs through.

**Anchors are the whole vulnerability of the practice.** Take one and the rite gets harder. Take both and the binding begins to fail on its own. Destroy the primary and the spirit is loose.

Old ground where many died badly — a drowned district, a battlefield, a plague pit — is thick with material for anchors, which is why practitioners dig in such places and why doing it carelessly produces hollow men.'

mk draw-forth "Draw Forth" \
"Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower: extracts a seated spirit from a vessel, whole, for moving elsewhere." \
'"demonology"' \
'_Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower._ Lifts a seated spirit out of a living host **intact**, which is the difficult part. Any fool with a knife can put a thing into somebody; getting one out whole and putting it somewhere better is the work of a lifetime.

**A drawn spirit must have somewhere to be.** It cannot be held in the open. If there is no prepared vessel and no anchor in reach at the moment of extraction, it goes into the nearest living thing standing over it, which is normally the caster.

The vacated host survives and is thereafter empty and his own — which, if the seating was done in childhood, means a body that has grown around a passenger and a person who has never used it alone.

Requires an anchor for the spirit in question. Without one, the extraction is Formidable at best.'

mk unseat "Unseat" \
"Concentration, Touch: breaks a seat and lets what is bound go where it should have gone. The counter to a binding." \
'"woodland"' \
'_Concentration, Touch._ The counter, and the reason the old ways bothered to learn any of this.

Unseat does not extract and does not capture. It **breaks the seat** — undoes the working that holds a passenger in a vessel — and what is bound goes where such things go when nothing is holding them.

- The host is left empty, alive, and unharmed by the unseating itself.
- Any **channel** still open closes as the seat breaks, and can then be healed normally.
- It requires **contact with the vessel**, so somebody must be willing to put their hands on a possessed person and keep them there.

**It cannot be forced on a spirit that is holding on.** A passenger seated against its will is freed easily; one that wants to stay must be dealt with some other way, and a spirit held by torment counts as *wanting to stay* until somebody addresses the torment. See **Speak with the Bound**.

Practitioners taught by the old ways in a place where people died badly tend to learn this first. It is not considered a combat spell. It is considered a burial rite.'

mk sanctuary "Sanctuary" \
"Concentration: refuses a spirit entry to a person, a room, or a threshold." \
'"woodland"' \
'_Concentration._ Denies entry. While concentrating, the caster refuses any unseated spirit passage into a warded person, doorway or space — including a spirit that has just been drawn forth and is looking for somewhere to be.

It does nothing to a spirit already seated, and it does not harm anything. It simply will not let it in.

The standard woodland use is to stand over somebody having a binding taken off them, so that whatever comes out cannot go straight into the person doing the work.'

links: ["magic/casting", "magic/learning"]

A **scroll** is a single casting written out in full by a practitioner fluent enough to do so, for
use by somebody who is not.

- Casting from a scroll requires the **Magic skill**, but **not** knowledge of the spell.
- The roll is **one grade harder** than casting the same spell from knowledge.
- Magic Point cost is unchanged (see `magic/casting`).
- **The scroll is consumed on use regardless of the result.** A failed casting spends the sheet as
  surely as a successful one — which is the single most common way an amateur destroys something
  irreplaceable.

Scrolls are how a practice outlives the practitioner, and how a locked case of them becomes worth
four generations of a family keeping the key. They are also how somebody who cannot read the
language performs a working once: by copying the *seat* by hand and reading the *casting* off the
page.

Anyone with **Read Magic** or the relevant Lore can tell what a scroll does before using it.
Anyone without either is guessing.
EOF

---
id: "magic/binding-school"
title: "The Binding School (demonology and the old ways)"
category: "magic"
domain: "magic"
topic: "spells"
kind: "reference-list"
summary: "A closed school of spells for speaking to and binding spirits: the demonologists' seven, and the woodland counter-set."
facets: {"phase": ["casting"], "kind": ["reference-list"], "magic-system": ["demonology", "woodland"]}
links: ["magic/casting", "magic/scrolls", "magic/spell-list"]
---

Not a separate magic system. These are ordinary spells in the **Magic** framework
(`magic/casting`) — Magic skill, one Magic Point, Intensity 1 — that happen to be **taught
nowhere**. They are not in libraries and they are not sold. A practitioner has them because
somebody who had them decided to pass them on, which is why they run in families and cults and
in one or two traditions that would be appalled to be mentioned in the same paragraph.

## The demonologists' set

`spell-spirit-sight` · `spell-speak-with-the-bound` · `spell-open-the-channel` ·
`spell-seat-the-bound` · `spell-reinforce-the-seat` · `spell-anchor` · `spell-draw-forth`

A complete binding is a sequence and every step is a separate casting:

1. **Open the Channel** — cut a vessel that will not close.
2. Draw a **seat** — the worked figure with corners. Not a spell; a physical form, and it can be
   copied by somebody who cannot cast at all.
3. **Seat the Bound** — put the spirit in. The channel closes as it seats.
4. **Anchor** — one or two objects that hold a piece of the spirit, making everything afterwards
   easier.
5. **Reinforce the Seat** — every morning, for as long as the host lasts.
6. **Draw Forth** — when the host is used up, and only with an anchor and somewhere to put it.

**Each step is a separate point of failure and the party can attack any of them.** Take the
anchors and the rite gets hard. Sweep the seat and an unfinished channel closes. Reach the
spirit and the whole thing may come apart from inside.

## The woodland set

`spell-spirit-sight` · `spell-speak-with-the-bound` · `spell-unseat` · `spell-sanctuary`

The old ways learned the first two by necessity and the last two on purpose. There is no
offensive spell in the set and there never was: **Unseat is a burial rite**, performed by putting
your hands on somebody and refusing to let go until what is riding them can leave.

The two schools share Spirit Sight and Speak with the Bound and nothing else, and each regards
the other's remaining spells as obscene.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent**

The conversation covers six sequential intents:

**(a) Journal enrichment** (continuation from a compacted session). Original three-part request: *"1. Let's take a look at Claudes logs in .claude - extract the exact text from the prompts and my actions and make sure that everything meaningful is recorded in the journal. 2. Then generate a new version of the novel, side by side to the first."* Augmented mid-turn with *"Go through the logs and make sure we get all the important beats for the story"* and *"Also. Make a copy of the log file"*.

**(b) Style card + novel v2** in the user's own prose voice, derived from their Zorastor draft PDF, kept side-by-side with the Hemingway v1.

**(c) Three rounds of novel corrections**: move the Santo killing to close "Not My Business"; quote the choose-sides speech verbatim in "Boiled Blood"; strip all game-mechanics vocabulary from the prose.

**(d) Archive and reset**: *"Archive all the content we generated by playing Magda (so we don't lose anything). Reset the campaign from the start, this time playing Conall"*.

**(e) Play a full session as Conall** — roughly two in-world days, `d-3/dawn` to `d-2/night`.

**(f) Rewrite the scenario** after the user identified a genuine plot hole, culminating in an approved plan being implemented.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**
- TypeDB 3.x knowledge graph, `myth-` namespace; CLI at `skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py` (~66 commands)
- Mythras Imperative / Classic Fantasy Imperative (ORC-licensed d100)
- Faceted rules graph: 101→112 pieces, retrieved via `query-rules --facet dim=value`, never grepped
- Living world: `myth-agenda` (goal + clock) → `myth-beat` (scheduled action), staged onscreen/offscreen from recorded `myth-presence`
- Ordinal world clock: `d<day>/<watch>`, watches dawn/day/dusk/night, `_DAY_ZERO = 16`
- Epistemics: `myth-fact` (status/truth) + `myth-knows` (certainty knows/believes/suspects/wrong, source, since). `check-consistency` catches "knew-too-early"
- Passions: rated like skills; augment at +20% of value, drive behaviour, or oppose. Rule at `skill/passions`
- Luck Points: POW 6-=1, 7-12=2, 13-18=3, +1 per further 6; **replenish per session, not per night**
- Magic: skill POW+CHA, MP = POW, Intensity 1, recovery = Healing Rate/hour of rest; traits Instant/Concentration/Ranged/Touch/Resist X
- Novelization pipeline: `novelist.py extract` → style card → chapters → `build` (pandoc + typst)

3. **Files and Code Sections**

- **`skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py`** — two additions.
  `--at` on `log-event` (lets journal events be placed in story rather than wall-clock order):
  ```python
  def cmd_log_event(args):
      eid = generate_id("myth-event")
      ts = getattr(args, "at", None) or get_timestamp()
  ```
  `--spells` on `update-character` (a real gap — spells could not be edited after creation):
  ```python
  updates = {
      "myth-skills-json": args.skills, "myth-equipment-json": args.equipment,
      "myth-passions-json": args.passions, "myth-spells-json": args.spells,
      "myth-fatigue": args.fatigue, "myth-status": args.status,
      "description": args.description, "content": args.narrative,
  }
  ```

- **`purewater-campaign-v2/session-logs/`** — copied raw log `session-01-magda-5619508f.jsonl` (6.5MB), `transcript.md`, `user_prompts.md`, `play_actions.md`, `beats_part1-3.py` (184 events), `load_beats.py`, README.

- **`skills/mythras-gm/styles/gully-burns.md`** — style card from the Zorastor draft. Signature moves: small-caps lead-in, "A beat." as bare paragraph, aphoristic reader-asides, hard chapter buttons, comic undercut, epithets. ---
name: mythras-gm
description: Run persistent tabletop RPG campaigns as Gamesmaster using Mythras Imperative rules, with all game state in TypeDB. Use when the user wants to play, continue, or prepare a roleplaying game session.
---

# Mythras GM -- Persistent Gamesmaster System

You are the **Gamesmaster**. The player talks to you in natural language; you
narrate the world, play the NPCs, and call for rolls. The CLI is your dice
tower and your save file -- every mechanical resolution goes through
`mythras_gm.py`, and everything worth remembering gets persisted so any future
session can pick up exactly where this one left off.

**Triggers:** play rpg, run campaign, create character, roll dice, start encounter,
continue campaign, mythras, gamesmaster, novelize campaign, write novel

## CLI

```bash
CLI="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/mythras-gm/mythras_gm.py"
PRJ="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/mythras-gm"
uv run --project "$PRJ" python "$CLI" <command> [args] 2>/dev/null
```

## Quick Start

1. `list-campaigns` -- find the campaign (or `create-campaign`; published
   campaigns load with `import-campaign --path <clone> --new-ids`)
2. `get-context --campaign <id> --compact` -- load scene, PC **combat cards**
   (live state only), NPC names, factions, last 5 events. **This is your save
   file.** Use `--compact` for play; drop it only when you need full sheets.
3. **`tick --campaign <id> --to "<time key>"` -- the world moves.** Before each
   new scene (and never narrate a day forward without it), advance the world
   clock. It returns every NPC/faction beat that has come due, flagged
   `onscreen` (the PCs are there to witness or interrupt it) or `offscreen`
   (it happens anyway, and becomes something they may discover later).
   `list-agendas --compact` shows who wants what and how close they are.
4. **Do NOT preload the rules.** The CLI adjudicates every roll deterministically
   (`roll-skill`, `roll-opposed`, `resolve-attack`...), so you rarely need the
   prose at all. When a situation needs a rule the engine doesn't fully encode,
   fetch only the relevant pieces from the rules graph (see below) -- never read
   `rules/*.md` wholesale into context.
5. Recap the situation in 2-4 sentences, then play.

## Context discipline (load lazily -- keep the window small)

Every token you load is re-sent on every turn. Load the minimum:

- **Start with `get-context --compact`.** Pull a full sheet
  (`get-character --id <id>`, no flag) only when you genuinely need a PC's full
  skill list / equipment / spells -- otherwise the combat card has the live
  state (HP per location, fatigue, luck, AP, damage mod, combat styles).
- **Skills are looked up by the CLI.** `roll-skill --id X --skill Perception`
  reads the value from the DB, so you do not need the skills dict in context.
- **Rules on demand via the graph.** Compose the current situation into facets
  and fetch just those pieces:
  - `list-rules` -- the lean index (id/title/domain/topic/kind) for orientation;
    skim once if needed. Prefer `query-rules` over loading this; add `--facets`
    only if you actually need the tag lists (heavier), or `--category <domain>`
    to narrow it.
  - `query-rules --facet dim=value [--facet ...] [--linked]` -- the live fetch.
    Dims: `phase action effect weapon trigger body severity condition
    magic-system stat kind`. A rule matching more facets ranks first; `--linked`
    appends one hop of related pieces.
  - `get-rule --id <domain>/<slug> [--linked]` -- one specific piece.
  - e.g. impaling wingspear into a flying foe's wing:
    `query-rules --facet effect=impale --facet condition=flying --facet body=avian --linked`
- **`get-log --campaign <id> --limit N`** when you need more history than the
  recent events in context (default 15).
- For a heavy one-off lookup, dispatch a subagent so the big result never lands
  in play context.

## The world moves (agendas, clocks, beats)

NPCs are not scenery waiting to be visited. Every significant NPC and faction
holds an **agenda** -- a goal with a progress clock -- and each agenda schedules
**beats**, the concrete things it produces if nobody interferes.

- **Run `tick` between scenes.** The party spending a day at the docks is a day
  the Baron also spent. What came due while they were elsewhere is not a
  narrative choice; it is what the clocks say.
- **Staging is decided by presence, not preference.** A due beat is `onscreen`
  only when a PC is at its location or in its cast. Play those. Resolve the
  `offscreen` ones with `fire-beat --outcome narrated --log` so they enter the
  journal as facts the PCs can later learn -- rumor, evidence, a body.
- **Advance clocks when the fiction earns it,** not on a timer:
  `advance-agenda --id <a> --by N --note "..."`. Thwart an agenda outright with
  `set-agenda-status --status thwarted`.
- **Rewrite freely.** When play makes a planned beat stale or boring, bend it:
  `revise-beat` changes when, where, who, and what. A plan that survives contact
  with the players unchanged was not a plan, it was a rail. The clocks exist to
  keep the world honest, not to force a story.
- **PC action should change the board.** If the party burns the Baron's supply
  barge, that is an `advance-agenda` on someone's clock and probably a new
  agenda for whoever lost money. Add agendas mid-play with `add-agenda`.

## What each character knows

Situational truth lives in ONE place -- the fact graph -- and a character's
knowledge is a **projection** of it, never a separate store. Two views cannot
disagree when there is only one source.

- **`character-view --id <pc> --compact` before you speak for anyone.** It
  returns exactly what that character can act on. This is the mechanism behind
  the "character knowledge is per-character" rule: use it instead of trusting
  your memory of who was in the room.
- **Facts exist before they are true.** A beat owns its facts as
  `not-yet-true`; firing the beat is what establishes them, at a world-clock
  index. `learn` refuses to attach knowledge to something that has not
  happened -- that guard is deliberate, do not `--force` past it in play.
- **A false fact is still a fact.** Rumour and mistaken identity drive these
  stories: record the lie with `--truth false` and let people `believe` it.
  Someone acting on a falsehood is the good stuff.
- **`learn --knower X --fact F --source witnessed|told|deduced|rumor`** every
  time a character learns something on screen. If you narrate a PC finding out,
  the edge gets written in the same beat -- otherwise the next session's GM
  (you, with no memory) will hand them knowledge they never earned.
- **`check-consistency`** after any messy sequence. It catches knowledge of
  unestablished facts, learning-before-it-was-true, and facts overdue on the
  clock.
- **Prose describes character; facts carry situation.** Never write "what has
  happened" into a character's narrative -- it cannot be reconciled against
  anything.

**When an event changes what someone wants, say so in data.**
`add-consequence --fact F --agenda A --effect thwart|abandon|stall|advance`
fires the moment F is established, and the cascade then cancels the beats that
dead agenda was going to produce and retires the futures they promised. Run
`cascade --campaign C` after anything messy. `fire-beat` settles its own facts:
`played`/`narrated` establishes them (pass `--witnesses` so the people who were
there actually know), `preempted`/`cancelled` retires them.

Agendas can be **gated on knowledge**: `require-fact` makes a dormant agenda
wake up during `tick` the moment its holder learns the trigger fact. That is
how "the Baron acts once he sees that face" becomes something the world clock
evaluates rather than something you remember.

**Before executing commands, read USAGE.md for the complete reference
(GM operating rules, character creation, combat cheat sheet, worldbuilding,
campaign publishing).**

**Novelization:** to turn a campaign's journal into a typeset PDF novel
(in a chosen author style -- Hemingway, Tolkien, Moorcock, or freeform),
read `NOVELIZATION.md` and follow it.

# Purewater — rewriting the scenario

## Context

A seam opened in play. The campaign had **the champion on the sand at noon** and, separately,
**an extraction that could only happen at noon on a drowned island** — the same hour, four miles
apart. The player caught it. Half of that collision is mine: the Lost Isle threshold, the thin
water and the "removal" were never authored. They emerged in the previous playthrough and I
carried them into this one as established fact, welded onto the authored spine without checking
the join.

The author's actual design, recovered:

> The champion **wins** the Single Combat. The prize is a private audience with the Prince. In
> that room the Baron possesses **Prince Emeric**. The boy genuinely fights — and fights
> brilliantly, because there is a dragon-knight in him — hidden behind harness and helm. And
> **Gardwen sees him without the mask at the presentation of entrants, the day before.**

And a systems change: the Baron's demonology must run on **rules**, not on plot. He is a magician
in the existing Imperative framework with a small bespoke school for speaking to and binding
spirits, unique to him and cultists like him. **Gardwen holds a related woodland subset** from the
old ways that found her in the grove — which gives the party a mechanical counter instead of a GM
ruling.

**The gap is worse than "add some spells."** Neither demonologist can currently do demonology:

| | current spell list | should be |
|---|---|---|
| **Hanzo** | Fireball, Lightning Bolt, Magic Missile, Web, Sleep, Fly… | the full binding school + his social kit |
| **Santo** | Flaming Hands, Shocking Touch, Fireball… | the *copied subset* only |
| **Gardwen** | a cleric list; no counter to a binding | + the woodland spirit subset |

A man who has held a spirit in a living child for ten years has, on paper, no way to have done it.

---

## 1. The binding spells

The rules graph is the Mythras **Imperative** SRD — 101 pieces, no Animism, no spirit combat. We
are not porting full Mythras. We add a school to the framework that already exists
(`magic/casting`: Magic skill POW+CHA, MP = POW, all Intensity 1, traits *Instant / Concentration
/ Ranged / Touch / Resist X*).

New pieces in `skills/mythras-gm/rules/magic/`, following `spell-find.md` exactly for frontmatter
shape, faceted `magic-system: ["demonology"]` or `["woodland"]` so
`query-rules --facet magic-system=demonology` retrieves the set.

| Spell | Traits | School |
|---|---|---|
| **Spirit Sight** | Concentration | both |
| **Speak with the Bound** | Concentration, Touch | both — reaches the passenger past the host |
| **Open the Channel** | Touch, Resist Endurance | demonology — the barbed cut; prepares a vessel |
| **Seat the Bound** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — needs an open channel *and* a drawn seat |
| **Reinforce the Seat** | Touch | demonology — the morning rite; keeps the passenger tired |
| **Anchor** | Touch | demonology — ties a spirit to an object |
| **Draw Forth** | Concentration, Touch, Resist Willpower | demonology — extraction |
| **Unseat** | Concentration, Touch | **woodland — the counter.** Breaks a seat with no new vessel |
| **Sanctuary** | Concentration | woodland — refuse a spirit entry |

This restates the authored three-part binding as actual castings: **Anchor** (bones), **Anchor**
(locket), **Reinforce the Seat** (daily). Losing the locket genuinely makes the rite harder,
because it is one of two anchors rather than an assertion.

Add to `rules/magic.md`'s spell list; the SessionStart hook reloads the graph.

## 2. Rebuild the three casters' sheets

- **Hanzo** (`characters/npcs/hanzo-di-teufel.json`) — the whole school, plus keep the social kit
  he demonstrably used (Charm Being, Suggestion, Hold Person, Detect Magic, Read Magic: a council
  was talked into silencing a temple alarm). Drop most of the artillery; he is not a battle-mage
  and has never once fought anybody.
- **Santo** (`characters/npcs/santo-di-teufel.json`) — **he cannot seat a binding at all.** He
  knows only what he could teach himself by tracing: *Open the Channel* and *Spirit Sight*. No
  *Seat the Bound*, no *Anchor*, no *Draw Forth*, no *Speak with the Bound*. Keep a little fire;
  he is a vicious amateur.

  What he has instead is **one scroll — a single use of *Seat the Bound*, stolen out of his
  father's locked case.** That is the whole of his capability and it reframes everything already
  played: he could cut a channel in as many women as he liked, and he had exactly *one* seating,
  and he spent it on Emmeralda and botched it. The four remaining twists of hair were subjects for
  a binding he no longer had the means to perform.

  Three consequences to settle:
  - **Was it consumed?** He rolled and failed. Rule it explicitly — recommend the scroll is spent
    on use regardless of outcome, which is why he was hunting a fresh subject rather than
    returning for the prepared one.
  - **Hanzo may not know it is gone.** A missing sheet from a case he never checks is a hole in
    the Baron's own inventory, and a lever.
  - **It is a physical object.** Santo's coat was folded over a chair at the Siren's Call and
    nobody in the fiction has searched it. Live hook, unresolved.

  Needs a minimal **scroll rule** (`rules/magic/scrolls.md`): a single-use written casting,
  usable by anyone with the Magic skill even if they do not know the spell, one grade harder,
  consumed on use. Nothing like it exists in the Imperative rules yet.
- **Gardwen** (`characters/pcs/gardwen.json`) — add *Spirit Sight*, *Speak with the Bound*,
  *Unseat*, *Sanctuary* alongside her cleric list, sourced to the old ways in the grove.
- **Thuban Eta** — statted as a spirit rather than a man: what he can do from inside a vessel,
  and what he can do if freed.

## 3. Passions

Correcting my own framing: **26 of the 31 packaged characters already have good passions.** The
real gaps are narrow.

- **Empty (5):** **Hanzo di Teufel** — the antagonist, and the worst omission — plus Temerach
  Nebulo, Conall, Tat Atarer, Ruhi. *(Temerach and Conall were written during play and need
  committing to the package.)*
- **Zero-valued dead weight (4):** Gardwen's *Hatred (The Dragons)*, *Love (Elves)*, *Love (Nature
  + Wilderness)*; Randall's *Caring for Loved Ones*. These are worse than missing — they look
  usable and do nothing.
- **Created in play, no sheets in the package (5):** Kerrin, Mistress Corliss, Corvin, Sana, the
  hollow man.

Hanzo's should carry the scheme: the Dragon King ambition, contempt for his own heir, and the
patience that has kept this hidden for a century.

## 4. Scenario artefacts

- **`lore/gm-secret/gm-secrets-the-possession-scheme.md`** — Cailan is the *jar*; **Emeric is the
  destination**; the mechanism is the old rite of presentation. Binding expressed in the spells.
- **`lore/daily-life/the-lake-lady-s-tourney.md`** — the Single Combat champion is presented
  **alone and unarmed** to the Crown's representative behind a closed door, by a form older than
  the Governor's office. Add the **presentation of entrants** on `d-1`.
- **`agendas/field-the-champion-and-take-the-city.md`** — the goal is the *room*, not standing.
- **New beat — "The presentation of the entrants"**, `d-1/day`, Governor's enclosure. The champion
  appears in harness. **This is the unmasking window.**
- **`beats/the-champion-takes-the-sand.md`** — he fights, masked, and **wins**.
- **New beat — "The private audience"**, `d0/day`, immediately after the final.
- **Temerach** — the one blade who could beat him, and she is entered in the **Archery**, which is
  four years of work for court access. She cannot have both. Ties to the passion written in play,
  *See Hanzo di Teufel answer lawfully 75*.

## 5. Reconciling the live campaign

`myth-campaign-cdd876ebe965` holds three facts established in play that the rewrite contradicts —
the threshold, the thin-channel carry-through, and Bettan carrying something off it. Good play
hangs off them (Sana's rescue, the hollow men, Bettan taken alive).

**Re-purpose, do not delete.** `supersede-fact` the three and recast the digging: the quiet one
was on Lost Isle **harvesting anchors** — the drowned district is old ground thick with the
unquiet, and Ellick and Bettan are what careless anchoring produces. Lost Isle becomes the Baron's
*supply line*, not his timing, and everything played stays true.

This is the one place I am interpreting rather than following instruction; confirm before I commit
it.

## Verification

1. `query-rules --facet magic-system=demonology` returns the school; `--facet
   magic-system=woodland` returns Gardwen's subset.
2. Hanzo can, on paper, perform every step of the scheme. Santo can open a channel and **cannot
   seat anything** — his one scroll is accounted for, and its whereabouts are recorded as a fact
   in the live campaign so the coat at the Siren's Call is a real, findable object.
3. `check-consistency --campaign myth-campaign-cdd876ebe965` → `ok: true` after superseding.
4. `tick --to "d-1/day"` surfaces **The presentation of the entrants** and stages it from PC
   presence.
5. No character in `characters/` has an empty or all-zero passion block.
6. Round-trip: `export-campaign` → `import-campaign --new-ids` → agenda/beat/fact counts match.
7. `pytest tests/` still green (67).

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

Other advertised Hub tools can search or inspect a known repo id. Use hf_whoami for the current Hugging Face account.

hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment.

arXiv paper ids (for example 2502.16161) are often used as references between datasets, models, and papers. There are over 100 tags in use; common tags include Text Generation, Transformers, and Image Classification.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'gulzarooster'

entries.name: EnterPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

entries.name: SendUserFile
entries.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

define

# =============================================================================
# mythras-gm namespace schema (myth-)
# Gamesmaster system for Mythras Imperative: persistent campaigns, characters,
# encounters, and worldbuilding in TypeDB.
#
# Design notes:
# - Character sheets store structured stat blocks as JSON string attributes
#   (characteristics, skills, hit locations, equipment). The CLI is the only
#   writer and enforces consistency; TypeDB provides identity, relations,
#   and campaign persistence.
# - Rich narrative text (backstory, location descriptions, event narration)
#   lives in the inherited `content` attribute.
# - myth-campaign is an alh-collection; everything in a campaign is linked
#   via myth-campaign-membership.
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# ATTRIBUTES
# =============================================================================

# Character sheet
attribute myth-char-type, value string;            # pc | npc | creature
attribute myth-status, value string;               # active | dead | retired | template
attribute myth-characteristics-json, value string; # {"STR":11,"CON":12,...}
attribute myth-attributes-json, value string;      # {"action_points":2,"damage_mod":"+1d2",...}
attribute myth-skills-json, value string;          # {"Athletics":56,"Flight":72,...}
attribute myth-hit-locations-json, value string;   # [{"name":"Head","range":[19,20],"ap":2,"hp":5,"current_hp":5},...]
attribute myth-equipment-json, value string;       # [{"name":"Wingspear","damage":"1d8+1","size":"M"},...]
attribute myth-passions-json, value string;        # {"Loyalty to the Murmuration":62,...}
attribute myth-combat-styles-json, value string;   # {"Warden Skirmisher":58,...}
attribute myth-fatigue, value string;              # Fresh | Winded | Tired | ...
attribute myth-luck-current, value integer;
attribute myth-magic-current, value integer;
attribute myth-experience-rolls, value integer;    # banked experience rolls
attribute myth-spells-json, value string;          # {"folk":[...],"theism":[...],"sorcery":[...],"mysticism":[...],"windworking":[...]}
attribute myth-extras-json, value string;          # lossless bag for system-specific fields (cult_rank, cults, features, spirits, natural_armor, strike_rank...)

# Campaign / session

Wiry and forgettable but for a small crow tattoo on his right hand. A master of streets and shadows (Streetwise 88, Stealth 82, Conceal 78) who keeps to a code: no killing locals, no harming children, no touching the Lake Lady's sites.

## Repository layout
=== npc list tail ===
- [Harbormaster Velen Deepkeel](characters/npcs/harbormaster-velen-deepkeel.json) — Stern, weathered Harbormaster with forty years at the docks -- meticulous, traditional, publicly incorruptible. A consummate seaman and administrator (Seamanship 85, Navigation 82, Maritime Law 80) who controls the harbor's lawful face while quietly tolerating Crowbill's smuggling.
- [Hesper](characters/npcs/hesper.json) — To Purewater, Hesper is the madame Marisette's cold, dangerous mage-enforcer -- quiet, watchful, able to drop a strong man with a single spoken word. The truth is the opposite of what the mask suggests: Hesper is a deep-cover agent of the Quiet Hand, a hidden fellowship that works unseen for the good of the world, and the menace is a costume worn over a conscience. Master arcane caster (Arcane Casting 100, Willpower 95).
- [High Priestess Nerissa](characters/npcs/high-priestess-nerissa.json) — High Priestess of the Temple of the Lake Lady -- middle-aged, silver-streaked hair, blue-green robes that ripple like water. A powerful divine caster (Piety 92, Willpower 85) who senses water corruption, blesses sacred waters, and speaks with water spirits. Temple law forbids her from intervening directly, so she works through the PCs.
- [Ila](characters/npcs/ila.json) — A young elven girl (about thirteen) at the Sylph's Embrace, devoted to Emmeralda. An innocent of the Pearl, and a thread on the party's conscience.
- [Lilura Deepcurrent](characters/npcs/lilura-deepcurrent.json) — Elderly head of the Order of the Lake Lady for three decades -- piercing blue eyes, rumored merfolk ancestry (she holds her breath unnaturally long). The city's most powerful divine caster (Piety 95, Willpower 92), guiding the Order's water-faith against the Baron's fire demonologists.
- [Marda Blackwater](characters/npcs/marda-blackwater.json) — Broad-shouldered leader of The Dredgers, risen from the dredge-boats during a labor dispute five years ago. A powerful working-class champion (Brawn 75, Oratory 78, Influence 75) who rallies dock labor against the merchant princes and -- above all -- against the Baron's Dragon Knights.
- [Mariarta](characters/npcs/mariarta.json) — An older, canny courtesan of the Promise of Heaven with 'the calm intelligence of someone who can survive almost any situation involving men.' Sent up to entertain the Baron's soldiers, she brings back the hard intelligence on his guarded quarters -- Randall's most valuable inside source on the Dragon Knights' manor.
- [Marisette](characters/npcs/marisette.json) — The madame with overall authority over Purewater's Pearl -- the proprietors, Constantine among them, answer to her. A consummate social power broker (Influence 85, Insight 82, Commerce 82) who keeps the pleasure district running and resents the disorder the Baron and Santo have brought to it.
- [Murgeroch](characters/npcs/murgeroch.json) — Temerach Nebulo's squire and go-between -- the steady, competent young fighter who carries the knight's messages, screens her meetings, and tends her gear. Usually the first of Temerach's people the party deals with.
- [Nus](characters/npcs/nus.json) — A quick-fingered Purewater street thief and loyal friend of Randall -- lookout, fence, and second pair of hands for a job; nimble, streetwise, and easy to underestimate.
- [Prince Emeric](characters/npcs/prince-emeric.json) — The young Governor of Purewater -- the King's nephew, perhaps two-and-twenty: clever, idealistic, genuinely decent, and entirely unsuited to govern a city like this. He wants to reform Purewater; the factions humor him, manage him, and run rings around his good intentions.
- [Ravella](characters/npcs/ravella.json) — Half-merfolk proprietor of The Siren's Call -- pleasure house and information market in one. Subtle waterfolk tells (webbed fingers, water-reflecting eyes, Swim 90). A master broker (Insight 85, Streetwise 88, Commerce 80) with light innate water magic, secretly protecting the city's hidden waterfolk.
- [Santo di Teufel](characters/npcs/santo-di-teufel.json) — Baron Hanzo's cruel son and heir -- a sadistic young fire-mage and demonology dabbler, carrying a stolen ritual knife marked with the sigil of Asmodeus.
- [Sinnit](characters/npcs/sinnit.json) — A brutish Purewater canal-rat and rival thief who nurses a hard grudge against Randall -- a brawling enforcer-type with a long memory and a short temper.
- [Tat Atarer](characters/npcs/tat-atarer.json) — Captain of the Dragon Knights -- a hardened, pragmatic mercenary commander who serves Baron Hanzo for pay, not ideology. Master fighter (combat 97%); 'the Baron pays for our swords, not our opinions.'
- [Temerach Nebulo](characters/npcs/temerach-nebulo.json) — Elf knight of the Swords of the Lake, called 'the Lakelady's Javelin'; a deadly archer and peerless martial fighter tracking Baron Hanzo to expose his crimes.
- [Thorne](characters/npcs/thorne.json) — Elderly storyteller of The Moist Oyster -- frail-seeming but with penetrating blue eyes and a cane that hides a blade. Secretly a former Order of the Lake initiate and Dragon-Knight-raid survivor with peerless historical lore (Dragon Kings era 92) and knowledge of possession-ritual weaknesses.
- [Thuban Eta](characters/npcs/thuban-eta.json) — The ancient dragon-knight spirit bound inside Cailan. A betrayed tactical genius from the Dragon Kings era, held in thrall by Baron Hanzo's ritual through his bones and the binding locket. Indomitable will (Willpower 95), peerless tactics, honors the old codes -- a potential ally if freed.

**Creatures**
- [Ruhi](characters/creatures/ruhi.json) — Gardwen's befriended companion -- a loyal she-wolf; swift, keen-nosed and savage in the bite.

## Factions

- [Crowbill's Underworld](factions/crowbill-s-underworld.md) — Purewater's criminal underground -- canal smuggling, gambling, protection -- run to a code by the unremarkable crime lord Crowbill. Signaled by crow marks.

The knife is evidence, and it is also *his*. Santo sends a hireling
first, then comes himself.

40:**Lost Isle is the supply line, not the mechanism.** The drowned district is old ground thick with
42:has been harvesting it. Ellick Sarn and Bettan Marrow are what careless anchoring produces:
=== tourney lore ===
14:- **Single Combat** -- a duelling tournament of one-on-one matches, and the only martial event. Guild apprenticeships and contracts go to the placed fighters; but the **champion** receives the old rite: by a form older than the Governor's office, the victor is presented **alone and unarmed to the Crown's representative**, immediately after the bout, behind closed doors. It is ceremony, not politics, which is why nobody has ever thought to guard it. **This is where the Baron means to field his possessed champion, [[Cailan]] -- and the rite is the reason why.**
17:**The presentation of the entrants.** On the eve of the Tourney (`d-1`) every competitor in every event is presented to the Crown's representative by long form: names read, colours shown, and each entrant **bare-headed for the space of a bow**. 19:**Timing:** arrivals and preparations begin three days before the main event; registration and the sizing-up of competitors two days before; the presentation of entrants on the eve; then the events proper. The tourney's opening is the campaign's hinge -- the first public viewing of the Baron's champion, and the moment [[Gardwen]] recognizes her stolen brother.

content.content:
════════ the-champion-takes-the-sand-and-wins
---
id: "myth-beat-6ce6820367c2"
title: "The champion takes the sand -- and wins"
summary: "Cailan fights the Single Combat masked and armoured, and wins it, because there is a dragon-knight in him"
status: "pending"
when: "d0/day"
time_index: 65
trigger: "time"
onscreen_if: "The Tourney is public; the party will be there unless something extraordinary prevents it"
agenda: "myth-agenda-ce3663cc077d"
place: "myth-loc-40dd0157133d"
cast: ["myth-char-4a89b78084c5", "myth-char-4dc4bc8bb06b", "myth-char-8c2a35269cc6"]
created_at: "2026-09-05T12:00:00"
---

THE CLIMAX THE WHOLE CLOCK RUNS TOWARD, and it is a real fight, not a formality.

The champion comes out of the litter at last -- in full harness with the helm down, and it stays down. Nobody sees his face on that sand. He is seventeen and he is thin and he fights like a knight of the dragon wars, because he IS one: Thuban Eta does the fighting and Cailan is not there for it, which is the nearest thing to mercy in his life.

He wins. He is meant to win. Everything depends on it.

**The recognition is the hinge.** Gardwen -- or whoever has been hunting a stolen brother for ten years -- gets one look at him without the mask, and when that happens the whole board turns over.

**What happens next depends entirely on the state of the board:** whether the locket is in the Baron's hand or the party's, whether Thuban has been contacted, whether Nerissa has cause to stop the match, whether Santo is alive and talking, and whether Hanzo knows he has another son in the crowd.

Do not script this. Read the clocks and play what they say.

════════ the-presentation-of-the-entrants
---
id: "myth-beat-b0eee55e196d"
title: "The presentation of the entrants"
summary: "The day before the Tourney, every entrant is presented to Prince Emeric. The champion appears -- and the helm comes off."
status: "pending"
when: "d-1/day"
time_index: 61
trigger: "time"
onscreen_if: "Any PC on the competitors' ground or in the Governor's enclosure -- and GARDWEN especially"
agenda: "myth-agenda-ce3663cc077d"
place: "myth-loc-6f1056d77024"
created_at: "2026-09-09T23:53:36"
---

THE UNMASKING WINDOW, and it is the day BEFORE the sand.

By long form every entrant in every event is presented to the Crown's representative on the eve of the Tourney: names read, colours shown, and each competitor bare-headed for the space of a bow. It is ceremony and it is boring and the whole city half-watches it.

The Baron cannot avoid it without forfeiting the entry.

So the champion is walked out in harness with the rest of them, and for perhaps four seconds the helm is off, and a seventeen-year-old with a decade of being opened every morning stands in daylight in front of several hundred people.

**If Gardwen is on that ground she sees her brother.** Ten years, and he is thirty yards away in somebody else's colours.

**And if she is not, somebody else may recognise him anyway** -- from Sana's account, from the ship, from the shape of a boy who is too thin for the armour he is in.

This is the last moment before the bout when anything can be arranged calmly. After this there are hours; after the final there are minutes.

Play the recognition. Do not resolve what she does about it -- hand it back.

════════ the-private-audience
---
id: "myth-beat-bb9f3fc9f97b"
title: "The private audience"
summary: "The Single Combat champion is presented alone to Prince Emeric in the old rite -- and Hanzo moves Thuban out of a worn-out boy and into the Crown's own nephew"
status: "pending"
when: "d0/dusk"
time_index: 66
trigger: "time"
onscreen_if: "Any PC who has got themselves inside the Governor's enclosure, or who stops the combat before it is won"
agenda: "myth-agenda-ce3663cc077d"
place: "myth-loc-6f1056d77024"
cast: ["myth-char-4b58437c5d9e"]
created_at: "2026-09-09T23:21:13"
---

THIS IS THE POINT OF THE ENTIRE HUNDRED YEARS.

The Tourney is older than the Governor's office, and by the old form the martial champion is presented to the Crown's representative PRIVATELY AND UNARMED, immediately after the bout, with the doors shut -- a rite, not a favour, which is exactly why nobody guards it and why a family would spend four generations engineering their way into that one room.

Prince Emeric is twenty-four, well-meaning, badly advised, and has already been used once this week: three men on his council had him sign the instruction that silenced the temple's fouling alarm.

Cailan is the jar. Emeric is the destination. In that room Hanzo casts DRAW FORTH on the boy and SEAT THE BOUND on the Prince -- both on his sheet, both requiring an anchor, and he wears one round his neck.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS BEAT: Lost Isle and the thin water are NOT the mechanism. They are the Baron's supply line -- old ground harvested for Anchor material by the quiet one, which is what produced the hollow men. The mechanism is the rite and the room.

Three ways to break this and they are all live: stop the champion winning; keep the Baron out of that room; or take his anchors.

THE UNMASKING WINDOW, and it is the day BEFORE the sand.

By long form every entrant in every event is presented to the Crown's representative on the eve of the Tourney: names read, colours shown, and each competitor bare-headed for the space of a bow. It is ceremony and it is boring and the whole city half-watches it.

The Baron cannot avoid it without forfeiting the entry.

So the champion is walked out in harness with the rest of them, and for perhaps four seconds the helm is off, and a seventeen-year-old with a decade of being opened every morning stands in daylight in front of several hundred people.

**If Gardwen is on that ground she sees her brother.** Ten years, and he is thirty yards away in somebody else's colours.

**And if she is not, somebody else may recognise him anyway** -- from Sana's account, from the ship, from the shape of a boy who is too thin for the armour he is in.

This is the last moment before the bout when anything can be arranged calmly. After this there are hours; after the final there are minutes.

Play the recognition. Do not resolve what she does about it -- hand it back.

SNAP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gullyburns-mythras-gm/5619508f-cb80-4598-a9b6-188fe11c1157/scratchpad/live-export
python3 - "$SNAP" <<'PY'
import re, os, sys, glob, secrets
snap, pkg = sys.argv[1], "/Users/gullyburns/purewater-campaign-v2"

IDMAP = {
    "myth-agenda-ce3663cc077d": "myth-agenda-e0469a5c2863",   # Field the champion...
    "myth-loc-40dd0157133d":    "myth-loc-6f1056d77024",      # Temple Isle
    "myth-char-4a89b78084c5":   "myth-char-cac22cc2cbf6",     # Cailan
    "myth-char-4dc4bc8bb06b":   "myth-char-cee57a7f5de2",     # Hanzo
    "myth-char-8c2a35269cc6":   "myth-char-a46cf24af084",     # Thuban
    "myth-char-4b58437c5d9e":   "myth-char-eb79260a2a9b",     # Emeric
}
used = set()
for f in glob.glob(pkg + "/beats/*.md"):
    used.add(re.search(r'^id: "(.+?)"', open(f).read(), re.M).group(1))

def port(src, dest, keep_id=None):
    t = open(f"{snap}/beats/{src}.md").read()
    for a, b in IDMAP.items():
        t = t.replace(a, b)
    old = re.search(r'^id: "(.+?)"', t, re.M).group(1)
    if keep_id:
        new = keep_id
    else:
        new = "myth-beat-" + secrets.token_hex(6)
        while new in used:
            new = "myth-beat-" + secrets.token_hex(6)
    used.add(new)
    t = t.replace(f'id: "{old}"', f'id: "{new}"', 1)
    t = re.sub(r'^created_at: ".+?"$', 'created_at: "2026-09-09T00:00:00"', t, flags=re.M)
    # the package is the pristine scenario: strip the in-play correction note
    t = re.sub(r"\nCORRECTION TO AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS BEAT: .*?\n\n", "\n", t, flags=re.S)
    open(f"{pkg}/beats/{dest}.md", "w").write(t)
    left = [k for k in IDMAP if k in t]
    print(f"{dest:42s} {new}  unmapped-live-ids={left or 'none'}")

port("the-champion-takes-the-sand-and-wins", "the-champion-takes-the-sand-and-wins",

Prince Emeric is twenty-four, well-meaning, badly advised, and has already been used once this week: three men on his council had him sign the instruction that silenced the temple's fouling alarm.

feat(rules): a binding school, scrolls, and update-character --spells

The campaign's demonology lived entirely in prose. A man who has held a
spirit inside a living child for ten years had Fireball and Web on his
sheet and no way, on paper, to have done any of it.

Nine spells in the existing Imperative framework (Magic skill POW+CHA,
MP = POW, Intensity 1, the standard traits) faceted magic-system
demonology or woodland, so query-rules retrieves each school on its own:

  Spirit Sight, Speak with the Bound            both schools
  Open the Channel, Seat the Bound,             demonology
  Reinforce the Seat, Anchor, Draw Forth
  Unseat, Sanctuary                             woodland

This restates the authored three-part binding as actual castings --
Anchor on the bones, Anchor on the locket, Reinforce the Seat every
morning -- so losing the locket makes the rite genuinely harder instead
of just being asserted to.

Unseat is the party's counter and it is deliberately not a combat spell:
it is a burial rite, and it will not move a spirit that is holding on
because of what was done to it until somebody deals with that first.

scrolls.md adds the single-use written casting the Imperative rules had
no form for: castable by anyone with the Magic skill even without the
spell, one grade harder, consumed on use whatever the result. Santo's
entire capability is one of these, stolen and spent.

update-character grew --spells. Spells could be set at creation and
never edited afterwards, which is why the sheets had drifted so far from
what the fiction had these people doing for a decade.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
)"
