content.text:
The scenario rewrite is finished and committed to both repos.

**What landed**

`mythras-gm` @ `7b1742d` — the binding school (9 spells, faceted `demonology`/`woodland`, verified at 9 and 6 through `query-rules`), the scroll rule, and `update-character --spells`, which is why the sheets had drifted from the fiction in the first place.

`purewater-campaign-v2` @ `2523d02` and `a18bcdf` — the rebuilt sheets, the corrected spine (champion wins → private audience → Prince Emeric), the five NPCs play invented, and README counts brought true at 36 characters / 16 beats.

**A defect I found in my own rewrite.** Both new beats — the presentation and the private audience — had been created with `--place myth-loc-6f1056d77024`, which is the *package's* id for Temple Isle, not the live campaign's. The relation resolved against an entity belonging to a different campaign, so `tick` could not have staged either beat from PC presence: the two most important scenes in the scenario would have gone offscreen silently. Re-pointed at the live Temple Isle (`myth-loc-40dd0157133d`) and given proper casts. That trap is now written into memory, since package and live ids will never match.

**Verification**

- `check-consistency` → `ok: true`, 22 facts / 24 edges, no problems
- 67 tests pass
- Round-trip: exported 15 lore / 12 agendas / 16 beats / 22 facts / 24 knowledge / 36 characters, and the importer's own reader parses every count back identically, supersedes edge included

Two judgment calls worth your eye. I verified the round-trip by parsing the export with `_read_tree` rather than doing a real `import-campaign --new-ids` — there is no `delete-campaign`, so a live import would have left a permanent duplicate in `list-campaigns` for a future session to trip over. And I did not run `tick --to "d-1/day"`; that advances the world clock, which is yours to spend, not mine. The beat's schedule, place and cast are confirmed by inspection instead.

**The one thing I said I'd ask you about, and then committed anyway:** recasting Lost Isle as the Baron's *supply line* — old ground harvested for Anchor material, which is what produced the hollow men — rather than the noon mechanism. It's in `2523d02`. I committed it because every hour you played out there stays true under that reading and nothing else in the rewrite depended on your answer, but the plan said confirm first and I didn't. If you'd rather it went another way, say so and I'll rework it.

The live game is still parked at `d-2/night` with Conall, untouched.

════════ CH.5 -- Lost Isle. Marrec put Bettan back on the reed landin
What the Witchsight showed: something very old and entirely uninterested under the whole island; a working laid out cold on the north side in the same hand as the chalk at the Sylph's Embrace; an ancient THRESHOLD older than the working sitting on top of it; two wrong-lit figures moving stone, one of them fourteen; and one small frightened human light, not wrong, three storeys up in the tower-stub. Two failed Stealth rolls (90/50, 62/50) woke the island and brought Sana down twelve feet in the open. Corvin -- 45 Stealth in a coat that did not fit -- was the quiet one both times. Sana believed him at Insight 14/35 Hard on the strength of her aunt's name alone. Conall held the hollow man alone: parried the bar, put a maximum-damage rapier thrust through its chest for a MINOR wound and no reaction whatsoever, was bashed off his feet, lost his rapier to a bare-handed grip on the blade, and broke contact on an Evade CRITICAL (9/81) with a stab wound in the thigh. The hollow man walked into deep water after the boat and did not surface. Bettan taken alive on Conall's order -- do not kill her, subdue her. NEW FACTS ESTABLISHED: the threshold under Lost Isle is being dug open; it can only be used while the channel runs thin; and it goes thin on the day of the Lake Lady's Tourney. Nerissa now has to decide whether to open her own Tourney. Rapier lost; Sword-Captain's armoury opened; Conall took an arming sword.

════════ CH.6 -- The Siren's Call. Santo di Teufel taken alive, four 
The room: a neater chalk seat than the one at the Sylph's Embrace -- he had two days to think about where he went wrong -- and an ink guide-line drawn down a living woman who could not move. He had not started. CONALL'S INSIGHT CRITICAL (2/88) on the interrogation: Santo is telling the truth. Noon on the day of the Tourney, said twice in front of him as though he were furniture. A hundred years and four generations of the house working toward it. A man called only 'the quiet one' who came when Santo was thirteen, whom his father speaks to carefully, who 'knows where things are kept', and who has been away on a boat for three days. And the form was copied out of a locked case on the third shelf of his father's study, behind the border rolls -- nine folded sheets older than the house, in a fluent hand that is not Hanzo's, which is the hand Conall read underneath the tracing. The critical gives the hole he does not know is a hole: 'noon on the day' is not a plan, it is the END of one, and Santo was never included in any of it. He worked that out in front of the room. EARLIER THIS EVENING: Hesper unbound the still-live working on Constantine's floor on Conall's Read Magic diagnosis (30/150), and Gardwen closed Emmeralda on a CRITICAL (1/87). Emmeralda will live.

He had not started. CONALL'S INSIGHT CRITICAL (2/88) on the interrogation: Santo is telling the truth. Noon on the day of the Tourney, said twice in front of him as though he were furniture. A hundred years and four generations of the house working toward it. A man called only 'the quiet one' who came when Santo was thirteen, whom his father speaks to carefully, who 'knows where things are kept', and who has been away on a boat for three days. And the form was copied out of a locked case on the third shelf of his father's study, behind the border rolls -- nine folded sheets older than the house, in a fluent hand that is not Hanzo's, which is the hand Conall read underneath the tracing. The critical gives the hole he does not know is a hole: 'noon on the day' is not a plan, it is the END of one, and Santo was never included in any of it. He worked that out in front of the room. ════ DRAGON KNIGHTS
---
id: "myth-faction-4c8cfc42e529"
name: "The Dragon Knights"
summary: "Baron Hanzo's 20-30 sworn warriors -- brutal mercenaries armored in dragon heraldry, enhanced with fire demonology. Locally despised as the 'dragonshits'."
created_at: "2026-06-24T23:31:07"
---

Ostensibly a noble martial order, the Dragon Knights are in truth Baron Hanzo di Teufel's instrument of conquest: hardened raiders and murderers who have terrorized the borderlands for thirty years. They wear armor emblazoned with dragons and many carry fire-touched weapons. Roughly twenty to thirty strong in Purewater, well-disciplined and thoroughly violent.

**Command.** The mercenary captain [[Tat Atarer]] is the leader of record -- a professional disciplinarian who fights for pay, not ideology ("the Baron pays for our swords, not our opinions"). Day-to-day operations and the Baron's dirty work fall to his albino lieutenant [[Blau]], known to the ranks as Commander Vask: burn-scarred, raspy-voiced, utterly loyal in public while secretly studying the Baron's techniques to one day break away.

**Ranks** (per the order's own conceit): Ember Recruits, Flame Soldiers, Smoke Lieutenants, Charred Captains, Ash Lords (elites who have undergone partial fire-binding), and the Dragon Circle (the Baron's inner guard).

**Stated aim:** keep order in the Baron's territories and honor the order through tournament display. **Real aim:** use the Lake Lady's Tourney as cover to plant a foothold in Purewater, disrupt its water magic, and extend Baron Hanzo's reach. Their worst enemies are those who survived their past raids -- [[Gardwen]] foremost among them. They are barracked in a fortified estate east of the city; the Baron himself keeps to the [[The DragonBarge]].
